### GOV-11.4 — Authorize Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS)

Does the organization compel data and/or process owners to obtain authorization for the production use of each Technology Asset, Application and/or Service (TAAS) under their control?

### GOV-11.5 — Monitor Controls

Does the organization compel data and/or process owners to monitor Technology Assets, Applications, Services and/or Data (TAASD) under their control on an ongoing basis for applicable threats and risks, as well as to ensure security, compliance and resilience controls are operating as intended?

### GOV-12 — Measures of Performance

Does the organization develop, report and monitor Security, Compliance & Resilience Program (SCRP) measures of performance?

### GOV-12.1 — Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)

Does the organization develop, report and monitor Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) to assist organizational management in performance monitoring and trend analysis of the Security, Compliance & Resilience Program (SCRP)?

### GOV-12.2 — Key Risk Indicators (KRIs)

Does the organization develop, report and monitor Key Risk Indicators (KRIs) to assist senior management in performance monitoring and trend analysis of the Security, Compliance & Resilience Program (SCRP)?

### GOV-13 — Forced Technology Transfer (FTT)

Does the organization avoid and/or constrain the forced exfiltration of sensitive and/or regulated information (e.g., Intellectual Property (IP)) to the host government for purposes of market access or market management practices?

### GOV-14 — State-Sponsored Espionage

Does the organization constrain the host government's ability to leverage its Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) for economic or political espionage and/or cyberwarfare activities?

### GOV-15 — Contacts With Authorities

Does the organization identify and document appropriate contacts with relevant law enforcement and regulatory bodies?

### GOV-16 — Contacts With Groups & Associations

Does the organization establish contact with selected groups and associations within the security, compliance and resilience communities to:
(1) Facilitate ongoing cybersecurity and data protection education and training for organizational personnel;
(2) Maintain currency with recommended cybersecurity and data protection practices, techniques and technologies; and
(3) Share current cybersecurity and/or data protection-related information including threats, vulnerabilities and incidents?

### GOV-17 — Quality Management System (QMS)

Does the organization govern a Quality Management System (QMS) to ensure security, compliance and resilience processes conform with applicable statutory, regulatory and/or contractual obligations?

### GOV-18 — Assurance

Does the organization define the basis for confidence that implemented capabilities conform to applicable security, compliance and resilience requirements?

### GOV-19 — Mergers, Acquisitions & Divestitures (MA&D)

Does the organization define standardized practices to conduct Mergers, Acquisitions and Divestiture (MA&D) activities?

### GOV-19.1 — Virtual Data Room (VDR)

Does the organization provision a Virtual Data Room (VDR), or similar technology, to securely share documentation among stakeholders to conduct Mergers, Acquisitions and Divestiture (MA&D) activities?

### AAT-01 — Artificial Intelligence & Autonomous Technologies Policy

Does the organization establish a formal, documented Artificial Intelligence and Autonomous Technologies (AAT) policy that:
 (1) Conveys executive management's intent;
 (2) Provides organizational direction and expected behaviors;
 (3) Is reviewed at least annually; and
 (4) Is updated, as necessary, to adapt to evolving risks, threats and other changes that affect the organization?

### AAT-02 — Artificial Intelligence (AI) & Autonomous Technologies Governance

Does the organization ensure policies, processes, procedures and practices related to the mapping, measuring and managing of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Autonomous Technologies (AAT)-related risks are in place, transparent and implemented effectively?

### AAT-03 — AI & Autonomous Technologies Mission and Goals Definition

Does the organization define and document its mission and defined goals for Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Autonomous Technologies (AAT)?

### AAT-03.1 — AI & Autonomous Technologies Value Sustainment

Does the organization sustain the value of deployed Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Autonomous Technologies (AAT)?

### AAT-04 — AI & Autonomous Technologies Context Definition

Does the organization establish and document the context surrounding Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Autonomous Technologies (AAT), including:
 (1) Intended purposes;
 (2) Potentially beneficial uses;
 (3) Context-specific laws and regulations;
 (4) Norms and expectations; and
 (5) Prospective settings in which the system(s) will be deployed?

### AAT-04.1 — AI & Autonomous Technologies-Related Legal Requirements Identification

Does the organization identify, understand, document and manage applicable statutory and regulatory requirements for Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Autonomous Technologies (AAT)?

### AAT-05 — Assigned Responsibilities for AI & Autonomous Technologies

Does the organization define and differentiate roles and responsibilities for:
(1) Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Autonomous Technologies (AAT) configurations; and
(2) Oversight of AAT systems?

### AAT-06 — Trustworthy AI & Autonomous Technologies

Does the organization ensure Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Autonomous Technologies (AAT) are designed to be reliable, safe, fair, secure, resilient, transparent, explainable and data privacy-enhanced to minimize emergent properties or unintended consequences?

### AAT-06.1 — AI & Autonomous Technologies Continuous Improvements

Does the organization continuously improve Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Autonomous Technologies (AAT) capabilities to maximize benefits and minimize negative impacts associated with AAT?

### AAT-07 — Situational Awareness of AI & Autonomous Technologies In Use

Does the organization develop and maintain an inventory of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Autonomous Technologies (AAT) (internal and third-party)?

### AAT-07.1 — AI Model & Agent Inventory & Lifecycle Management

Does the organization track the lifecycle of all AI models and AI agents, including ownership, intended purpose and status across:
(1) Development;
(2) Deployment;
(3) Updates; and
(4) Decommissioning?

### AAT-07.2 — Artificial Intelligence and Autonomous Technologies (AAT) & AI Agent Categorization

Does the organization assign defined classes to Artificial Intelligence and Autonomous Technologies (AAT) and AI agents based on their characteristics (e.g., intended use, autonomy, access, potential impact and risk) to determine applicable:
(1) Approval requirements;
(2) Security, compliance and/or resilience controls;
(3) Testing rigor;
(4) Monitoring requirements;
(5) Supporting documentation; and
(6) Oversight requirements?

### AAT-08 — AI & Autonomous Technologies Internal Controls

Does the organization identify and document internal security, compliance and resilience for Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Autonomous Technologies (AAT)?

### AAT-08.1 — Adequate Protections For AI & Autonomous Technologies

Does the organization ensure Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Autonomous Technologies (AAT) include reasonable security, compliance and resilience protections that are commensurate with assessed risks and threats?

### AAT-09 — AI & Autonomous Technologies Impact Assessment

Does the organization assess the impact(s) of proposed Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Autonomous Technologies (AAT) on individuals, groups, communities, organizations and society (e.g., Fundamental Rights Impact Assessment (FRIA))?

### AAT-10 — AI & Autonomous Technologies Risk Profiling

Does the organization document the risks and potential impacts of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Autonomous Technologies (AAT) that are:
(1) Designed;
(2) Developed;
(3) Deployed;
(4) Evaluated; and/or
(5) Used?

### AAT-10.1 — AI & Autonomous Technologies Risk Mapping

Does the organization identify Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Autonomous Technologies (AAT) in use and map those components to potential legal risks, including statutory and regulatory compliance requirements?

### AAT-11 — AI & Autonomous Technologies Risk Management Decisions

Does the organization leverage decision makers from a diversity of demographics, disciplines, experience, expertise and backgrounds for mapping, measuring and managing Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Autonomous Technologies (AAT)-related risks?

### AAT-11.1 — AI & Autonomous Technologies Likelihood & Impact Risk Analysis

Does the organization define the potential likelihood and impact of each identified risk based on expected use and past uses of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Autonomous Technologies (AAT) in similar contexts?

### AAT-11.2 — AI & Autonomous Technologies High Risk Designations

Does the organization designate Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Autonomous Technologies (AAT) "High Risk" if one (1), or more, of the following criteria are met:
(1) AAT is used as a safety component of a product or service;
(2) AAT poses a significant risk of harm to an individual's health, safety or fundamental rights; and/or
(3) AAT materially influences the outcome of an individual's decision making?

### AAT-12 — AI Threat Modeling & Risk Assessment

Does the organization conduct Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Autonomous Technologies (AAT)-specific threat modeling and risk assessments to address the following criteria across the lifecycle of the AAT:
(1) Attack surfaces;
(2) Adversarial threats; and
(3) Abuse / misuse scenarios?

### AAT-12.1 — Novel Risk Assessment Methods & Technologies

Does the organization utilize novel methods and technologies for the measurement of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Autonomous Technologies (AAT)-related risks to evaluate, if applicable:
(1) Content provenance;
(2) Oﬀensive cyber capabilities;
(3) Chemical, Biological, Radiological or Nuclear (CBRN) weapons; and/or
(4) Other dangerous materials or agents?

### AAT-13 — AI & Autonomous Technologies Risk Response

Does the organization prioritize, respond to and remediate Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Autonomous Technologies (AAT)-related risks based on assessments and other analytical output?

### AAT-13.1 — AI & Autonomous Technologies Risk Tracking Approaches

Does the organization track Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Autonomous Technologies (AAT)-related risks are difficult to assess using currently available measurement techniques or where metrics are not yet available?

### AAT-13.2 — Fine Tuning Risk Mitigation

Does the organization ensure actions to fine-tune Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Autonomous Technologies (AAT) do not compromise existing security, compliance and resilience controls?

### AAT-13.3 — Responsibility To Supersede, Deactivate and/or Disengage AI & Autonomous Technologies

Does the organization define the criteria and responsible party(ies) for superseding, disengaging or deactivating Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Autonomous Technologies (AAT) that demonstrate performance or outcomes inconsistent with intended use?

### AAT-14 — AI & Autonomous Technologies Business Case

Does the organization benchmark capabilities, targeted usage, goals and expected benefits and costs of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Autonomous Technologies (AAT)?

### AAT-14.1 — AI & Autonomous Technologies Potential Benefits Analysis

Does the organization assess the potential benefits of proposed Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Autonomous Technologies (AAT)?

### AAT-14.2 — AI & Autonomous Technologies Potential Costs Analysis

Does the organization assess potential costs, including non-monetary costs, resulting from expected or realized Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Autonomous Technologies (AAT)-related errors or system functionality and trustworthiness?

### AAT-14.3 — AI & Autonomous Technologies Targeted Application Scope

Does the organization specify and document the targeted application scope of the proposed use and operation of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Autonomous Technologies (AAT)?

### AAT-14.4 — AI & Autonomous Technologies Cost / Benefit Mapping

Does the organization map risks and benefits for all components of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Autonomous Technologies (AAT), including third-party software and data?

### AAT-15 — Model & AI Agent Documentation

Does the organization create, maintain and provide access to documentation artifacts for AI models and agents, including:
(1) Data lineage;
(2) Intended use; and
(3) Limitations?

### AAT-16 — AI & Autonomous Technologies Output Marking

Does the organization mark output from Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Autonomous Technologies (AAT) in a machine-readable format so it is detectable as artificially generated or manipulated?

### AAT-17 — Release Owner Gate (ROG) For AI-Augmented Content

Does the organization implement a Release Owner Gate (ROG), or similar function, that prohibits the external release of AI-augmented content without formal Subject Matter Expert (SME) review and Line of Business (LOB) approval that validates:
(1) Material facts;
(2) Citations; and
(3) Other relevant content that could discredit the organization?

### AAT-17.1 — AI & Autonomous Technologies Output Filtering

Does the organization prevent Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Autonomous Technologies (AAT) from generating content that is:
(1) Inappropriate;
(2) Harmful;
(3) False;
(4) Illegal; and/or
(5) Violent?

### AAT-17.2 — Human Moderation of AI & Autonomous Technologies-Generated Content

Does the organization assign personnel to review Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Autonomous Technologies (AAT)-generated content for alignment with culturally accepted norms?

### AAT-18 — AI & Autonomous Technologies Intellectual Property Infringement Protections

Does the organization prevent third-party Intellectual Property (IP) rights infringement by Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Autonomous Technologies (AAT)?

### AAT-18.1 — Data Source Identification

Does the organization identify and document data sources utilized in the training and/or operation of Artificial Intelligence and Autonomous Technologies (AAT)?

### AAT-18.2 — Data Source Integrity

Does the organization protect the integrity of source data to prevent accidental contamination or malicious corruption (e.g., data poisoning) that could compromise the performance of Artificial Intelligence and Autonomous Technologies (AAT)?

### AAT-18.3 — Data Source Lineage & Origin Disclosure

Does the organization ensure Artificial Intelligence and Autonomous Technologies (AAT) publicly disclose information with sufficient detail to assess:
(1) Content lineage; and
(2) The origin of data used by the AAT?

### AAT-18.4 — Digital Content Modification Logging

Does the organization ensure Artificial Intelligence and Autonomous Technologies (AAT):
(1) Enable auditing of content modifications; and
(2) Generate event logs for content-related changes?

### AAT-18.5 — Training Data Source & Integrity

Does the organization validate the reliability, accuracy and integrity of training data used by Artificial Intelligence and Autonomous Technologies (AAT)?

### AAT-18.6 — Prohibit Training

Does the organization prohibit Artificial Intelligence and Autonomous Technologies (AAT) from training, fine-tuning and/or improving capabilities using organizational data without prior, explicit consent from applicable data owner(s)?

### AAT-19 — AI & Autonomous Technologies Harm Prevention

Does the organization proactively prevent harm by regularly identifying and tracking existing, unanticipated and emergent Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Autonomous Technologies (AAT)-related risks?

### AAT-19.1 — AI & Autonomous Technologies Human Subject Protections

Does the organization protect human subjects from harm?

### AAT-19.2 — AI & Autonomous Technologies Environmental Impact & Sustainability

Does the organization assess and document the environmental impacts and sustainability of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Autonomous Technologies (AAT)?

### AAT-19.3 — Previously Unknown AI & Autonomous Technologies Threats & Risks

Does the organization respond to and recover from a previously unknown Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Autonomous Technologies (AAT)-related risk when it is identified?

### AAT-20 — AI & Autonomous Technologies Conformity

Does the organization ensure deployed Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Autonomous Technologies (AAT) conform to applicable statutory and regulatory requirements, based on:
(1) Defined use cases;
(2) Geographic markets; and
(3) Use of Intellectual Property (IP)?

### AAT-20.1 — Manipulative or Deceptive Techniques

Does the organization prohibit the sale, deployment and/or use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Autonomous Technologies (AAT) that utilize manipulative or deceptive techniques (including biased data) to impair an individual's ability to make a reasonably informed decision?

### AAT-20.2 — Materially Distorting Behaviors

Does the organization prohibit the sale, deployment and/or use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Autonomous Technologies (AAT) that exploit a human subject to materially affect a targeted behavior due to their:
(1) Age;
(2) Disability; or
(3) Specific social or economic situation?

### AAT-20.3 — Social Scoring

Does the organization prohibit the sale, deployment and/or use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Autonomous Technologies (AAT) that:
(1) Evaluate human subjects over a certain period of time based on their social behavior or known, inferred or predicted personal or personality characteristics; and
(2) Assign a "social score" branding or equivalent classification?

### AAT-20.4 — Detrimental or Unfavorable Treatment

Does the organization prohibit the sale, deployment and/or use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Autonomous Technologies (AAT) that lead to the detrimental or unfavorable treatment of certain data subjects, or groups of data subjects, in social contexts that is:
(1) Are unrelated to the contexts in which the data was originally generated or collected; and/or
(2) Is unjustified or disproportionate to their social behavior or its gravity?

### AAT-20.5 — Risk and Criminal Profiling

Does the organization prohibit the sale, deployment and/or use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Autonomous Technologies (AAT) that:
(1) Assess the risk of an individual committing a criminal offence; and
(2) Predicts risk based solely on the profiling of personality traits and characteristics?

### AAT-20.6 — Populating Facial Recognition Databases

Does the organization prohibit the sale, deployment and/or use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Autonomous Technologies (AAT) that create, or expand, facial recognition databases through scraping facial images from:
(1) The Internet; or
(2) Closed-Circuit Television (CCTV) footage?

### AAT-20.7 — Emotion Inference

Does the organization prohibit the sale, deployment and/or use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Autonomous Technologies (AAT) that infer human emotions of an individual based on observed characteristics?

### AAT-20.8 — Biometric Categorization

Does the organization prohibit the sale, deployment and/or use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Autonomous Technologies (AAT) that categorize an individual based on their biometric data to deduce, or infer, the individual's:
(1) Race;
(2) Political opinions;
(3) Trade union membership;
(4) Religious or philosophical beliefs;
(5) Sex life or sexual orientation; and/or
(6) Age?

### AAT-21 — AI & Autonomous Technologies Requirements Definitions

Does the organization take socio-technical implications into account to address risks associated with Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Autonomous Technologies (AAT)?

### AAT-22 — AI & Autonomous Technologies Fairness & Bias

Does the organization prevent Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Autonomous Technologies (AAT) from unfairly identifying, profiling and/or statistically singling out a segmented population defined by race, religion, gender identity, national origin, religion, disability or any other politically-charged identifier?

### AAT-23 — AI & Autonomous Technologies Knowledge Limits

Does the organization identify and document knowledge limits of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Autonomous Technologies (AAT) to provide sufficient information to assist relevant stakeholder decision making?

### AAT-24 — AI & Autonomous Technologies Development Practices

Does the organization ensure Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Autonomous Technologies (AAT) are designed and developed to:
(1) Achieve an appropriate level of accuracy, robustness and cybersecurity;
(2) Perform consistently in those respects throughout the AAT system's lifecycle; and
(3) Be effectively overseen by competent individuals?

### AAT-24.1 — AI & Autonomous Technologies Transparency

Does the organization ensure Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Autonomous Technologies (AAT) are designed and developed so its operation is sufficiently transparent such that output can be easily interpreted by personnel implementing the AAT?

### AAT-24.2 — AI & Autonomous Technologies Implementation Documentation

Does the organization ensure Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Autonomous Technologies (AAT) include clear and concise documentation that is relevant, accessible and comprehensible to personnel implementing and maintaining the AAT that, at a minimum, provides:
(1) Contact details of the provider;
(2) Characteristics, capabilities and limitations of performance of the AAT;
(3) Errata from the AAT's initial conformity assessment;
(4) Details necessary to interpret the outputs of the AAT;
(5) Human oversight measures necessary to facilitate the interpretation of the outputs of the AAT;
(6) Computational and hardware resources needed to operate the AAT;
(7) Projected useable lifetime of the AAT; and
(8) A description of the mechanisms included within the AAT system to properly collect, store and interpret event logs?

### AAT-24.3 — AI & Autonomous Technologies Human Domain Knowledge Reliance

Does the organization document the extent to which human domain knowledge is employed to improve Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Autonomous Technologies (AAT) performance including:
(1) Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF);
(2) Fine-tuning;
(3) Retrieval- augmented generation;
(4) Content moderation; and
(5) Business rules?

### AAT-25 — AI & Autonomous Technologies Implementation Tasks Definition

Does the organization define the tasks that Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Autonomous Technologies (AAT) will support (e.g., classifiers, generative models and recommenders)?

### AAT-26 — Real World Testing of AI & Autonomous Technologies

Does the organization obtain consent from the subjects of testing Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Autonomous Technologies (AAT):
(1) Prior to their participation in such testing; and
(2) After they have been provided with clear and concise information regarding the testing?

### AAT-27 — AI & Autonomous Technologies Testing Techniques

Does the organization develop and implement fact-checking techniques to verify the accuracy and veracity of information generated by Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Autonomous Technologies (AAT)?

### AAT-27.1 — Generative Artificial Intelligence (GAI) Identification

Does the organization develop and implement testing techniques to identify Generative Artificial Intelligence (GAI) produced content (e.g., synthetic media)?

### AAT-27.2 — AI & Autonomous Technologies Capabilities Testing

Does the organization delineate human proﬁciency tests from tests of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Autonomous Technologies (AAT) capabilities?

### AAT-27.3 — Real-World Testing

Does the organization include relevant end-users, practitioners and operators in Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Autonomous Technologies (AAT) prototyping and testing activities to cover:
(1) Applicable use case scenarios;
(2) Crisis situations; and/or
(3) Ethically sensitive contexts?

### AAT-27.4 — Documenting Testing Guidance

Does the organization document the instructions given to:
(1) Data annotators; and/or
(2) Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Autonomous Technologies (AAT) red-teamers?

### AAT-28 — Artificial Intelligence Test, Evaluation, Validation & Verification (AI TEVV)

Does the organization implement Artificial Intelligence Test, Evaluation, Validation & Verification (AI TEVV) practices to enable Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Autonomous Technologies (AAT)-related security, resilience and compliance-related conformity testing throughout the lifecycle of the AAT?

### AAT-28.1 — AI TEVV Trustworthiness Assessment

Does the organization evaluate Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Autonomous Technologies (AAT) for trustworthy behavior and operation including security, anonymization and disaggregation of captured and stored data for approved purposes?

### AAT-28.2 — AI TEVV Tools

Does the organization document test sets, metrics and details about the tools used during Artificial Intelligence Test, Evaluation, Validation & Verification (AI TEVV) practices?

### AAT-28.3 — AI TEVV Trustworthiness Demonstration

Does the organization demonstrate the Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Autonomous Technologies (AAT) to be deployed are:
(1) Valid;
(2) Reliable; and
(3) Operate as intended, based on approved designs?

### AAT-28.4 — AI TEVV Safety Demonstration

Does the organization demonstrate the Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Autonomous Technologies (AAT) to be deployed are safe, residual risk does not exceed its risk tolerance and can fail safely, particularly if made to operate beyond its knowledge limits?

### AAT-28.5 — AI TEVV Security & Resiliency Assessment

Does the organization evaluate the security and resilience of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Autonomous Technologies (AAT) to be deployed?

### AAT-28.6 — AI TEVV Transparency & Accountability Assessment

Does the organization examine risks associated with transparency and accountability of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Autonomous Technologies (AAT) to be deployed?

### AAT-28.7 — AI TEVV Privacy Assessment

Does the organization examine the data privacy risk of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Autonomous Technologies (AAT) to be deployed?

### AAT-28.8 — AI TEVV Fairness & Bias Assessment

Does the organization examine fairness and bias of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Autonomous Technologies (AAT) to be deployed?

### AAT-28.9 — AI & Autonomous Technologies Model Validation

Does the organization validate the Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Autonomous Technologies (AAT) model?

### AAT-28.10 — AI TEVV Comparable Deployment Settings

Does the organization evaluate Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Autonomous Technologies (AAT)-related performance or the assurance criteria demonstrated for conditions similar to deployment settings?

### AAT-28.11 — AI TEVV Empirically Validated Methods

Does the organization evaluate claims of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Autonomous Technologies (AAT) model capabilities using empirically validated methods?

### AAT-28.12 — AI TEVV Benchmarking Content Provenance

Does the organization benchmark the verifiable lineage and origin of content used by Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Autonomous Technologies (AAT) according to industry-recognized standards?

### AAT-28.13 — AI TEVV Model Collapse Mitigations

Does the organization mitigate concerns of model collapse by:
(1) Assessing the proportion of synthetic to non-synthetic training data; and
(2) Verifying training data is not overly homogenous or Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Autonomous Technologies (AAT) system-produced?

### AAT-28.14 — AI TEVV Third-Party Risk Management

Does the organization assess, approve and continuously monitor third-party Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Autonomous Technologies (AAT):
(1) Components;
(2) Application Programming Interfaces (APIs); and/or
(3) Services used by AI agents for security, privacy and compliance?

### AAT-29 — AI TEVV Results Evaluation

Does the organization evaluate the results of Artificial Intelligence Test, Evaluation, Validation & Verification (AI TEVV) to determine the viability of the proposed Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Autonomous Technologies (AAT)?

### AAT-29.1 — AI TEVV Effectiveness

Does the organization evaluate the effectiveness of the processes utilized to perform Artificial Intelligence Test, Evaluation, Validation & Verification (AI TEVV)?

### AAT-30 — AI TEVV Reporting

Does the organization report the status and results of Artificial Intelligence Test, Evaluation, Validation & Verification (AI TEVV) to relevant stakeholders, including governing bodies, as required?

### AAT-30.1 — AI & Autonomous Technologies Residual Risks

Does the organization identify and document negative, residual risks (defined as the sum of all unmitigated risks) to both downstream acquirers and end users of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Autonomous Technologies (AAT)?

### AAT-30.2 — AI & Autonomous Technologies Viability Decisions

Does the organization define the criteria as to whether Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Autonomous Technologies (AAT) achieved intended purposes and stated objectives to determine whether its development or deployment should proceed?

### AAT-31 — AI TEVV Post-Deployment Monitoring

Does the organization proactively and continuously monitor deployed Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Autonomous Technologies (AAT)?

### AAT-32 — Updating AI & Autonomous Technologies

Does the organization integrate continual improvements for deployed Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Autonomous Technologies (AAT)?

### AAT-33 — Robust Stakeholder Engagement for AI & Autonomous Technologies

Does the organization compel ongoing engagement with relevant Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Autonomous Technologies (AAT) stakeholders to encourage feedback about positive, negative and unanticipated impacts?

### AAT-33.1 — AI & Autonomous Technologies Stakeholder Feedback Integration

Does the organization regularly collect, consider, prioritize and integrate risk-related feedback from those external to the team that developed or deployed Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Autonomous Technologies (AAT)?

### AAT-33.2 — AI & Autonomous Technologies Ongoing Assessments

Does the organization conduct regular assessments of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Autonomous Technologies (AAT) with independent assessors and stakeholders not involved in the development of the AAT?

### AAT-33.3 — AI & Autonomous Technologies End User Feedback

Does the organization collect and integrate feedback from end users and impacted communities into Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Autonomous Technologies (AAT)-related system evaluation metrics?

### AAT-33.4 — AI & Autonomous Technologies Incident & Error Reporting

Does the organization communicate Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Autonomous Technologies (AAT)-related incidents and/or errors to relevant stakeholders, including affected communities?

### AAT-34 — AI & Autonomous Technologies Stakeholder Diversity

Does the organization ensure Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Autonomous Technologies (AAT) stakeholder competencies, skills and capacities incorporate demographic diversity, broad domain and user experience expertise?

### AAT-34.1 — AI & Autonomous Technologies Stakeholder Competencies

Does the organization ensure Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Autonomous Technologies (AAT)-related operator and practitioner proficiency requirements for Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Autonomous Technologies (AAT) are defined, assessed and documented?

### AAT-35 — AI & Autonomous Technologies Deployment

Does the organization ensure the deployment of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Autonomous Technologies (AAT) includes appropriate technical and organizational measures so that AAT are used in accordance with the AAT developer-provided instructions for use?

### AAT-35.1 — AI & Autonomous Technologies Human Oversight

Does the organization assign human oversight of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Autonomous Technologies (AAT) to prevent or minimize the risks to:
(1) Health;
(2) Safety; and/or
(3) Fundamental rights?

### AAT-35.2 — AI & Autonomous Technologies Oversight Measures

Does the organization ensure Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Autonomous Technologies (AAT) oversight measures are commensurate with the:
(1) Assessed risk(s);
(2) Level of autonomy; and
(3) Context of use?

### AAT-35.3 — AI & Autonomous Technologies Separate Verification

Does the organization ensure no action or decision is taken by the deployer of an Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Autonomous Technologies (AAT) based solely based on AAT-generated evidence, unless that evidence has been separately verified and confirmed by at least two (2) individuals with the necessary competence, training and authority?

### AAT-35.4 — AI & Autonomous Technologies Oversight Functions Competency

Does the organization ensure the deployment of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Autonomous Technologies (AAT) assigns human oversight to individuals who have the necessary:
(1) Competence;
(2) Training;
(3) Authority; and
(4) Resources?

### AAT-35.5 — AI & Autonomous Technologies Data Relevance

Does the organization ensure the input to Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Autonomous Technologies (AAT) is relevant to the intended purpose of the AAT?

### AAT-35.6 — AI & Autonomous Technologies Irregularity Reporting

Does the organization ensure serious incidents and/or irregularities associated with the deployment of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Autonomous Technologies (AAT) are reported without delay to the:
(1) AAT provider;
(2) AAT importer or distributor, if applicable; and/or
(3) Local law authorities and/or governmental agency, as required?

### AAT-35.7 — AI & Autonomous Technologies Use Notification To Employees

Does the organization ensure employees, including workers' representatives, are informed about Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Autonomous Technologies (AAT) deployments, prior to the use of the AAT in a production environment?

### AAT-35.8 — AI & Autonomous Technologies Use Notification To Users

Does the organization ensure Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Autonomous Technologies (AAT) that make decisions, or assist in making decisions, inform the people in a clear manner that they are:
(1) Utilizing an AAT solution; and
(2) Expected to validate the output for relevance and accuracy?

### AAT-36 — AI & Autonomous Technologies Production Monitoring

Does the organization monitor the functionality and behavior of the deployed Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Autonomous Technologies (AAT)?

### AAT-36.1 — AI & Autonomous Technologies Measurement Approaches

Does the organization measure Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Autonomous Technologies (AAT)-related risks to deployment context(s) through review and consultation with industry experts, domain specialists and end users?

### AAT-36.2 — Measuring AI & Autonomous Technologies Effectiveness

Does the organization regularly assess the effectiveness of existing security, compliance and resilience controls, including reports of errors and potential impacts on affected communities?

### AAT-36.3 — Unmeasurable AI & Autonomous Technologies Risks

Does the organization identify and document unmeasurable risks or trustworthiness characteristics related to Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Autonomous Technologies (AAT)?

### AAT-36.4 — Efficacy of AI & Autonomous Technologies Measurement

Does the organization gather and assess feedback about the efficacy of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Autonomous Technologies (AAT)-related measurements?

### AAT-36.5 — AI & Autonomous Technologies Domain Expert Reviews

Does the organization utilize input from domain experts and relevant stakeholders to validate whether the Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Autonomous Technologies (AAT) perform consistently, as intended?

### AAT-36.6 — AI & Autonomous Technologies Performance Changes

Does the organization evaluate performance improvements or declines with domain experts and relevant stakeholders to define context-relevant risks and trustworthiness issues?

### AAT-36.7 — Pre-Trained AI & Autonomous Technologies Models

Does the organization validate the information source(s) and quality of pre-trained models used in Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Autonomous Technologies (AAT) training, maintenance and improvement-related activities?

### AAT-36.8 — AI & Autonomous Technologies Event Logging

Does the organization ensure Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Autonomous Technologies (AAT) system event logging capabilities at a minimum provide:
(1) Start date, start time, end date and end time for each use;
(2) Database(s) against which input data has been checked by the system;
(3) Input data for which the search has led to a match; and
(4) Identification of individual(s) involved in the verification of the results?

### AAT-36.9 — Serious Incident Reporting For AI & Autonomous Technologies

Does the organization report any serious incident involving operational Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Autonomous Technologies (AAT) to relevant authorities as to when and where the serious incident occurred, in accordance with mandated reporting timelines?

### AAT-36.10 — Serious Incident Root Cause Analysis (RCA) For AI & Autonomous Technologies

Does the organization perform an investigation when there is a serious incident involving operational Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Autonomous Technologies (AAT) that documents a:
(1) Root Cause Analysis (RCA);
(2) Risk assessment of the incident; and
(3) Description of corrective actions taken, including measures implemented to prevent a recurrence of the incident?

### AAT-36.11 — Anomaly Detection & Human Oversight

Does the organization analyze anomalous Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Autonomous Technologies (AAT) behavior and provide escalation paths for human oversight, including:
(1) Real-time review; and
(2) Intervention?

### AAT-36.12 — Human-in-the-Loop & Escalation

Does the organization require human review and clear escalation paths for approval for high-risk or ambiguous Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Autonomous Technologies (AAT) actions?

### AAT-36.13 — Emergent Behavior & Collusion Protections

Does the organization detect and contain emergent or collusive behaviors among multiple Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Autonomous Technologies (AAT), including:
(1) Automated or human-triggered containment; and
(2) Formal investigation to determine the root cause of agentic cascades or collusion?

### AAT-36.14 — Multi-Agent Trust & Communication Validation

Does the organization validate AI agent to AI agent communications to:
(1) Detect poisoning or consensus manipulation; and
(2) Identify rogue or compromised AI agents in distributed or multi-agent environments?

### AAT-37 — AI & Autonomous Technologies System Value Chain

Does the organization document the sequence of events and relevant stakeholders involved in creating and deploying Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Autonomous Technologies (AAT)?

### AAT-37.1 — AI & Autonomous Technologies System Value Chain Fallbacks

Does the organization identify:
(1) Over-reliance on third-party data with Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Autonomous Technologies (AAT); and
(2) Fallback methods to address the inability to access third-party data, as necessary?

### AAT-38 — AI Model Resilience

Does the organization ensure AI models are designed with resilience capabilities that are sufficient to withstand reasonable threats?

### AAT-38.1 — AI Model Pollution

Does the organization prevent "model pollution" due to accidental and/or malicious inputs by an AI agent that can negatively alter the AI model?

### AAT-38.2 — Cascading Hallucination Defense

Does the organization detect and prevent the propagation of false data (e.g., hallucinations) within the AI model or between AI agents?

### AAT-38.3 — Resource Exhaustion & Denial of Service (DoS) Resilience

Does the organization monitor and prevent resource overload or Denial of Service (DoS) conditions through:
(1) Enforcement of quotas;
(2) Workload controls; and
(3) Auto-suspension of runaway AI agent processes?

### AAT-39 — AI Agent Governance

Does the organization ensure AI agents are designed, developed and deployed to securely operate under human oversight?

### AAT-39.1 — Infrastructure Hardening & Isolation

Does the organization protect, isolate and harden infrastructure resources used by AI agents, including:
(1) Resource allocation;
(2) Privilege management;
(3) Network segmentation; and
(4) Workload isolation?

### AAT-39.2 — AI Agent Limitations

Does the organization implement limitations for AI agents according to:
(1) Least privileges, where the AI agent operates with the minimal permissions necessary to perform designated tasks; and
(2) Least functionality, where the AI agent is restricted to communicate with the minimal Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) and networks necessary to perform designated tasks?

### AAT-39.3 — Tool & Application Programming Interface (API) Invocation Controls

Does the organization authenticate, authorize, validate and monitor all tool and Application Programming Interface (API) invocations by AI agents, including;
(1) Schema validation;
(2) Rate limiting;
(3) Access controls; and
(4) Output validation?

### AAT-39.4 — AI Agent Orchestration Protocol Safeguards

Does the organization validate, secure and restrict AI agent orchestration protocols to prevent:
(1) Unauthorized tool chaining;
(2) Context manipulation; and/or
(3) Protocol-based escalation?

### AAT-39.5 — AI Agent Data Pipeline & Input Integrity

Does the organization validate, sanitize and monitor all data inputs and retrieval pipelines for AI agents to:
(1) Ensure data provenance; and
(2) Prevent unauthorized access risks (e.g., injection, manipulation or exfiltration)?

### AAT-39.6 — AI Agent Privileged Role & Delegation Boundaries

Does the organization prevent privilege escalation or unauthorized delegation by AI agents by:
(1) Monitoring and enforcing dynamic roles; and
(2) Establishing cross-agent delegation boundaries and privileged actions?

### AAT-39.7 — AI Agent Data Access Restrictions

Does the organization restrict agent access to sensitive and/or regulated data so that AI agents cannot ingest, generate or act on unauthorized data?

### AAT-39.8 — AI Agent Data Extraction

Does the organization prevent AI agents from extracting sensitive and/or regulated data from volatile memory that can be exploited at a later point?

### AAT-39.9 — AI Agent Identity & Impersonation Defense

Does the organization ensure user identification and authentication methods are capable of preventing AI agents from
(1) Spoofing;
(2) Mimicry; and/or
(3) Impersonation attacks?

### AAT-39.10 — AI Agent Logic Integrity

Does the organization prevent AI agent logic from being subverted or manipulated?

### AAT-39.11 — Sandboxing AI Agents

Does the organization utilize a "sandbox" capability to restrict AI agents from unrestricted access to both local and remote resources?

### AAT-39.12 — AI Agent Prompt Injection Defense

Does the organization detect and mitigate prompt injection / input attacks that seek to manipulate AI agent instructions, bypass security, compliance and/or resilience controls or result in unauthorized actions?

### AAT-39.13 — AI Agent Kill Switch / User Control

Does the organization allow authorized users or operators to immediately halt or disable AI agent activity in case of unexpected behavior or harm?

### AAT-39.14 — AI Agent Adversarial & Red Team Testing

Does the organization regularly conduct adversarial testing that simulates attacks against AI agents to identify and mitigate vulnerabilities?

### AAT-39.15 — AI Agent Self-Modification Controls

Does the organization control, restrict and log AI agent self-modification?

### AAT-39.16 — Purging AI Agent Data

Does the organization restrict purging of any persistent memory or long-term data used by AI agents?

### AAT-39.17 — AI Agent Delegation and Chaining Control

Does the organization restrict agentic delegation, chaining and multi-agent communication to prevent unauthorized task escalation or emergent risks?

### AAT-39.18 — AI Agent Behavioral Drift Detection

Does the organization continuously monitor for behavioral drift or deviation from established AI agent baselines?

### AAT-39.19 — AI Agent Action Authentication & Authorization

Does the organization ensure that all AI agent-initiated actions are properly mapped to authenticated user or system identities, with enforced authorization checks?

### AAT-39.20 — AI Agent Transparency & Audit

Does the organization provide comprehensive audit trails of AI agent actions including:
(1) Rationales; and
(2) User/trigger mappings?

### AAT-39.21 — AI Agent Explainability

Does the organization:
(1) Provide human-understandable explanations for significant AI agent actions or decisions; and
(2) Enable users to contest outcomes?

### AAT-39.22 — AI Agent Ethics, Fairness & Bias Detection

Does the organization detect unfair, unethical or biased AI agent actions?

### AAT-39.23 — AI Agent Output Integrity & Verification

Does the organization validate AI agent-generated outputs through the use of:
(1) Content scanning; and
(2) Output vetting through human approvals, where appropriate?

### AAT-39.24 — AI Agent Resource Limiting

Does the organization use automated mechanisms to enforce resource limits for Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Autonomous Technologies (AAT), including:
(1) Energy consumption;
(2) Processing capacity; and
(3) Financial consumption (e.g., allocated budget)?

### AAT-40 — Agentic Output Traceability & Repudiation

Does the organization ensure AI agent actions offer non-repudiation and enable forensic examination to determine accountability?

### AAT-40.1 — AI Agent Logging

Does the organization generate event logs for Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Autonomous Technologies (AAT) actions to ensure transparency and auditability?

### AAT-40.2 — AI Agent Session Management

Does the organization control AI agent sessions by:
(1) Embedding session IDs into the requests to the AI model;
(2) Implementing capabilities to correlate sessions; and
(3) Terminating sessions after a defined time period?

### AAT-41 — Human-in-the-Loop Workload & Manipulation

Does the organization prevent cognitive overload or decision fatigue for humans-in-the-loop (HITL) through risk-based prioritization?

### AAT-42 — Robotic Process Automation (RPA)

Does the organization implement Robotic Process Automation (RPA) to improve efficiency, accuracy and speed for high-volume, repetitive and rules-based business processes?

### AAT-43 — Business Process Task Enumeration

Does the organization identify and enumerate business process task activities that can be executed both manually and in an automated fashion?

### AST-01 — Asset Management Policy

Does the organization establish a formal, documented asset management policy that:
 (1) Conveys executive management's intent;
 (2) Provides organizational direction and expected behaviors;
 (3) Is reviewed at least annually; and
 (4) Is updated, as necessary, to adapt to evolving risks, threats and other changes that affect the organization?

### AST-02 — Asset Governance

Does the organization facilitate an IT Asset Management (ITAM) program to implement and manage asset management controls?

### AST-03 — Standardized Naming Convention

Does the organization implement a scalable, standardized naming convention for Technology Assets, Applications, Services and/or Data (TAASD) that avoids asset naming conflicts?

### AST-04 — Asset Inventories

Does the organization perform inventories of Technology Assets, Applications, Services and/or Data (TAASD) that:
 (1) Accurately reflects the current TAASD in use;
 (2) Identifies authorized software products, including business justification details;
 (3) Is at the level of granularity deemed necessary for tracking and reporting;
 (4) Includes organization-defined information deemed necessary to achieve effective property accountability; and
 (5) Is available for review and audit by designated organizational personnel?

### AST-04.1 — Updates During Installations / Removals

Does the organization update asset inventories as part of component installations, removals and asset upgrades?

### AST-04.2 — Component Duplication Avoidance

Does the organization establish and maintain an authoritative source and repository to provide a trusted source and accountability for approved and implemented system components that prevents assets from being duplicated in other asset inventories?

### AST-05 — Identify Critical Assets

Does the organization identify and document the critical Technology Assets, Applications, Services and/or Data (TAASD) that support essential missions and business functions?

### AST-05.1 — Technology Assets, Applications, Services and/or Data (TAASD) Criticality Ratings

Does the organization assign Business Continuity & Disaster Recovery (BC/DR)-relevant criticality ratings for Technology Assets, Applications, Services and/or Data (TAASD)?

### AST-06 — Asset-Service Dependencies

Does the organization identify and assess the security of Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) that support more than one critical business function?

### AST-07 — Stakeholder Identification & Involvement

Does the organization identify and involve pertinent stakeholders of critical Technology Assets, Applications, Services and/or Data (TAASD) to support the ongoing secure management of those assets?

### AST-07.1 — Technology Assets, Applications, Services and/or Data (TAASD) Ownership Assignment

Does the organization ensure asset ownership responsibilities are assigned, tracked and managed at a team, individual, or responsible organization level to establish a common understanding of requirements for asset protection?

### AST-07.2 — Accountability Information

Does the organization include capturing the name, position and/or role of individuals responsible/accountable for administering assets as part of the technology asset inventory process?

### AST-08 — Comprehensive Asset Inventory Management

Does the organization maintain a dynamically updated inventory of Technology Assets, Applications, Services and/or Data (TAASD) that provides a highly contextualized understanding of every asset that is capable of providing operational visibility required to:
 (1) Detect anomalies;
 (2) Manage complex vulnerabilities;
 (3) Maintain compliance; and
 (4) Maintain resilient capabilities?

### AST-08.1 — Configuration Management Database (CMDB)

Does the organization implement and manage a Configuration Management Database (CMDB), or similar technology, to monitor and govern technology asset-specific information?

### AST-08.2 — Component Assignment

Does the organization bind components to a specific system?

### AST-09 — Asset Discovery

Does the organization use automated mechanisms to perform asset discovery to identify Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) connected to organizational networks, including assets not present in existing inventories?

### AST-09.1 — Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol (DHCP) Server Logging

Does the organization enable Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol (DHCP) server logging to:
 (1) Improve asset inventories;
 (2) Assist in detecting unknown systems; and
 (3) Provide support during troubleshooting or forensic analysis activities?

### AST-09.2 — Automated Network Asset Discovery

Does the organization automate network asset discovery through Software Defined Networking (SDN), or similar technologies, that analyzes network traffic to:
(1) Identify;
(2) Document; and
(3) Track devices?

### AST-09.3 — Automated Location Tracking

Does the organization track the geographic location of system components?

### AST-10 — Approved Technologies

Does the organization maintain a current list of approved technologies (hardware and software)?

### AST-10.1 — Authorized To Connect

Does the organization maintain a list of Technology Asset, Application and/or Service (TAAS) that are authorized to connect to organizational Technology Assets, Applications, Services and/or Data (TAASD)?

### AST-11 — Automated Unauthorized Component Detection

Does the organization use automated mechanisms to detect and alert upon the detection of unauthorized hardware, software and firmware components?

### AST-12 — Prohibited Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS)

Does the organization govern Supply Chain Risk Management (SCRM) sanctions that require the removal and prohibition of certain Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) that are designated as supply chain threats by a statutory or regulatory body?

### AST-13 — Software Licensing Restrictions

Does the organization protect Intellectual Property (IP) rights with software licensing restrictions?

### AST-14 — Provenance

Does the organization track the origin, development, ownership, location and changes to Technology Assets, Applications, Services and/or Data (TAASD)?

### AST-15 — Asset Categorization

Does the organization categorize Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS)?

### AST-15.1 — High-Risk Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) Categorization

Does the organization categorize a system and/or service as "High Risk" if it poses a significant risk of harm to an individual's:
(1) Health;
(2) Safety; and/or
(3) Fundamental human rights?

### AST-15.2 — Categorize Artificial Intelligence (AI)-Related Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS)

Does the organization categorize Artificial Intelligence (AI)-enabled Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS)?

### AST-15.3 — Asset Attributes

Does the organization dynamically associate asset-specific attributes to enable Attribute-Based Access Control (ABAC)?

### AST-16 — Asset Scope Classification

Does the organization determine security, compliance and resilience control applicability by identifying, assigning and documenting the appropriate asset scope categorization for all Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) and personnel (internal and third-parties)?

### AST-16.1 — Compliance-Specific Asset Identification

Does the organization create and maintain a current inventory of Technology Assets, Applications, Services and/or Data (TAASD) that are in scope for statutory, regulatory and/or contractual compliance obligations that provides sufficient detail to determine control applicability, based on asset scope categorization?

### AST-17 — Network Diagrams & Data Flow Diagrams (DFDs)

Does the organization maintain network architecture diagrams that:
 (1) Contain sufficient detail to assess the security of the network's architecture;
 (2) Reflect the current architecture of the network environment; and
 (3) Document all sensitive and/or regulated data flows?

### AST-17.1 — Control Applicability Boundary Graphical Representation

Does the organization ensure control applicability is appropriately-determined for Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) and third parties by graphically representing applicable boundaries?

### AST-17.2 — Data Action Mapping

Does the organization create and maintain a map of Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) where sensitive and/or regulated data is stored, transmitted or processed?

### AST-18 — Security of Assets & Media

Does the organization maintain strict control over Technology Assets, Applications, Services and/or Data (TAASD) to preserve confidentiality and integrity?

### AST-18.1 — Management Approval For External Media Transfer

Does the organization obtain management approval for any sensitive and/or regulated media that is transferred outside of its facilities?

### AST-19 — Technology Assets, Applications, Services and/or Data (TAASD) Storage

Does the organization ensure Technology Assets, Applications, Services and/or Data (TAASD) are stored in rooms and/or facilities with reasonable physical security protections?

### AST-19.1 — Temporary Asset Storage In Automobiles

Does the organization educate users on the need to physically secure laptops and other mobile devices out of sight when traveling, preferably in the trunk of a vehicle?

### AST-20 — Unattended End-User Equipment

Does the organization implement enhanced protection measures for unattended technology assets to protect against tampering and unauthorized access?

### AST-21 — Kiosks & Point of Interaction (PoI) Devices

Does the organization appropriately protect devices that capture sensitive and/or regulated data via direct physical interaction from tampering and substitution?

### AST-22 — Secure Disposal, Destruction or Re-Use of Equipment

Does the organization securely dispose of, destroy or repurpose technology assets using organization-defined techniques and methods to prevent:
 (1) Data recovery; and
 (2) Components from being resold, redistributed and/or reused through unauthorized channels?

### AST-23 — Return of Assets

Does the organization ensure that employees and third-party users return all organizational assets in their possession upon termination of employment, contract or agreement?

### AST-24 — Removal of Assets

Does the organization authorize, control and track technology assets entering and exiting organizational facilities?

### AST-25 — Use of Personal Devices

Does the organization restrict the possession and/or use of personally-owned Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) within organization-controlled facilities?

### AST-26 — Use of Third-Party Devices

Does the organization reduce the risk associated with third-party assets that are connected to the network from:
 (1) Harming organizational assets;
 (2) Accessing unauthorized resources within the organization; and/or
 (3) Exfiltrating organizational data?

### AST-27 — Bring Your Own Device (BYOD) Usage

Does the organization implement and govern a Bring Your Own Device (BYOD) program to reduce risk associated with personally-owned devices in the workplace?

### AST-28 — Usage Parameters

Does the organization monitor and enforce usage parameters that limit the potential damage caused from the unauthorized or unintentional alteration of system parameters?

### AST-29 — Technology Asset Inspections

Does the organization physically and logically inspect critical technology assets to detect evidence of tampering?

### AST-29.1 — Physical Tampering Detection

Does the organization periodically inspect systems and system components for Indicators of Compromise (IoC)?

### AST-29.2 — Logical Tampering Protection

Does the organization assess the integrity of critical Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) to detect evidence of tampering, where:
(1)	Logical assessments evaluate the integrity of critical components (e.g., configuration settings); and
(2)	Physical assessments evaluate assets for evidence of unauthorized access and/or modifications?

### AST-30 — Roots of Trust Protection

Does the organization provision and protect the confidentiality, integrity and authenticity of product supplier keys and data that can be used as a “roots of trust” basis for integrity verification?

### AST-31 — Telecommunications Equipment

Does the organization establish usage restrictions and implementation guidance for telecommunication equipment to prevent potential damage or unauthorized modification and to prevent potential eavesdropping?

### AST-32 — Travel-Only Devices

Does the organization issue personnel travelling overseas with temporary, loaner or "travel-only" end user technology (e.g., laptops and mobile devices) when travelling to authoritarian countries with a higher-than average risk for Intellectual Property (IP) theft or espionage against individuals and private companies?

### AST-33 — Re-Imaging Devices After Travel

Does the organization re-image end user technology (e.g., laptops and mobile devices) when returning from overseas travel to an authoritarian country with a higher-than average risk for Intellectual Property (IP) theft or espionage against individuals and private companies?

### AST-34 — Jump Server

Does the organization conduct remote system administrative functions via a "jump box" or "jump server" that is located in a separate network zone to user workstations?

### AST-35 — Database Management System (DBMS)

Does the organization implement and maintain Database Management Systems (DBMSs), where applicable?

### AST-36 — Decommissioning

Does the organization ensure Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) are properly decommissioned so that data is properly transitioned to new systems or archived in accordance with applicable organizational standards, as well as statutory, regulatory and contractual obligations?

### AST-37 — Technology Lifecycle Management

Does the organization manage the usable lifecycles of Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS)?

### AST-37.1 — Stable Versions

Does the organization install the latest stable version of any software and/or security-related updates on all applicable systems?

### AST-37.2 — Removal of Previous Versions

Does the organization remove old versions of software and firmware components after updated versions have been installed?

### AST-38 — Technical Debt Reviews

Does the organization conduct ongoing “technical debt” reviews of hardware and software technologies to remediate outdated and/or unsupported technologies?

### AST-39 — Unsupported Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS)

Does the organization prevent unsupported Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) by:
(1) Removing and/or replacing TAAS when support for the components is no longer available from the developer, vendor or manufacturer; and
(2) Requiring justification and documented approval for the continued use of unsupported TAAS required to satisfy mission/business needs?

### AST-39.1 — Alternate Sources for Continued Support

Does the organization provide in-house support or contract external providers for support with unsupported Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS)?

### AST-40 — Predictable Failure Analysis

Does the organization determine the Mean Time to Failure (MTTF) for system components in specific environments of operation?

### BCD-01 — Business Continuity & Disaster Recovery Policy

Does the organization establish a formal, documented Business Continuity and Disaster Recovery (BC/DR) policy that:
 (1) Conveys executive management's intent;
 (2) Provides organizational direction and expected behaviors;
 (3) Is reviewed at least annually; and
 (4) Is updated, as necessary, to adapt to evolving risks, threats and other changes that affect the organization?

### BCD-02 — Business Continuity Management System (BCMS)

Does the organization operate a Business Continuity Management System (BCMS) to achieve resilient Technology Assets, Applications, Services and/or Data (TAASD) during:
 (1) Routine operations; and
 (2) Adverse conditions?

### BCD-02.1 — Defined Operational Resilience Requirements

Does the organization define operational resilience requirements for Technology Assets, Applications, Services and/or Data (TAASD) to operate in a controlled and acceptable manner during:
 (1) Routine operations; and
 (2) Adverse conditions?

### BCD-03 — Operational Resilience Capabilities

Does the organization ensure capabilities are implemented to provide operational resilience to:
 (1) Unintentional errors; and
 (2) Intentional attack or circumvention?

### BCD-04 — Business Continuity & Disaster Recovery (BC/DR) Plans

Does the organization ensure process owners establish and maintain formal Business Continuity & Disaster Recovery (BC/DR) plans to ensure information is detailed enough, accurate and representative of current operations in order to sustain and/or restore operations under adverse conditions?

### BCD-04.1 — Recovery Time / Point Objectives (RTO / RPO)

Does the organization facilitate recovery operations in accordance with Recovery Time Objectives (RTOs) and Recovery Point Objectives (RPOs)?

### BCD-05 — Recovery Operations Criteria

Does the organization define specific criteria that must be met to initiate Business Continuity / Disaster Recover (BC/DR) plans that facilitate business continuity operations capable of meeting applicable Recovery Time Objectives (RTOs) and Recovery Point Objectives (RPOs)?

### BCD-06 — Recovery Operations Communications

Does the organization communicate the status of recovery activities and progress in restoring operational capabilities to designated internal and external stakeholders?

### BCD-06.1 — Alternate Communications Channels

Does the organization maintain command and control capabilities via alternate communications channels and designating alternative decision makers if primary decision makers are unavailable?

### BCD-07 — Ongoing Contingency Planning

Does the organization update contingency plans due to changes affecting:
(1) People (e.g., personnel changes);
(2) Processes (e.g., new, altered or decommissioned business practices, including third-party services)
(3) Technologies (e.g., new, altered or decommissioned technologies);
(4) Data (e.g., changes to data flows and/or data repositories);
(5) Facilities (e.g., new, altered or decommissioned physical infrastructure); and/or
(6) Feedback from contingency plan testing activities?

### BCD-07.1 — Contingency Planning Components

Does the organization identify components that potentially impact its ability to execute contingency plans, including changes to:
(1) Personnel roles;
(2) Business processes (including the use of third-party services);
(3) Deployed technologies;
(4) Data repositories and/or data flows; and/or
(5) Physical infrastructure?

### BCD-07.2 — Contingency Plan Update Notifications

Does the organization keep stakeholders informed of changes to contingency plans?

### BCD-07.3 — Coordinate with Related Plans

Does the organization coordinate contingency plan development with internal and external elements responsible for related plans?

### BCD-07.4 — Coordinate With External Service Providers

Does the organization coordinate internal contingency plans with the contingency plans of external service providers to ensure that contingency requirements can be satisfied?

### BCD-08 — Resume All Missions & Business Functions

Does the organization resume all missions and business functions within Recovery Time Objectives (RTOs) of the contingency plan's activation?

### BCD-08.1 — Continue Essential Mission & Business Functions

Does the organization continue essential missions and business functions with little or no loss of operational continuity and sustain that continuity until full system restoration at primary processing and/or storage sites?

### BCD-08.2 — Resume Essential Missions & Business Functions

Does the organization resume essential missions and business functions within an organization-defined time period of contingency plan activation?

### BCD-09 — Contingency Training

Does the organization adequately train contingency personnel and applicable stakeholders in their contingency roles and responsibilities?

### BCD-09.1 — Simulated Events

Does the organization incorporate simulated events into contingency training to facilitate effective response by personnel in crisis situations?

### BCD-09.2 — Automated Training Environments

Does the organization use automated mechanisms to provide a more thorough and realistic contingency training environment?

### BCD-10 — Contingency Plan Testing & Exercises

Does the organization conduct tests and/or exercises to evaluate the contingency plan's effectiveness and its readiness to execute the plan?

### BCD-10.1 — Coordinated Testing with Related Plans

Does the organization coordinate contingency plan testing with internal and external elements responsible for related plans?

### BCD-10.2 — Contingency Plan Testing For Alternate Storage & Processing Sites

Does the organization test contingency plans at alternate storage & processing sites to both familiarize contingency personnel with the facility and evaluate the capabilities of the alternate processing site to support contingency operations?

### BCD-11 — Contingency Plan Root Cause Analysis (RCA) & Lessons Learned

Does the organization conduct a Root Cause Analysis (RCA) and "lessons learned" activity every time the contingency plan is activated?

### BCD-12 — Alternate Storage Site

Does the organization establish an alternate storage site that stores both the assets and necessary agreements needed for the recovery of Technology Assets, Applications, Services and/or Data (TAASD)?

### BCD-12.1 — Separation from Primary Storage Site

Does the organization separate the alternate storage site from the primary storage site to reduce susceptibility to similar threats?

### BCD-12.2 — Primary Storage Site Accessibility

Does the organization identify and mitigate potential accessibility problems to the alternate storage sites in the event of an area-wide disruption or disaster?

### BCD-13 — Alternate Processing Site

Does the organization establish an alternate processing site that provides security measures equivalent to that of the primary site?

### BCD-13.1 — Separation from Primary Processing Site

Does the organization separate the alternate processing site from the primary processing site to reduce susceptibility to similar threats?

### BCD-13.2 — Alternate Processing Site Accessibility

Does the organization identify and mitigate potential accessibility problems to the alternate processing sites and possible mitigation actions, in the event of an area-wide disruption or disaster?

### BCD-14 — Alternate Site Priority of Service

Does the organization address priority-of-service provisions in alternate processing and storage sites that support availability requirements, including Recovery Time Objectives (RTOs)?

### BCD-15 — Preparation for Use

Does the organization prepare the alternate processing alternate to support essential missions and business functions so that the alternate site is capable of being used as the primary site?

### BCD-16 — Inability to Return to Primary Site

Does the organization plan and prepare for both natural and manmade circumstances that preclude returning to the primary site?

### BCD-16.1 — Personnel Transfer to Alternate Processing / Storage Site

Does the organization redeploy personnel to other roles during a disruptive event or in the execution of a continuity plan?

### BCD-17 — Telecommunications Services Availability

Does the organization reduce the likelihood of a single point of failure with primary telecommunications services?

### BCD-17.1 — Telecommunications Priority of Service Provisions

Does the organization formalize primary and alternate telecommunications service agreements contain priority-of-service provisions that support availability requirements, including Recovery Time Objectives (RTOs)?

### BCD-17.2 — Separation of Primary / Alternate Providers

Does the organization reduce threat susceptibility by obtaining services from alternative providers that are different from the primary service providers?

### BCD-18 — Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) Recovery & Reconstitution

Does the organization ensure the secure recovery and reconstitution of Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) to a known state after a disruption, compromise or failure?

### BCD-18.1 — Restore Within Time Period

Does the organization restore Technology Assets, Applications, Services and/or Data (TAASD) within organization-defined restoration time-periods from configuration-controlled and integrity-protected information; representing a known, operational state for the asset?

### BCD-18.2 — Recovery Images

Does the organization reimage assets from configuration-controlled and integrity-protected images that represent a secure, operational state?

### BCD-19 — Isolated Recovery Environment

Does the organization utilize an isolated, non-production environment to perform data backup and recovery operations through offline, cloud or off-site capabilities?

### BCD-20 — Reserve Hardware

Does the organization purchase and maintain a sufficient reserve of spare hardware to ensure essential missions and business functions can be maintained in the event of a supply chain disruption?

### BCD-21 — Redundant Secondary System

Does the organization maintain a failover capability, which is not collocated with the primary Technology Asset, Application and/or Service (TAAS), which can be activated with little-to-no loss of information or disruption to operations?

### BCD-22 — Failover Capability

Does the organization implement real-time or near-real-time failover capability to maintain availability of critical Technology Assets, Applications, Services and/or Data (TAASD)?

### BCD-23 — Resilient Data Backup Architecture

Does the organization maintain a secure, immutable backup
 architecture?

### BCD-24 — Data Backups

Does the organization create recurring backups of data, software and/or system images, as well as verify the integrity of these backups, to ensure the availability of the data to satisfy Recovery Time Objectives (RTOs) and Recovery Point Objectives (RPOs)?

### BCD-24.1 — Transfer to Alternate Storage Site

Does the organization transfer backup data to the alternate storage site at a rate that is capable of meeting both Recovery Time Objectives (RTOs) and Recovery Point Objectives (RPOs)?

### BCD-24.2 — Separate Storage for Critical Information

Does the organization store backup copies of critical software and other security-related information in a separate facility or in a fire-rated container that is not collocated with the system being backed up?

### BCD-24.3 — Cryptographic Protection

Are cryptographic mechanisms utilized to prevent the unauthorized disclosure and/or modification of backup information?

### BCD-25 — Redundant Copies of Business-Critical Data

Does the organization maintain redundant copies of all business-critical data within one (1), or more, logically vaulted or offline environments?

### BCD-26 — Transaction Recovery

Does the organization utilize specialized backup mechanisms that will allow transaction recovery for transaction-based Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) in accordance with Recovery Point Objectives (RPOs)?

### BCD-27 — Data Replication

Does the organization replicate data to alternate storage or processing locations at a frequency capable of satisfying Recovery Point Objectives (RPOs)?

### BCD-28 — Data Archiving

Does the organization archive data that is no longer in active use to secure storage, in accordance with applicable statutory, regulatory and contractual retention obligations?

### BCD-29 — Continuous Data Protection (CDP)

Does the organization use automated mechanisms to implement Continuous Data Protection (CDP) to capture data changes as they occur, enabling granular data recovery to a specific point in time?

### BCD-30 — Data Backup Access

Does the organization restrict access to backups to privileged users with assigned roles for data backup and recovery operations?

### BCD-31 — Data Backup & Restoration Hardware Protection

Does the organization protect backup and restoration hardware and software?

### BCD-31.1 — Restoration Integrity Verification

Does the organization verify the integrity of backups and other restoration assets prior to using them for restoration?

### BCD-32 — Testing for Reliability & Integrity

Does the organization routinely test backups that verify the reliability of the backup process, as well as the integrity and availability of the data?

### BCD-32.1 — Test Restoration Using Sampling

Does the organization utilize sampling of available backups to test recovery capabilities as part of business continuity plan testing?

### BCD-33 — Data Backup Modification and/or Destruction

Does the organization restrict access to modify and/or delete backups to privileged users with assigned data backup and recovery operations roles?

### BCD-33.1 — Dual Authorization For Sensitive / Regulated Backup Media Destruction

Does the organization implement and enforce dual authorization for the deletion or destruction of sensitive backup media and data?

### CAP-01 — Capacity & Performance Planning Policy

Does the organization establish a formal, documented capacity and performance planning policy that:
 (1) Conveys executive management's intent;
 (2) Provides organizational direction and expected behaviors;
 (3) Is reviewed at least annually; and
 (4) Is updated, as necessary, to adapt to evolving risks, threats and other changes that affect the organization?

### CAP-02 — Capacity & Performance Management

Does the organization facilitate the implementation of capacity management controls to ensure optimal system performance to meet expected and anticipated future capacity requirements?

### CAP-03 — Capacity Planning

Does the organization conduct capacity planning so that necessary capacity for information processing, telecommunications and environmental support will exist during contingency operations?

### CAP-04 — Resource Priority

Does the organization control resource utilization of Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) that are susceptible to Denial of Service (DoS) attacks to limit and prioritize the use of resources?

### CAP-05 — Performance Monitoring

Does the organization use automated mechanisms to centrally-monitor and alert on the operating state and health status of critical Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS)?

### CAP-06 — Elastic Expansion

Does the organization automatically scale the resources available for Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS), as demand conditions change?

### CAP-07 — Regional Delivery

Does the organization support operations that are geographically dispersed via regional delivery of technological Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS)?

### CAP-08 — Resiliency Planning For Alternate Sites

Does the organization include resiliency planning in performance and capacity planning to ensure alternate storage and/or processing sites have adequate capacity to run production operations throughout the duration of Business Continuity and Disaster Recovery (BD/DR) operations?

### CHG-01 — Change Management Policy

Does the organization establish a formal, documented change management policy that:
 (1) Conveys executive management's intent;
 (2) Provides organizational direction and expected behaviors;
 (3) Is reviewed at least annually; and
 (4) Is updated, as necessary, to adapt to evolving risks, threats and other changes that affect the organization?

### CHG-02 — Change Management Program

Does the organization facilitate the implementation of a change management program?

### CHG-03 — Configuration Change Control

Does the organization govern the technical configuration change control processes?

### CHG-04 — Prohibition Of Changes
