Does the organization prohibit unauthorized changes, unless approved through the organization's defined change management processes?

### CHG-04.1 — Access Restriction For Change

Does the organization define, document, approve and enforce access restrictions associated with changes to Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS)?

### CHG-04.2 — Role-Based Permissions To Implement Changes

Does the organization limit the ability to implement Technology Asset, Application and/or Service (TAAS) changes to designated privileged roles?

### CHG-04.3 — Dual Authorization for Changes To Critical / Sensitive Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS)

Does the organization enforce a two-person rule for implementing changes to critical Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS)?

### CHG-04.4 — Dual Approval For High-Impact Environments

Does the organization require dual approval for any changes that might result in a serious incident that could adversely impact:
(1) Business processes; and/or
(2) Technology Assets, Applications, Services and/or Data (TAASD)?

### CHG-05 — Security, Compliance & Resilience Representative for Asset Lifecycle Changes

Does the organization include a cybersecurity and/or data protection representative in the configuration change control review process?

### CHG-06 — Security Impact Analysis for Changes

Does the organization analyze proposed changes for potential security impacts, prior to the implementation of the change?

### CHG-07 — Test, Validate & Document Changes

Does the organization appropriately test and document proposed changes in a non-production environment before changes are implemented in a production environment?

### CHG-08 — Stakeholder Notification of Changes

Does the organization ensure stakeholders are made aware of and understand the impact of proposed changes?

### CHG-09 — Control Functionality Verification

Does the organization verify the functionality of security, compliance and resilience controls following implemented changes to ensure applicable controls operate as designed?

### CHG-09.1 — Report Verification Results

Does the organization report the results of security, compliance and resilience capability verification to appropriate organizational management?

### CHG-10 — Emergency Changes

Does the organization govern change management procedures for "emergency" changes?

### CHG-10.1 — Documenting Emergency Changes

Does the organization document the results of "emergency" changes, including an explanation for why standard change management procedures could not be followed?

### CHG-11 — Post Configuration Change Reviews

Does the organization perform after-the-fact reviews of configuration change logs to discover any unauthorized changes?

### CHG-11.1 — Automated Security Response

Does the organization use automated mechanisms to restore organization-approved configuration settings upon the detection of unauthorized configurations change(s)?

### CHG-12 — Unauthorized Software Installation Alerts

Does the organization use automated mechanisms to generate an alert upon the detection of an unauthorized software installation?

### CHG-13 — Signed Components

Does the organization prevent the installation of software and firmware components without verification that the component has been digitally signed using an organization-approved certificate authority?

### CLD-01 — Cloud Security Policy

Does the organization establish a formal, documented cloud security policy that:
 (1) Conveys executive management's intent;
 (2) Provides organizational direction and expected behaviors;
 (3) Is reviewed at least annually; and
 (4) Is updated, as necessary, to adapt to evolving risks, threats and other changes that affect the organization?

### CLD-02 — Cloud Services

Does the organization facilitate the implementation of cloud management controls to ensure cloud instances are secure and in-line with industry practices?

### CLD-03 — Cloud Infrastructure Onboarding

Does the organization ensure cloud services are designed and configured so Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) are secured in accordance with applicable organizational standards, as well as statutory, regulatory and contractual obligations?

### CLD-03.1 — Customer Responsibility Matrix (CRM)

Does the organization formally document a Customer Responsibility Matrix (CRM), delineating assigned responsibilities for security, compliance and resilience controls between the Cloud Service Provider (CSP) and its customers?

### CLD-04 — Cloud Infrastructure Offboarding

Does the organization ensure cloud services are decommissioned so that data is securely transitioned to new systems or archived in accordance with applicable organizational standards, as well as statutory, regulatory and contractual obligations?

### CLD-05 — Cloud Security Architecture

Does the organization ensure the cloud security architecture supports its technology strategy to securely design, configure and maintain cloud employments?

### CLD-06 — Cloud Infrastructure Security Subnet

Does the organization host security-specific technologies in a dedicated subnet?

### CLD-07 — Multi-Tenant Environments

Does the organization ensure multi-tenant owned or managed assets (physical and virtual) are designed and governed such that provider and customer (tenant) user access is appropriately segmented from other tenant users?

### CLD-07.1 — Multi-Tenant Event Logging Capabilities

Does the organization ensure Multi-Tenant Service Providers (MTSP) facilitate security event logging capabilities for its customers that are consistent with applicable statutory, regulatory and/or contractual obligations?

### CLD-07.2 — Multi-Tenant Forensics Capabilities

Does the organization ensure Multi-Tenant Service Providers (MTSP) facilitate prompt forensic investigations in the event of a suspected or confirmed security incident?

### CLD-07.3 — Multi-Tenant Incident Response Capabilities

Does the organization ensure Multi-Tenant Service Providers (MTSP) facilitate prompt response to suspected or confirmed security incidents and vulnerabilities, including timely notification to affected customers?

### CLD-08 — Data Handling & Portability

Does the organization ensure cloud providers use secure protocols for the import, export and management of data in cloud-based Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS)?

### CLD-09 — Standardized Virtualization Formats

Does the organization ensure interoperability by requiring cloud providers to use industry-recognized formats and provide documentation of custom changes for review?

### CLD-10 — Sensitive Data In Public Cloud Providers

Does the organization limit and manage the storage of sensitive and/or regulated data in public cloud providers?

### CLD-11 — Cloud Access Security Broker (CASB)

Does the organization utilize a Cloud Access Security Broker (CASB), or similar technology, to provide boundary protection and monitoring functions that both provide access to the cloud and protect the organization from misuse of cloud resources?

### CLD-12 — Hosted Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS)

Does the organization specify applicable security, compliance and resilience that must be implemented on external Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS), consistent with the contractual obligations established with the External Service Providers (ESP) owning, operating and/or maintaining external TAAS?

### CLD-12.1 — Authorized Individuals For Hosted Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS)

Does the organization authorize specified individuals to access External Service Providers (ESP) owned, operated and/or maintained external Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS)?

### CLD-12.2 — Sensitive / Regulated Data On Hosted Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS)

Does the organization define formal processes to store, process and/or transmit sensitive and/or regulated data using External Service Providers (ESP) owned, operated and/or maintained external Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS), in accordance with all applicable statutory, regulatory and/or contractual obligations?

### CLD-13 — Prohibition On Unverified Hosted Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS)

Does the organization prohibit access to, or usage of, hosted Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) until applicable security, compliance and/or resilience control implementation is verified?

### CPL-01 — Compliance Policy

Does the organization establish a formal, documented compliance policy that:
 (1) Conveys executive management's intent;
 (2) Provides organizational direction and expected behaviors;
 (3) Is reviewed at least annually; and
 (4) Is updated, as necessary, to adapt to evolving risks, threats and other changes that affect the organization?

### CPL-02 — Statutory, Regulatory & Contractual Compliance

Does the organization facilitate the identification and implementation of relevant statutory, regulatory and contractual controls?

### CPL-03 — Compliance Scope

Does the organization document and validate the scope of security, compliance and resilience controls that are determined to meet statutory, regulatory and/or contractual compliance obligations?

### CPL-04 — Ability To Demonstrate Conformity

Does the organization ensure the organization is able to demonstrate security, compliance and/or resilience capability conformity with applicable cybersecurity and data protection laws, regulations and/or contractual obligations?

### CPL-04.1 — Conformity Assessment

Does the organization conduct assessments to demonstrate security, compliance and/or resilience capability conformity with applicable cybersecurity and data protection laws, regulations and/or contractual obligations?

### CPL-04.2 — Designated Certifying Official

Does the organization designate an individual the authority to make statements of conformity on behalf of the organization?

### CPL-04.3 — Conformity Attestations

Does the organization have a certifying official attest to the accuracy of conformity attestations, based on applicable laws, regulations and/or contractual criteria?

### CPL-04.4 — Declaration of Conformity

Does the organization generate a declaration of conformity for each conformity assessment, where the document:
(1) Is concise;
(2) Unambiguously reflects the current status;
(3) Is physically or electronically signed; and
(4) Where possible, is machine readable?

### CPL-05 — Conformity Monitoring

Does the organization validate that Technology Assets, Applications, Services and/or Data (TAASD) conform to its security, compliance and/or resilience policies, standards and other applicable requirements?

### CPL-05.1 — Functional Review Of Security, Compliance & Resilience Controls

Does the organization regularly review Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) for adherence to its security, compliance and/or resilience policies and standards?

### CPL-06 — Non-Conformity Oversight

Does the organization document and review instances of non-compliance with statutory, regulatory and/or contractual obligations to develop appropriate risk mitigation actions?

### CPL-06.1 — Non-Conformity Corrective Action

Does the organization take corrective action to remediate instances of non-conformity with applicable statutory, regulatory, and/or contractual compliance obligations?

### CPL-07 — Executive Leadership Oversight of Security, Compliance & Resilience Controls

Does the organization provide a security, compliance and resilience controls oversight function that reports to its executive leadership?

### CPL-07.1 — Internal Audit Function

Does the organization implement an internal audit function that is capable of providing executive management with insights into the overall management of the organization's security, compliance and resilience capabilities?

### CPL-07.2 — Periodic Audits

Does the organization conduct periodic audits of security, compliance and resilience controls to evaluate conformity with its documented policies, standards and procedures?

### CPL-07.3 — Audit Planning Activities

Does the organization thoughtfully plan audits by including input from operational risk and compliance partners to minimize the impact of audit-related activities on business operations?

### CPL-08 — Independent Assessors

Does the organization utilize independent assessors to evaluate security, compliance and resilience at planned intervals or when the Technology Asset, Application and/or Service (TAAS) undergoes significant changes?

### CPL-09 — Assessment Team Subject Matter Expertise

Does the organization ensure individuals performing audits and/or assessments have reasonable:
(1) Professional qualifications to perform the audit and/or assessment; and
(2) Subject matter expertise to perform review, interview and test activities for in-scope People, Processes, Technologies, Data and/or Facilities (PPTDF)?

### CPL-10 — Assessor Access

Does the organization grant assessors minimum necessary access to conduct conformity assessments, including:
(1) Logical access to design, development, production, inspection and testing artifacts; and
(2) Physical access to facilities?

### CPL-11 — Assessment Methods

Does the organization define acceptable methods to conduct a cybersecurity and/or data protection assessment?

### CPL-12 — Assessment Rigor

Does the organization define the level of assessment rigor necessary to conduct a cybersecurity and/or data protection assessment?

### CPL-13 — Assurance Levels (AL)

Does the organization utilize defined Assurance Levels (AL) for assessment activities to standardize the following assurance attributes:
(1) Depth that addresses the rigor and level of detail of the assessment; and
(2) Coverage that addresses the scope and breadth of the assessment?

### CPL-14 — Control Reciprocity

Does the organization define instances of control reciprocity within assessment boundaries?

### CPL-15 — Control Inheritance

Does the organization define instances of control inheritance within assessment boundaries?

### CPL-16 — Evidence Request List (ERL)

Does the organization define an Evidence Request List (ERL) prior to the start of a cybersecurity and/or data protection assessment?

### CPL-17 — Evidence Sampling

Does the organization define evidence sampling criteria for cybersecurity and/or data protection assessments?

### CPL-18 — Continuous Control Monitoring (CCM)

Does the organization use automated mechanisms to perform Continuous Control Monitoring (CCM) to assess and report the conformity status of the organization's Technology Assets, Applications, Services and Data (TAASD) against applicable security, compliance and resilience controls?

### CPL-19 — Legal Assessment of Investigative Inquires

Does the organization determine whether a government agency has an applicable and valid legal basis to request data from the organization and what further steps need to be taken, if necessary?

### CPL-19.1 — Investigation Request Notifications

Does the organization notify customers about investigation request notifications, unless the applicable legal basis for a government agency's action prohibits notification (e.g., potential criminal prosecution)?

### CPL-19.2 — Investigation Access Restrictions

Does the organization support official investigations by provisioning government investigators with "least privileges" and "least functionality" to ensure that government investigators only have access to the Technology Assets, Applications, Services and/or Data (TAASD) needed to perform the investigation?

### CPL-20 — Government Surveillance

Does the organization constrain the host government from having unrestricted and non-monitored access to its Technology Assets, Applications, Services and/or Data (TAASD) that could potentially violate other applicable statutory, regulatory and/or contractual obligations?

### CPL-21 — Potential Human Rights Abuses

Does the organization constrain the supply of physical and/or digital activity logs to the host government that can directly lead to contravention of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR), as well as other applicable statutory, regulatory and/or contractual obligations?

### CPL-22 — Grievances

Does the organization govern the intake and analysis of grievances related to its cybersecurity and/or data protection practices?

### CPL-22.1 — Grievance Response

Does the organization respond to legitimate grievances related to its cybersecurity and/or data protection practices?

### CPL-23 — Localized Representation

Does the organization appoint localized representation with a physical presence in localities, as required by applicable laws and/or regulations?

### CPL-23.1 — Representative Powers

Does the organization contract localized representation to perform specified functions in regard to representing statutory and/or regulatory compliance matters?

### CPL-24 — Dual Use Technology

Does the organization govern technologies and/or data that have potential:
(1) Dual-use capabilities for civil and military;
(2) Use by terrorists; and/or
(3) Weapons of Mass Destruction (WMD) applications?

### CPL-24.1 — USML or CCL Identification

Does the organization identify if the organization handles United States Munitions List (USML) or Commerce Control List (CCL):
(1) Items;
(2) Technical data; and/or
(3) Provides defense services?

### CPL-24.2 — Export-Controlled Access Restrictions

Does the organization restrict logical and physical access to United States (US) export-controlled data to US:
(1) Citizens; and/or
(2) Green Card holders?

### CPL-24.3 — Export Activities Documentation

Does the organization generate detailed logs of export-controlled data including:
(1) Logical and physical access; and
(2) Export activities?

### CPL-25 — Statement of Applicability (SOA)

Does the organization produce a Statement of Applicability (SOA), or similar document, for compliance-related scoping activities?

### CPL-26 — Work Products

Does the organization produce work products (e.g., process artifacts) that demonstrate the ability to comply with applicable requirements?

### CPL-26.1 — Defensible Evidence of Due Diligence

Does the organization produce evidence of due diligence activities performed, capable of withstanding external audit or regulatory scrutiny?

### CPL-26.2 — Defensible Evidence of Due Care

Does the organization produce evidence of due care activities performed, capable of withstanding external audit or regulatory scrutiny?

### CPL-27 — Security, Compliance & Resilience Status Reporting

Does the organization submit status reporting of its security, compliance and/or resilience program to applicable statutory and/or regulatory authorities, as required?

### CPL-28 — AI & Autonomous Technologies Registration

Does the organization maintain a current registration for Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Autonomous Technologies (AAT) with the appropriate governing body, as required by statutory or regulatory requirements?

### CPL-29 — Control Assurance Automation (CAA) Oversight

Does the organization bring Control Assurance Automation (CAA) engineering pipelines, tooling and automated collection under the same governance and risk oversight applied to other technology functions?

### CPL-30 — Control Assurance Automation (CAA) Evidence Integrity & Provenance

Does the organization preserve the integrity and chain of custody of logs, telemetry and evidence collected by Control Assurance Automation (CAA) automation, including:
 (1) Verification of source-to-repository transfer; and
 (2) Tamper-evident storage?

### CFG-01 — Configuration Management Policy

Does the organization establish a formal, documented configuration management policy that:
 (1) Conveys executive management's intent;
 (2) Provides organizational direction and expected behaviors;
 (3) Is reviewed at least annually; and
 (4) Is updated, as necessary, to adapt to evolving risks, threats and other changes that affect the organization?

### CFG-02 — Configuration Management Program

Does the organization facilitate the implementation of configuration management controls?

### CFG-03 — Least Functionality

Does the organization configure systems to provide only essential capabilities by specifically prohibiting or restricting the use of ports, protocols, and/or services?

### CFG-03.1 — Baseline Tailoring

Does the organization allow baseline controls to be specialized or customized by applying a defined set of tailoring actions that are specific to:
 (1) Mission / business functions;
 (2) Operational environment;
 (3) Specific threats or vulnerabilities; or
 (4) Other conditions or situations that could affect mission / business success?

### CFG-03.2 — Development & Test Environment Configurations

Does the organization manage baseline configurations for development and test environments separately from operational baseline configurations to minimize the risk of unintentional changes?

### CFG-04 — Secure Baseline Configurations

Does the organization develop, document and maintain secure baseline configurations for Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) that are consistent with industry-accepted system hardening standards?

### CFG-04.1 — Account Lockout

Does the organization enforce a limit for consecutive invalid login attempts by a user during an organization-defined time period and automatically locks the account when the maximum number of unsuccessful attempts is exceeded?

### CFG-04.2 — Concurrent Session Control

Does the organization limit the number of concurrent sessions for each system account?

### CFG-04.3 — Session Lock

Does the organization initiate a session lock after an organization-defined time period of inactivity, or upon receiving a request from a user and retain the session lock until the user reestablishes access using established identification and authentication methods?

### CFG-04.4 — Pattern-Hiding Displays

Does the organization implement pattern-hiding displays to conceal information previously visible on the display during the session lock?

### CFG-04.5 — Session Termination

Does the organization use automated mechanisms to log out users, both locally on the network and for remote sessions, at the end of the session or after an organization-defined period of inactivity?

### CFG-04.6 — User-Initiated Logouts / Message Displays

Does the organization provide a logout capability and display an explicit logout message to users indicating the reliable termination of the session?

### CFG-04.7 — Non-Console Administrative Access

Are cryptographic mechanisms utilized to protect the confidentiality and integrity of non-console administrative access?

### CFG-04.8 — Wireless Access Authentication & Encryption

Does the organization protect the confidentiality and integrity of wireless networking technologies by implementing authentication and strong encryption?

### CFG-04.9 — Bluetooth & Wireless Devices

Does the organization prevent the usage of Bluetooth and wireless devices (e.g., Near Field Communications (NFC)) in sensitive areas or unless used in a Radio Frequency (RF)-screened building?

### CFG-04.10 — Infrared Communications

Does the organization prevent line of sight and reflected infrared (IR) communications use in an unsecured space?

### CFG-04.11 — Microphones & Web Cameras

Does the organization configure assets to prohibit the use of endpoint-based microphones and web cameras in secure areas or where sensitive and/or regulated information is discussed?

### CFG-04.12 — Multi-Function Devices (MFD)

Does the organization securely configure Multi-Function Devices (MFD) according to industry-recognized secure practices for the type of device?

### CFG-04.13 — Radio Frequency Identification (RFID) Security

Does the organization securely govern Radio Frequency Identification (RFID) deployments to ensure RFID is used safely and securely to protect the confidentiality and integrity of data and prevent the compromise of secure spaces?

### CFG-04.14 — Contactless Access Control Systems

Does the organization securely configure contactless access control systems incorporating contactless RFID or smart cards to protect the confidentiality and integrity of data and prevent the compromise of secure spaces?

### CFG-04.15 — Thin Nodes

Does the organization configure thin nodes to have minimal functionality and information storage?

### CFG-04.16 — Video Teleconference (VTC) Security

Does the organization implement secure Video Teleconference (VTC) capabilities on endpoint devices and in designated conference rooms, to prevent potential eavesdropping?

### CFG-04.17 — Voice Over Internet Protocol (VoIP) Security

Does the organization implement secure Internet Protocol Telephony (IPT) that logically or physically separates Voice Over Internet Protocol (VoIP) traffic from data networks?

### CFG-04.18 — Disable Wireless Networking

Does the organization disable unnecessary wireless networking capabilities that are internally embedded within system components prior to issuance to end users?

### CFG-05 — Configure Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) for High-Risk Areas

Does the organization configure Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) utilized in high-risk areas with more restrictive baseline configurations?

### CFG-05.1 — Physically Disable or Remove Capabilities

Does the organization physically disable or remove unnecessary connection ports or input/output devices from technology assets at greater risk of device tampering?

### CFG-06 — Approved Configuration Deviations

Does the organization document, assess risk and approve or deny deviations to standardized configurations?

### CFG-07 — Baseline Configuration Reviews & Updates

Does the organization review and update baseline configurations:
 (1) At least annually;
 (2) When required due to so; or
 (3) As part of system component installations and upgrades?

### CFG-07.1 — Automated Baseline Configuration Management & Verification

Does the organization use automated mechanisms to govern and report on baseline configurations of Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) through Continuous Diagnostics and Mitigation (CDM), or similar technologies?

### CFG-08 — Periodic Configuration Reviews

Does the organization periodically review system configurations to identify and disable unnecessary and/or non-secure functions, ports, protocols and services?

### CFG-08.1 — Respond To Unauthorized Changes

Does the organization respond to unauthorized changes to secure baseline configurations as security incidents?

### CFG-08.2 — Integrity Assurance & Enforcement (IAE)

Does the organization use automated mechanisms to identify unauthorized deviations from an approved baseline and implement automated resiliency actions to remediate the unauthorized change?

### CFG-09 — Retention Of Previous Configurations

Does the organization retain previous versions of baseline configuration to support roll back?

### CFG-10 — Network Device Configuration File Synchronization

Does the organization configure network devices to synchronize startup and running configuration files?

### CFG-11 — Software Usage Restrictions

Does the organization enforce software usage restrictions to comply with applicable contract agreements and copyright laws?

### CFG-12 — Restrict Roles Permitted To Install Software

Does the organization configure systems to prevent the installation of software, unless the action is performed by a privileged user or service?

### CFG-12.1 — Configuration Management Role Assignment

Does the organization implement a segregation of duties for configuration management that prevents developers from performing production configuration management duties?

### CFG-13 — Open Source Software

Does the organization establish parameters for the secure use of open source software?

### CFG-14 — Prevent Unauthorized Software Execution

Does the organization configure systems to prevent the execution of unauthorized software programs?

### CFG-14.1 — Explicitly Allow / Deny Applications

Does the organization explicitly allow (allowlist / whitelist) and/or block (denylist / blacklist) applications that are authorized to execute on systems?

### CFG-15 — Unsupported Internet Browsers & Email Clients

Does the organization allow only approved Internet browsers and email clients to run on systems?

### CFG-16 — Zero-Touch Provisioning (ZTP)

Does the organization implement Zero-Touch Provisioning (ZTP), or similar technology, to automatically and securely configure devices upon being added to a network?

### CFG-17 — Production Software Repository

Does the organization maintain an authoritative repository for production software?

### CFG-17.1 — Third-Party Libraries

Does the organization restrict the use and import of third-party libraries and/or software components to trustworthy sources?

### CFG-17.2 — Software Repository Protections

Does the organization protect software repositories from importing untrusted and/or malicious software artifacts by:
(1) Scanning artifacts for malicious content;
(2) Verifying a digital signature or secure hash provided over a secure channel; and
(3) Scanning artifacts to identify plain text or encoded secrets and keys?

### CFG-17.3 — Software Development Repository

Does the organization maintain an authoritative repository for software development activities that is separate from production software?

### CFG-18 — Embedded Sensor Capability

Does the organization configure embedded sensors on systems to:
 (1) Prohibit the remote activation of sensing capabilities; and
 (2) Provide an explicit indication of sensor use to users?

### CFG-18.1 — Embedded Sensor Data Use Restrictions

Does the organization ensure data collected by embedded sensors is restricted to authorized purposes?

### CFG-18.2 — Notice of Embedded Sensor Data Collection

Does the organization notify individuals of embedded sensor data collection?

### CFG-18.3 — Embedded Sensor Data Collection Minimization

Does the organization utilize sensors that are configured to minimize the collection of information about individuals?

### CFG-18.4 — Embedded Sensor Configuration Verification

Does the organization verify embedded sensor configurations so that the delivery of collected data is restricted to authorized:
 (1) Repositories; and/or
 (2) Individuals or roles?

### CFG-19 — Refresh from Trusted Sources

Does the organization ensure that software and data needed for system component and service refreshes are obtained from trusted sources?

### CFG-20 — Hypervisor Access

Does the organization restrict access to hypervisor management functions or administrative consoles for systems hosting virtualized systems?

### CFG-21 — Restrict Access To Security Functions

Does the organization ensure security functions are restricted to authorized individuals and enforce least privilege control requirements for necessary job functions?

### CFG-22 — Host-Based Security Function Isolation

Does the organization implement underlying software separation mechanisms to facilitate security function isolation?

### CFG-23 — Control Assurance Automation (CAA) Change Control

Does the organization place Control Assurance Automation (CAA) collection code, queries and transformation logic under version control, peer review, testing and change management commensurate with the sensitivity of the Technology Assets, Applications, Services and/or Data (TAASD) accessed?

### CFG-24 — Control Assurance Automation (CAA) Unauthorized Change Detection

Does the organization detect and alert on changes to Control Assurance Automation (CAA) collection or scoring logic that could alter reported control status without corresponding, authorized change records?

### CFG-25 — Control Assurance Automation (CAA) Separation of Duties

Does the organization prevent an individual responsible for operating a control from unilaterally modifying the Control Assurance Automation (CAA) automated collection, transformation, or scoring logic used to evidence that control?

### MON-01 — Continuous Monitoring Policy

Does the organization establish a formal, documented continuous monitoring policy that:
 (1) Conveys executive management's intent;
 (2) Provides organizational direction and expected behaviors;
 (3) Is reviewed at least annually; and
 (4) Is updated, as necessary, to adapt to evolving risks, threats and other changes that affect the organization?

### MON-02 — Continuous Monitoring

Does the organization facilitate the implementation of enterprise-wide monitoring controls?

### MON-03 — Event Log & Security-Relevant Telemetry Monitoring

Does the organization review event logs on an ongoing basis and escalate incidents in accordance with established timelines and procedures?

### MON-03.1 — Centralized Management of Event Log & Security-Relevant Telemetry Content

Does the organization centrally manage and update the criteria to be captured in event logs generated by organization-defined system components?

### MON-03.2 — Analyze and Prioritize Monitoring Requirements

Does the organization assess its needs for monitoring and prioritize the monitoring of Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS), based on TAAS criticality and the sensitivity of the data it stores, transmits and processes?

### MON-03.3 — Audit Level Adjustments

Does the organization adjust the level of audit review, analysis and reporting based on evolving threat information from law enforcement, industry associations or other credible sources of threat intelligence?

### MON-04 — System Generated Event Logs & Security-Relevant Telemetry

Does the organization generate, monitor, correlate and respond to alerts from physical, cybersecurity, data protection and supply chain activities to achieve integrated situational awareness?

### MON-04.1 — System-Wide / Time-Correlated Audit Trail

Does the organization use automated mechanisms to compile audit records into an organization-wide audit trail that is time-correlated?

### MON-05 — Centralized Collection of Event Logs & Security-Relevant Telemetry

Does the organization utilize a Security Incident Event Manager (SIEM), or similar automated tool, to support the centralized collection of security-related event logs?

### MON-05.1 — Centralized Event Log & Security-Relevant Telemetry Review & Analysis

Does the organization use automated mechanisms to centrally collect, review and analyze event logs and security-relevant telemetry from multiple sources?

### MON-05.2 — Event Log & Security-Relevant Telemetry Analysis & Triage

Does the organization ensure event log reviews include analysis and triage practices that integrate with its established incident response processes?

### MON-05.3 — Event Log & Security-Relevant Telemetry Review Escalation Matrix

Does the organization make event log review processes more efficient and effective by developing and maintaining an incident response escalation matrix?

### MON-05.4 — Automated Tools for Real-Time Event Log & Security-Relevant Telemetry Analysis

Does the organization utilize a Security Incident Event Manager (SIEM), or similar automated tool, to support near real-time analysis and incident escalation?

### MON-05.5 — Automated Incident Responder Alerting

Does the organization automatically alert incident response personnel to inappropriate or anomalous activities that have potential security incident implications?

### MON-06 — Monitoring Reporting

Does the organization provide an event log report generation capability to aid in detecting and assessing anomalous activities?

### MON-06.1 — Trend Analysis Reporting

Does the organization employ trend analyses to determine if security control implementations, the frequency of continuous monitoring activities, and/or the types of activities used in the continuous monitoring process need to be modified based on empirical data?

### MON-07 — Alert Threshold Tuning

Does the organization "tune" event monitoring technologies through analyzing communications traffic/event patterns and developing profiles representing common traffic patterns and/or events?

### MON-08 — Correlate Monitoring Information

Does the organization use automated mechanisms to correlate both technical and non-technical information from across the enterprise by a Security Incident Event Manager (SIEM) or similar automated tool, to enhance organization-wide situational awareness?

### MON-08.1 — Integration of Scanning & Other Monitoring Information

Does the organization use automated mechanisms to integrate the analysis of audit records with analysis of vulnerability scanners, network performance, system monitoring and other sources to further enhance the ability to identify inappropriate or unusual activity?

### MON-08.2 — Correlation with Physical Monitoring

Does the organization use automated mechanisms to correlate information from audit records with information obtained from monitoring physical access to further enhance the ability to identify suspicious, inappropriate, unusual or malevolent activity?

### MON-09 — Content of Event Logs

Does the organization configure Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) to produce event logs that contain sufficient information to, at a minimum:
 (1) Establish what type of event occurred;
 (2) When (date and time) the event occurred;
 (3) Where the event occurred;
 (4) The source of the event;
 (5) The outcome (success or failure) of the event; and
 (6) The identity of any user/subject associated with the event?

### MON-09.1 — Audit Trails

Does the organization link system access to individual users or service accounts?

### MON-10 — Event Log & Security-Relevant Telemetry Storage Capacity

Does the organization allocate and proactively manage sufficient event log storage capacity to reduce the likelihood of such capacity being exceeded?

### MON-10.1 — Event Log & Security-Relevant Telemetry Storage Capacity Alerting

Does the organization use automated mechanisms to alert appropriate personnel when the allocated volume reaches an organization-defined percentage of maximum event log storage capacity?

### MON-11 — Time Stamps

Does the organization configure Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) to use an authoritative time source to generate time stamps for event logs?

### MON-11.1 — Synchronization With Authoritative Time Source

Does the organization synchronize internal system clocks with an authoritative time source?

### MON-12 — Protection of Event Logs & Security-Relevant Telemetry

Does the organization protect event logs and audit tools from unauthorized access, modification and deletion?

### MON-12.1 — Event Log & Security-Relevant Telemetry Backup on Separate Physical Systems / Components

Does the organization back up event logs onto a physically different system or system component than the Security Incident Event Manager (SIEM) or similar automated tool?

### MON-12.2 — Event Log & Security-Relevant Telemetry Access by Subset of Privileged Users

Does the organization restrict access to the management of event logs to privileged users with a specific business need?

### MON-12.3 — Cryptographic Protection of Event Logs & Security-Relevant Telemetry

Are cryptographic mechanisms utilized to protect the integrity of event logs and audit tools?

### MON-12.4 — Dual Authorization for Event Log & Security-Relevant Telemetry Movement

Does the organization use automated mechanisms to enforce dual authorization for the movement or deletion of event logs?

### MON-12.5 — Write Once Read Many (WORM) Event Log Generation

Does the organization produce event logs on hardware-enforced, write-once media (e.g., Write Once Read Many (WORM) technologies)?

### MON-13 — Event Log & Security-Relevant Telemetry Retention

Does the organization retain event logs for a time period consistent with records retention requirements to provide support for after-the-fact investigations of security incidents and to meet statutory, regulatory and contractual retention requirements?

### MON-14 — Privileged Functions Logging

Does the organization log and review the actions of users and/or services with elevated privileges?

### MON-14.1 — Account Creation and Modification Logging

Does the organization use automated mechanisms to generate event logs for permissions changes to privileged accounts and/or groups?

### MON-14.2 — Privileged User Oversight

Does the organization implement enhanced activity monitoring for privileged users?

### MON-15 — Inventory of Technology Asset Event Logging

Does the organization maintain a current and accurate inventory of technology-related Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) being logged?

### MON-16 — Anomalous Behavior

Does the organization utilize User & Entity Behavior Analytics (UEBA) and/or User Activity Monitoring (UAM) solutions to detect and respond to anomalous behavior that could indicate account compromise or other malicious activities?

### MON-16.1 — Unusual Transactions

Does the organization establish organization-defined "normal business activities" to identify anomalous transaction activities that can reduce the opportunity for sending (outbound) and/or receiving (inbound) fraudulent actions?

### MON-17 — Monitoring for Indicators of Compromise (IOC)

Does the organization use automated mechanisms to identify and alert on Indicators of Compromise (IoC)?

### MON-17.1 — Deactivated Account Activity

Does the organization monitor deactivated accounts for attempted usage?

### MON-17.2 — Automated Response to Suspicious Events

Does the organization use automated mechanisms to implement pre-determined corrective actions in response to detected events that have security incident implications?

### MON-17.3 — Insider Threats

Does the organization monitor internal personnel activity for potential security incidents?

### MON-17.4 — Third-Party Threats

Does the organization monitor third-party personnel activity for potential security incidents?

### MON-18 — Individuals Posing Greater Risk

Does the organization implement enhanced activity monitoring for individuals who have been identified as posing an increased level of risk?

### MON-18.1 — Session Audit

Does the organization provide session audit capabilities that can:
 (1) Capture and log all content related to a user session; and
 (2) Remotely view all content related to an established user session in real time?

### MON-18.2 — Real-Time Session Monitoring

Does the organization enable authorized personnel the ability to remotely view and hear content related to an established user session in real time, in accordance with organizational standards, as well as statutory, regulatory and contractual obligations?

### MON-19 — Monitoring For Information Disclosure

Does the organization monitor for evidence of unauthorized exfiltration or disclosure of non-public information?

### MON-19.1 — Monitoring for Third-Party Information Disclosure

Does the organization monitor for evidence of unauthorized exfiltration or disclosure of organizational information?

### MON-20 — Covert Channel Analysis

Does the organization conduct covert channel analysis to identify aspects of communications that are potential avenues for covert channels?

### MON-20.1 — Analyze Traffic for Covert Exfiltration

Does the organization use automated mechanisms to analyze network traffic to detect covert data exfiltration?

### MON-21 — Unauthorized Activities

Does the organization monitor for unauthorized activities, accounts, connections, devices and software?

### MON-21.1 — Unauthorized Network Services

Does the organization use automated mechanisms to detect unauthorized network services and alert incident response personnel?

### MON-22 — Inbound & Outbound Communications Traffic

Does the organization continuously monitor inbound and outbound communications traffic for unusual or unauthorized activities or conditions?

### MON-22.1 — Proxy Logging

Does the organization log all Internet-bound requests, in order to identify prohibited activities and assist incident handlers with identifying potentially compromised systems?

### MON-23 — Network Intrusion Detection & Prevention Systems (NIDS & NIPS) Monitoring

Does the organization implement Intrusion Detection / Prevention Systems (IDS / IPS) technologies on critical systems, key network segments and network choke points?

### MON-24 — Host Intrusion Detection & Prevention Systems (HIDS & HIPS) Monitoring

Does the organization monitor Host Intrusion Detection / Prevention Systems (HIDS / HIPS) to actively alert on or block unwanted activities?

### MON-25 — De-Militarized Zone (DMZ) Monitoring

Does the organization monitor De-Militarized Zone (DMZ) network segments to separate untrusted networks from trusted networks?

### MON-26 — Wireless Network Monitoring

Does the organization monitor wireless network segments for:
(1) Rogue wireless devices; and
(2) Anomalous and/or hostile activities?

### MON-27 — File Integrity Monitoring (FIM)

Does the organization utilize a File Integrity Monitor (FIM), or similar change-detection technology, on critical Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) to generate alerts for unauthorized modifications?

### MON-28 — File Activity Monitoring (FAM)

Does the organization use automated mechanisms to monitor sensitive and/or regulated data in Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) and data repositories?

### MON-29 — Permitted Monitoring Actions

Does the organization specify the permitted actions for both users and Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) associated with the review, analysis and reporting of audit information?

### MON-29.1 — Changes by Authorized Individuals

Does the organization provide privileged users or roles the capability to change the auditing to be performed on specified system components, based on specific event criteria within specified time thresholds?

### MON-29.2 — Query Parameter Audits of Personal Data (PD)

Does the organization provide and implement the capability for auditing the parameters of user query events for data sets containing Personal Data (PD)?

### MON-30 — Sensitive Event Log & Security-Relevant Telemetry Data

Does the organization protect sensitive and/or regulated data contained in event logs and security-relevant telemetry?

### MON-30.1 — Limit Personal Data (PD) In Event Logs & Security-Relevant Telemetry

Does the organization limit Personal Data (PD) contained in event logs and security-relevant telemetry to the elements identified in the Data Privacy Risk Assessment (DPRA)?

### MON-31 — Verbosity Logging for Boundary Devices

Does the organization verbosely log all traffic (both allowed and blocked) arriving at network boundary devices, including firewalls, Intrusion Detection / Prevention Systems (IDS/IPS) and inbound and outbound proxies?

### MON-32 — Database Logging

Does the organization ensure databases produce audit records that contain sufficient information to monitor database activities?

### MON-33 — Response To Event Log Processing Failures

Does the organization alert appropriate personnel in the event of a log processing failure and take actions to remedy the disruption?

### MON-33.1 — Real-Time Alerts of Event Logging Failure

Does the organization provide 24x7x365 near real-time alerting capability when an event log processing failure occurs?

### MON-34 — Non-Repudiation

Does the organization utilize a non-repudiation capability to protect against an individual falsely denying having performed a particular action?

### MON-34.1 — Identity Binding

Does the organization bind the identity of the information producer to the information generated?

### MON-35 — Alternate Event Logging Capability

Does the organization provide an alternate event logging capability in the event of a failure in primary audit capability?

### MON-36 — Sharing of Event Logs & Security-Relevant Telemetry

Does the organization share event logs with third-party organizations based on specific cross-organizational sharing agreements?

### MON-36.1 — Cross-Organizational Monitoring

Does the organization coordinate sanitized event logs among external organizations to identify anomalous events when event logs are shared across organizational boundaries, without giving away sensitive or critical business data?

### MON-37 — Control Assurance Automation (CAA) Data Feed Identification

Does the organization reconcile authorized Control Assurance Automation (CAA) collection activities so that legitimate collection is known and distinguishable from unauthorized data exfiltration?

### CRY-01 — Cryptographic Protections Policy

Does the organization establish a formal, documented cryptographic protections policy that:
 (1) Conveys executive management's intent;
 (2) Provides organizational direction and expected behaviors;
 (3) Is reviewed at least annually; and
 (4) Is updated, as necessary, to adapt to evolving risks, threats and other changes that affect the organization?

### CRY-02 — Use of Cryptographic Controls

Does the organization facilitate the implementation of cryptographic protections controls using known public standards and trusted cryptographic technologies?

### CRY-03 — Cryptographic Management

Does the organization govern assets involved in providing cryptographic protections according to its configuration management processes?

### CRY-03.1 — Alternate Physical Protection

Are cryptographic mechanisms utilized to prevent unauthorized disclosure of information as an alternative to physical safeguards?

### CRY-03.2 — Pre/Post Transmission Handling

Are cryptographic mechanisms utilized to ensure the confidentiality and integrity of information during preparation for transmission and during reception?

### CRY-04 — Cryptographic Cipher Suites and Protocols Inventory

Does the organization identify, document and review deployed cryptographic cipher suites and protocols to proactively respond to industry trends regarding the continued viability of utilized cryptographic cipher suites and protocols?

### CRY-05 — Encrypting Data In Transit

Are cryptographic mechanisms utilized to prevent the unauthorized disclosure of data in transit?

### CRY-06 — Integrity of Data In Transit

Are cryptographic mechanisms utilized to detect unauthorized changes to data in transit?

### CRY-07 — Encrypting Data At Rest

Are cryptographic mechanisms utilized to prevent unauthorized disclosure of data at rest?

### CRY-07.1 — Encrypting Storage Media

Are cryptographic mechanisms utilized to protect the confidentiality and integrity of sensitive and/or regulated data residing on storage media?

### CRY-07.2 — Encrypting Offline Storage

Does the organization remove unused data from online storage and archive it off-line in a secure location until it can be disposed of according to data retention requirements?

### CRY-08 — Database Encryption

Does the organization ensure that database servers utilize encryption to protect the confidentiality of the data within the databases?

### CRY-09 — Public Key Infrastructure (PKI)

Does the organization securely implement an internal Public Key Infrastructure (PKI) infrastructure or obtain PKI services from a reputable PKI service provider?

### CRY-09.1 — Public Key Infrastructure (PKI) Availability

Does the organization ensure the availability of data in the event of the loss of cryptographic keys?

### CRY-10 — Cryptographic Key Management

Does the organization facilitate cryptographic key management controls to protect the confidentiality, integrity and availability of keys?

### CRY-10.1 — Symmetric Keys

Does the organization facilitate the production and management of symmetric cryptographic keys using Federal Information Processing Standards (FIPS)-compliant key management technology and processes?

### CRY-10.2 — Asymmetric Keys

Does the organization facilitate the production and management of asymmetric cryptographic keys using Federal Information Processing Standards (FIPS)-compliant key management technology and processes that protect the user's private key?

### CRY-10.3 — Cryptographic Key Loss or Change

Does the organization ensure the availability of information in the event of the loss of cryptographic keys by individual users?

### CRY-10.4 — Control & Distribution of Cryptographic Keys

Does the organization facilitate the secure distribution of symmetric and asymmetric cryptographic keys using industry recognized key management technology and processes?

### CRY-10.5 — Assigned Cryptographic Key Owners

Does the organization ensure cryptographic keys are bound to individual identities?

### CRY-10.6 — Third-Party Cryptographic Keys

Does the organization ensure customers are provided with appropriate key management guidance whenever cryptographic keys are shared?

### CRY-10.7 — External System Cryptographic Key Control

Does the organization maintain control of cryptographic keys for encrypted material stored or transmitted through an external system?

### CRY-11 — Transmission of Cybersecurity & Data Protection Attributes

Does the organization associate Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) security attributes with information exchanged between TAAS?

### CRY-12 — Certificate Authorities

Does the organization use automated mechanisms to enable the use of organization-defined Certificate Authorities (CAs) to facilitate the establishment of protected sessions?

### CRY-13 — Certificate Monitoring

Does the organization use automated mechanisms to discover when new certificates are issued for organization-controlled domains?

### CRY-14 — Cryptographic Hash

Does the organization utilize hash algorithms to generate a hash value that can be used to validate the integrity of data and/or software?

### CRY-15 — Export-Controlled Cryptography

Does the organization address the exporting of cryptographic technologies in compliance with relevant statutory and regulatory requirements?

### DCH-01 — Data Classification & Handling Policy

Does the organization establish a formal, documented data classification and handling policy that:
 (1) Conveys executive management's intent;
 (2) Provides organizational direction and expected behaviors;
 (3) Is reviewed at least annually; and
 (4) Is updated, as necessary, to adapt to evolving risks, threats and other changes that affect the organization?

### DCH-02 — Data Protection

Does the organization facilitate the implementation of data protection controls?

### DCH-03 — Sensitive / Regulated Data Governance

Does the organization facilitate data governance to oversee its policies, standards and procedures so that sensitive and/or regulated data is effectively managed and maintained in accordance with applicable statutory, regulatory and contractual obligations?

### DCH-03.1 — Data Catalog

Does the organization identify and catalog the organization's data holdings in a structured format to document each sensitive and/or regulated data asset?

### DCH-04 — Data & Asset Classification

Does the organization ensure data and assets are categorized in accordance with applicable statutory, regulatory and contractual requirements?

### DCH-04.1 — Highest Classification Level

Does the organization ensure that Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) are classified according to the highest level of data sensitivity that is stored, transmitted and/or processed?

### DCH-04.2 — Data Reclassification

Does the organization reclassify data, including associated Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS), commensurate with the security category and/or classification level of the information?

### DCH-05 — Sensitive Data Inventories

Does the organization maintain inventory logs of all sensitive media and conduct sensitive media inventories at least annually?

### DCH-05.1 — Periodic Scans for Sensitive / Regulated Data

Does the organization periodically scan unstructured data sources for sensitive and/or regulated data or data requiring special protection measures by statutory, regulatory or contractual obligations?

### DCH-06 — Data Stewardship

Does the organization ensure data stewardship is assigned, documented and communicated?

### DCH-06.1 — Defining Access Authorizations for Sensitive / Regulated Data

Does the organization explicitly define authorizations for specific individuals and/or roles for logical and /or physical access to sensitive and/or regulated data?

### DCH-07 — Sensitive / Regulated Data Protection

Does the organization protect sensitive and/or regulated data wherever it is processed and/or stored?

### DCH-07.1 — Restrict Sensitive / Regulated Data Access To Authorized Individuals

Does the organization control and restrict access to sensitive and/or regulated data on digital and non-digital media formats to authorized individuals?

### DCH-08 — Limitations on Use & Distribution of Sensitive / Regulated Data

Does the organization restrict the use and distribution of sensitive and/or regulated data?

### DCH-08.1 — Sensitive / Regulated Data Sharing Decisions

Does the organization utilize a process to assist users in making information sharing decisions to ensure data is appropriately protected?

### DCH-08.2 — Disclosure of Sensitive / Regulated Data

Does the organization restrict the disclosure of sensitive and/or regulated data to authorized parties with a need to know?

### DCH-08.3 — Controlled Release of Sensitive / Regulated Data

Does the organization use automated mechanisms to validate cybersecurity and data protection attributes prior to releasing information to external Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS)?

### DCH-08.4 — Sensitive / Regulated Data Release Sanitization

Does the organization remove Personal Data (PD) elements from a dataset prior to its release if those elements in the dataset do not need to be part of the data release?

### DCH-09 — Sensitive / Regulated Data Access Mapping

Does the organization leverage data-specific Access Control Lists (ACL) or Interconnection Security Agreements (ISAs) to generate a logical map of the parties with whom sensitive and/or regulated data is shared?

### DCH-10 — Sensitive / Regulated Media Records

Does the organization ensure media records for sensitive and/or regulated data contain sufficient information to determine the potential impact in the event of a data loss incident?

### DCH-11 — Media Marking

Does the organization mark media in accordance with data protection requirements so that personnel are alerted to distribution limitations, handling caveats and applicable security requirements?

### DCH-11.1 — Automated Marking

Does the organization use automated mechanisms to mark physical media and digital files to indicate the distribution limitations, handling requirements and applicable security markings (if any) of the information to aid Data Loss Prevention (DLP) technologies?

### DCH-12 — Masking Displayed Sensitive / Regulated Data

Does the organization apply data masking to sensitive and/or regulated information that is displayed or printed?

### DCH-12.1 — Making Sensitive / Regulated Data Unreadable In Storage

Does the organization ensure sensitive and/or regulated data is rendered human unreadable anywhere sensitive and/or regulated data is stored?

### DCH-13 — Media Storage

Does the organization:
(1) Physically control and securely store digital and non-digital media within controlled areas using organization-defined security measures; and
(2) Protect system media until the media are destroyed or sanitized using approved equipment, techniques and procedures?

### DCH-13.1 — Data Storage Location Reviews

Does the organization perform periodic security reviews of storage locations that contain sensitive and/or regulated data?

### DCH-14 — Physically Secure All Media Containing Sensitive / Regulated Data

Does the organization physically secure all media that contains sensitive and/or regulated data?

### DCH-15 — Storing Authentication Data

Does the organization prohibit the storage of sensitive transaction authentication data after authorization?

### DCH-16 — Media Transportation

Does the organization protect and control digital and non-digital media during transport outside of controlled areas using appropriate security measures?

### DCH-16.1 — Media Transportation Custodians

Does the organization identify custodians throughout the transport of digital or non-digital media?

### DCH-16.2 — Encrypting Data Outside of Controlled Areas

Are cryptographic mechanisms utilized to protect the confidentiality and integrity of information stored on digital media during transport outside of controlled areas?

### DCH-17 — Digital & Non-Digital Media Disposal

Does the organization securely dispose of, destroy and/or erase digital and non-digital media when it is no longer required, using organization-defined procedures?

### DCH-17.1 — Dual Authorization for Sensitive / Regulated Data Destruction

Does the organization enforce dual authorization for the destruction, disposal or sanitization of digital media that contains sensitive and/or regulated data?

### DCH-18 — Digital Media Sanitization

Does the organization sanitize system media with the strength and integrity commensurate with the classification or sensitivity of the information prior to disposal, release out of organizational control or release for reuse?

### DCH-18.1 — Sanitization of Sensitive / Regulated Data

Does the organization facilitate the sanitization of sensitive and/or regulated data?

### DCH-18.2 — Digital Media Sanitization Documentation

Does the organization supervise, track, document and verify system media sanitization and disposal actions?

### DCH-18.3 — Digital Media Sanitization Equipment Testing

Does the organization test sanitization equipment and procedures to verify that the intended result is achieved?

### DCH-18.4 — First Time Use Sanitization

Does the organization apply nondestructive sanitization techniques to portable storage devices prior to first use?

### DCH-19 — Digital Media Use Restrictions

Does the organization restrict the use of types of digital media on systems or system components?

### DCH-20 — Portable Storage Devices

Does the organization restrict or prohibit the use of portable storage devices by users on external systems?

### DCH-20.1 — Prohibit Portable Storage Devices Use Without Owner

Does the organization prohibit the use of portable storage devices in organizational systems when such devices have no identifiable owner?

### DCH-21 — Removable Media Security

Does the organization restrict removable media in accordance with data handling and acceptable usage parameters?

### DCH-22 — Use of External Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS)

Does the organization govern how external parties, including Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS), are used to securely store, process and transmit data?

### DCH-22.1 — Limits of Authorized Use To Process, Store and/or Transmit Data

Does the organization prohibit external parties, including Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS), from storing, processing and transmitting data unless authorized individuals first:
(1) Verifying the implementation of required security, compliance and/or resilience controls; or
(2) Retaining a processing agreement with the entity hosting the external TAAS?

### DCH-22.2 — Protecting Sensitive / Regulated Data on External Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS)

Does the organization ensure that the requirements for the protection of sensitive and/or regulated data processed, stored or transmitted on external Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS), are implemented in accordance with applicable statutory, regulatory and contractual obligations?

### DCH-22.3 — Non-Organizationally Owned Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS)

Does the organization restrict the use of non-organizationally owned Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) to process, store or transmit organizational information?

### DCH-23 — Information Search & Retrieval

Does the organization ensure Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) implement data search and retrieval functions that properly enforce data protection / sharing restrictions?

### DCH-23.1 — Electronic Discovery (eDiscovery)

Does the organization utilize electronic discovery (eDiscovery) that covers current and archived communication transactions?

### DCH-24 — Publicly Accessible Content

Does the organization control publicly-accessible content?

### DCH-24.1 — Data Mining Protection

Does the organization protect data storage objects against unauthorized data mining and data harvesting techniques?

### DCH-25 — Ad-Hoc Transfers

Does the organization secure ad-hoc exchanges of large digital files with internal or external parties?

### DCH-26 — Transfer Authorizations

Does the organization verify that individuals or Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) transferring data between interconnecting TAAS have the requisite authorizations (e.g., write permissions or privileges) prior to transferring said data?

### DCH-27 — Media & Data Retention

Does the organization retain media and data in accordance with applicable statutory, regulatory and contractual obligations?

### DCH-27.1 — Minimize Sensitive / Regulated Data Exposure

Does the organization minimize sensitive and/or regulated data that is collected, received, processed, stored and/or transmitted throughout the information lifecycle to only those elements necessary to support necessary business processes?

### DCH-27.2 — Archived Data Set Retention

Does the organization protect archived data in accordance with applicable statutory, regulatory and contractual obligations?

### DCH-27.3 — Archiving Sensitive / Regulated Data

Does the organization refrain from archiving Personal Data (PD) elements if those elements in a dataset will not be needed after the dataset is archived?

### DCH-27.4 — Mobile Device Data Retention Limitations

Does the organization limit data retention on mobile devices to the smallest usable dataset and timeframe?

### DCH-28 — Limit Sensitive / Regulated Data In Testing, Training & Research

Does the organization minimize the use of sensitive and/or regulated data for research, testing, or training, in accordance with authorized, legitimate business practices?

### DCH-29 — Logical Data Location

Does the organization identify and document the logical location of data and the specific Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) on which the data resides?

### DCH-29.1 — Automated Tools to Support Logical Data Location

Does the organization use automated mechanisms to identify by data classification type to ensure adequate security, compliance and resilience controls are in place to protect organizational information and individual data protection?

### DCH-30 — Geographic Data Location

Does the organization inventory, document and maintain data flows for data that is resident (permanently or temporarily) within geographically distributed Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) (physical and virtual)?

### DCH-30.1 — Geolocation Requirements for Processing, Storage and Service Locations

Does the organization control the location of cloud processing/storage based on business requirements that includes statutory, regulatory and contractual obligations?

### DCH-31 — Data Localization

Does the organization constrain the impact of "digital sovereignty laws," that require localized data within the host country, where data and processes may be subjected to arbitrary enforcement actions that potentially violate other applicable statutory, regulatory and/or contractual obligations?

### DCH-32 — External Transfer of Sensitive / Regulated Data

Does the organization restrict and govern the transfer of sensitive and/or regulated data:
 (1) Cross-border; and/or
 (2) Interorganizational?

### DCH-33 — Data Quality Operations

Does the organization check for Redundant, Obsolete/Outdated, Toxic or Trivial (ROTT) data to ensure the accuracy, relevance, timeliness, impact, completeness and de-identification of information throughout the information lifecycle?

### DCH-33.1 — Data Management Board

Does the organization establish a written charter for a Data Management Board (DMB) and assigned organization-defined roles to the DMB?

### DCH-33.2 — Data Quality Management

Does the organization manage the quality, utility, objectivity, integrity and impact determination and de-identification of sensitive and/or regulated data across the information lifecycle?

### DCH-33.3 — Data Quality Automation

Does the organization use automated mechanisms to support the evaluation of data quality across the information lifecycle?

### DCH-34 — Data Modeling Guidelines

Does the organization issue data modeling guidelines to support tagging of sensitive and/or regulated data?

### DCH-34.1 — Data Tags

Does the organization utilize data tags to automate tracking of sensitive and/or regulated data across the information lifecycle?

### DCH-35 — Data Analytics Bias

Does the organization evaluate its analytical processes for potential bias?

### DCH-36 — De-Identification (Anonymization)

Does the organization de-identify sensitive and/or regulated data through
 (1) Anonymization;
 (2) De-identification;
 (3) Pseudonymization; and/or
 (4) Redaction?

### DCH-36.1 — Automated De-Identification of Sensitive / Regulated Data

Does the organization perform de-identification of sensitive and/or regulated data, using validated algorithms and software to implement the algorithms?

### DCH-36.2 — De-Identify Dataset Upon Collection

Does the organization de-identify the dataset upon collection by not collecting sensitive and/or regulated data?

### DCH-36.3 — Removal, Masking, Encryption, Hashing or Replacement of Direct Identifiers

Does the organization remove, mask, encrypt, hash or replace direct identifiers in a dataset?

### DCH-36.4 — Statistical Disclosure Control

Does the organization manipulate numerical data, contingency tables and statistical findings so that no person or organization is identifiable in the results of the analysis?

### DCH-36.5 — Motivated Intruder

Does the organization perform a motivated intruder test on the de-identified dataset to determine if the identified data remains or if the de-identified data can be re-identified?

### DCH-36.6 — Differential Privacy

Does the organization implement differential privacy to prevent the disclosure of Personal Data (PD) by adding non-deterministic noise to analysis results using:
 (1) A defined privacy loss parameter;
 (2) Noise calibrated to query sensitivity; and
 (3) Accounting for cumulative privacy loss across queries?

### DCH-37 — Cybersecurity & Data Protection Attributes

Does the organization bind cybersecurity and data protection attributes to information as it is stored, transmitted and processed?

### DCH-37.1 — Dynamic Attribute Association

Does the organization dynamically associate cybersecurity and data protection attributes with individuals and objects as information is created, combined, or transformed, in accordance with organization-defined cybersecurity and data protection policies?

### DCH-37.2 — Attribute Value Changes By Authorized Individuals

Does the organization provide authorized individuals (or processes acting on behalf of individuals) the capability to define or change the value of associated cybersecurity and data protection attributes?

### DCH-37.3 — Maintenance of Attribute Associations By System

Does the organization maintain the association and integrity of cybersecurity and data protection attributes to individuals and objects?

### DCH-37.4 — Association of Attributes By Authorized Individuals

Does the organization provide the capability to associate cybersecurity and data protection attributes with individuals and objects by authorized individuals (or processes acting on behalf of individuals)?

### DCH-37.5 — Attribute Displays for Output Devices

Does the organization display cybersecurity and data protection attributes in human-readable form on each object that the system transmits to output devices to identify special dissemination, handling or distribution instructions using human-readable, standard naming conventions?

### DCH-37.6 — Data Subject Attribute Associations

Does the organization require personnel to associate and maintain the association of cybersecurity and data protection attributes with individuals and objects in accordance with cybersecurity and data protection policies?

### DCH-37.7 — Consistent Attribute Interpretation

Does the organization provide a consistent, organizationally agreed upon interpretation of cybersecurity and data protection attributes employed in access enforcement and flow enforcement decisions between distributed system components?

### DCH-37.8 — Identity Association Techniques & Technologies

Does the organization associate cybersecurity and data protection attributes to information?

### DCH-37.9 — Attribute Reassignment

Does the organization reclassify data as required, due to changing business/technical requirements?

### DCH-37.10 — Attribute Configuration By Authorized Individuals

Does the organization provide authorized individuals the capability to define or change the type and value of cybersecurity and data protection attributes available for association with subjects and objects?

### DCH-37.11 — Audit Changes

Does the organization audit changes to cybersecurity and data protection attributes and responds to events in accordance with incident response procedures?

### DCH-38 — Code Names

Does the organization use aliases to name assets, which are mission-critical and/or contain highly-sensitive and/or regulated data, are unique and not readily associated with a product, project or type of data?

### DCH-39 — Data Rights Management (DRM)

Does the organization utilize Data Rights Management (DRM), or similar technologies, to protect Intellectual Property (IP) rights by preventing the unauthorized distribution and/or modification of sensitive IP?

### DCH-40 — Data Loss Prevention (DLP)

Does the organization use automated mechanisms to implement Data Loss Prevention (DLP) to protect sensitive information as it is stored, transmitted and processed?

### DCH-41 — Control Assurance Automation (CAA) Aggregated Telemetry

Does the organization classify and protect aggregated Control Assurance Automation (CAA) telemetry commensurate with the elevated sensitivity that aggregation can create?

### EMB-01 — Embedded Technology Policy

Does the organization establish a formal, documented embedded technology policy that:
 (1) Conveys executive management's intent;
 (2) Provides organizational direction and expected behaviors;
 (3) Is reviewed at least annually; and
 (4) Is updated, as necessary, to adapt to evolving risks, threats and other changes that affect the organization?

### EMB-02 — Embedded Technology Security Program

Does the organization facilitate the implementation of embedded technology controls?

### EMB-03 — Separate Operating Environments For Embedded Technologies

Does the organization logically or physically separate embedded technologies from organizational Information Technology (IT) networks?

### EMB-04 — Embedded Technology Inventory Management

Does the organization augment organizational IT Asset Management (ITAM) processes for Operational Technology (OT) and Internet of Things (IoT) devices with:
 (1) Passive network monitoring; and
 (2) Periodic physical inspections?

### EMB-05 — Internet of Things (IOT)

Does the organization proactively manage the security, compliance and resilience risks associated with Internet of Things (IoT)?

### EMB-06 — Operational Technology (OT)

Does the organization proactively manage the security, compliance and resilience risks associated with Operational Technology (OT)?

### EMB-07 — Interface Security

Does the organization protect embedded devices against unauthorized use of the physical factory diagnostic and test interface(s)?

### EMB-08 — Embedded Technology Configuration Monitoring

Does the organization generate log entries on embedded devices when configuration changes or attempts to access interfaces are detected?

### EMB-09 — Prevent Alterations

Does the organization protect embedded devices by preventing the unauthorized installation and execution of software?

### EMB-10 — Embedded Technology Maintenance

Does the organization securely update software and upgrade functionality on embedded devices?

### EMB-11 — Resilience To Outages

Does the organization configure embedded technology to be resilient to data network and power outages?

### EMB-12 — Power Level Monitoring

Does the organization use automated mechanisms to monitor the power levels of embedded technologies for decreased or excessive power usage, including battery drainage, to investigate for device tampering?

### EMB-13 — Embedded Technology Reviews

Does the organization perform evaluations of deployed embedded technologies as needed, or at least on an annual basis, to ensure that necessary updates to mitigate the risks associated with legacy embedded technologies are identified and implemented?

### EMB-14 — Message Queuing Telemetry Transport (MQTT) Security

Does the organization enforce the security of Message Queuing Telemetry Transport (MQTT) traffic?

### EMB-15 — Remote Management of Embedded Technologies

Does the organization restrict remote management of embedded technologies by:
 (1) Allowing access only when needed;
 (2) Eliminating "always on" connections; and
 (3) Requiring strong authentication?

### EMB-16 — Restrict Communications

Does the organization require embedded technologies to initiate all communications and drop new, incoming communications?

### EMB-17 — Authorized Communications

Does the organization restrict embedded technologies to communicate only with authorized peers and service endpoints?

### EMB-18 — Operating Environment Certification

Does the organization determine if embedded technologies are certified for secure use in the proposed operating environment?

### EMB-19 — Safety Assessment

Does the organization evaluate the safety aspects of embedded technologies via a fault tree analysis, or similar method, to determine possible consequences of misuse, misconfiguration and/or failure?

### EMB-20 — Certificate-Based Authentication

Does the organization enforce certificate-based authentication for embedded technologies (e.g., IoT and OT) and their supporting services?

### EMB-21 — Chip-To-Cloud Security

Does the organization implement embedded technologies that utilize pre-provisioned cloud trust anchors to support secure bootstrap and Zero Touch Provisioning (ZTP)?

### EMB-22 — Real-Time Operating System (RTOS) Security

Does the organization ensure embedded technologies utilize a securely configured Real-Time Operating System (RTOS)?

### EMB-23 — Safe Operations

Does the organization continuously validate autonomous systems that trigger an automatic state change when safe operation is no longer assured?

### EMB-24 — Proximity Sensor
