Does the organization use automated mechanisms to monitor physical proximity to robotic or autonomous platforms to reduce applied force or stop the operation when sensors indicate a potentially dangerous scenario?

### EMB-25 — Safety Instrumented System (SIS)

Does the organization use automated mechanisms to monitor and control hazardous processes to reduce the potential negative consequences of hazardous events?

### EMB-26 — Safety Instrumented Function (SIF)

Does the organization use automated mechanisms within a Safety Instrumented System (SIS) to execute predetermined actions upon detection of a potentially hazardous event?

### EMB-27 — Safety Integrity Level (SIL)

Does the organization assign a Safety Integrity Level (SIL) that measures the performance and reliability with which a Safety Instrumented Function (SIF) reduces risk?

### END-01 — Endpoint Security Policy

Does the organization establish a formal, documented endpoint security policy that:
 (1) Conveys executive management's intent;
 (2) Provides organizational direction and expected behaviors;
 (3) Is reviewed at least annually; and
 (4) Is updated, as necessary, to adapt to evolving risks, threats and other changes that affect the organization?

### END-02 — Endpoint Device Management (EDM)

Does the organization facilitate the implementation of Endpoint Device Management (EDM) controls?

### END-03 — Endpoint Protection Mechanisms

Does the organization protect the confidentiality, integrity, availability and safety of endpoint devices?

### END-03.1 — Centralized Management of Endpoint Protection Mechanisms

Does the organization centrally-manage endpoint protection-related Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS)?

### END-03.2 — Automatic Endpoint Protection Mechanism Updates

Does the organization use automated mechanisms to update endpoint protection-related Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) when new releases are available, in accordance with organization-defined configuration and change management practices?

### END-03.3 — Evolving Endpoint Protection Threats

Does the organization perform periodic evaluations evolving malware threats to assess systems that are generally not considered to be commonly affected by malicious software?

### END-03.4 — Binary or Machine-Executable Code

Does the organization prohibit the use of binary or machine-executable code from sources with limited or no warranty and without access to source code?

### END-04 — Malicious Code Protection (Antimalware)

Does the organization utilize antimalware technologies to detect and eradicate malicious code?

### END-04.1 — Always On Antimalware Protection

Does the organization ensure that anti-malware technologies are continuously running in real-time and cannot be disabled or altered by non-privileged users, unless specifically authorized by management on a case-by-case basis for a limited time period?

### END-04.2 — Heuristic / Nonsignature-Based Malware Detection

Does the organization utilize heuristic / nonsignature-based antimalware detection capabilities?

### END-05 — Antimalware Protection Mechanism Testing

Does the organization test antimalware technologies by introducing a known benign, non-spreading test case into the system and subsequently verifying that both detection of the test case and associated incident reporting occurs?

### END-06 — Documented Endpoint Security Protection Measures

Does the organization document endpoint protection-related Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS)?

### END-07 — Software Firewall

Does the organization utilize host-based firewall software, or a similar technology, on all endpoint devices, where technically feasible?

### END-08 — Unified Endpoint Device Management (UEDM)

Does the organization utilize a centralized Unified Endpoint Device Management (UEDM) solution that provides agent and/or agentless management of endpoint devices regardless of device location?

### END-09 — Endpoint Detection & Response (EDR)

Does the organization utilize Endpoint Detection & Response (EDR) capabilities to detect, investigate and respond to anomalous and/or malicious activity?

### END-10 — Extended Detection & Response (XDR)

Does the organization implement Extended Detection & Response (XDR) technologies to correlate data and respond to threats across multiple security layers, including:
(1) Endpoints;
(2) On-premises networks;
(3) Cloud-based networks;
(4) Electronic communications;
(5) Applications; and
(6) Services?

### END-11 — Endpoint File Integrity Monitoring (FIM)

Does the organization utilize File Integrity Monitor (FIM), or similar technologies, to detect and report on unauthorized changes to selected files and configuration settings?

### END-11.1 — Endpoint Integrity Checks

Does the organization validate configurations through integrity checking of software and firmware?

### END-11.2 — Automated Notifications of Integrity Violations

Does the organization use automated mechanisms to alert incident response personnel upon discovering discrepancies during integrity verification?

### END-11.3 — Automated Response to Integrity Violations

Does the organization use automated mechanisms to implement remediation actions when integrity violations are discovered?

### END-11.4 — Boot Process Integrity

Does the organization use automated mechanisms to verify the integrity of the boot process of systems?

### END-11.5 — Protection of Boot Firmware

Does the organization use automated mechanisms to protect the integrity of boot firmware in systems?

### END-12 — Host Intrusion Detection and Prevention Systems (HIDS / HIPS)

Does the organization utilize Host-based Intrusion Detection / Prevention Systems (HIDS / HIPS), or similar technologies, to monitor for and protect against anomalous host activity, including lateral movement across the network?

### END-13 — Mobile Code

Does the organization address mobile code / operating system-independent applications?

### END-14 — Collaborative Computing Devices

Does the organization unplug or prohibit the remote activation of collaborative computing devices with the following exceptions:
 (1) Networked whiteboards;
 (2) Video teleconference cameras; and
 (3) Teleconference microphones?

### END-14.1 — Collaborative Computing Capability Disabling / Removal In Secure Work Areas

Does the organization disable or remove collaborative computing devices from critical systems and secure work areas?

### END-14.2 — Explicitly Indicate Current Participants

Does the organization use automated mechanisms to provide an explicit indication of current participants in online meetings and teleconferences?

### END-14.3 — Participant Identity Verification

Does the organization verify individual identities to ensure that access to virtual meetings is limited to appropriate individuals?

### END-14.4 — Participant Connection Management

Does the organization ensure the meeting host can positively control an individual's participation in virtual meetings?

### END-14.5 — Malicious Link & File Protections

Does the organization use automated mechanisms to detect malicious links and/or files in communications and prevent users from accessing those malicious links and/or files?

### END-14.6 — Explicit Indication Of Use

Does the organization configure collaborative computing devices to provide physically-present individuals with an explicit indication of use?

### HRS-01 — Human Resources Security Policy

Does the organization establish a formal, documented human resources security policy that:
 (1) Conveys executive management's intent;
 (2) Provides organizational direction and expected behaviors;
 (3) Is reviewed at least annually; and
 (4) Is updated, as necessary, to adapt to evolving risks, threats and other changes that affect the organization?

### HRS-02 — Human Resources Security Management

Does the organization facilitate the implementation of personnel security controls?

### HRS-03 — Position Categorization

Does the organization manage personnel security risk by assigning a risk designation to all positions and establishing screening criteria for individuals filling those positions?

### HRS-03.1 — Users With Elevated Privileges

Does the organization ensure that every user accessing Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) that process, store and/or transmit sensitive and/or regulated data is cleared and regularly trained to handle the information in question?

### HRS-03.2 — Competency Requirements for Security, Compliance & Resilience-Related Positions

Does the organization ensure that all security-related positions are staffed by qualified individuals who have the necessary skill set?

### HRS-04 — Defined Roles & Responsibilities

Does the organization define cybersecurity roles & responsibilities for all personnel?

### HRS-04.1 — Assigned Roles & Responsibilities Awareness

Does the organization communicate with users about their roles and responsibilities to maintain a safe and secure working environment?

### HRS-05 — Personnel Screening

Does the organization manage personnel security risk by screening individuals prior to authorizing access?

### HRS-05.1 — Roles With Special Protection Measures

Does the organization ensure that individuals accessing a system that stores, transmits or processes information requiring special protection satisfy organization-defined personnel screening criteria?

### HRS-05.2 — Citizenship Requirements

Does the organization verify that individuals accessing a system processing, storing, or transmitting sensitive information meet applicable statutory, regulatory and/or contractual requirements for citizenship?

### HRS-06 — Terms of Employment

Does the organization require all employees and contractors to apply cybersecurity and data protection principles in their daily work to enable secure, compliant and resilient capabilities?

### HRS-06.1 — Rules of Behavior

Does the organization define acceptable and unacceptable rules of behavior for the use of technologies, including consequences for unacceptable behavior?

### HRS-06.2 — Social Media & Social Networking Restrictions

Does the organization define rules of behavior that contain explicit restrictions on the use of social media and networking sites, posting information on commercial websites and sharing account information?

### HRS-06.3 — Technology Use Restrictions

Does the organization establish usage restrictions and implementation guidance for organizational technologies based on the potential to cause damage to Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS), if used maliciously?

### HRS-06.4 — Use of Critical Technologies

Does the organization govern usage policies for critical technologies?

### HRS-06.5 — Use of Mobile Devices

Does the organization manage business risks associated with permitting mobile device access to organizational resources?

### HRS-06.6 — Security-Minded Dress Code

Does the organization prohibit the use of oversized clothing (e.g., baggy pants and oversized hooded sweatshirts) to prevent the unauthorized exfiltration of data and technology assets?

### HRS-07 — Access Agreements

Does the organization require internal and third-party users to sign appropriate access agreements prior to being granted access?

### HRS-07.1 — Confidentiality Agreements

Does the organization require Non-Disclosure Agreements (NDAs) or similar confidentiality agreements that reflect the needs to protect data and operational details, or both employees and third-parties?

### HRS-08 — Onboarding, Transferring & Offboarding Personnel

Does the organization proactively govern the following personnel management actions:
(1) Onboarding new personnel (e.g., new hires);
(2) Transferring personnel into new roles within the organization; and
(3) Offboarding personnel (e.g., termination of employment)?

### HRS-08.1 — Formal Indoctrination

Does the organization formally educate authorized users on proper data handling practices for all the relevant types of data to which they have access?

### HRS-08.2 — Policy Familiarization & Acknowledgement

Does the organization ensure personnel receive recurring familiarization with its security, compliance and resilience policies and provide acknowledgement?

### HRS-08.3 — Post-Employment Requirements Awareness

Does the organization notify individuals of their applicable, legally-binding post-employment requirements for the protection of sensitive and/or regulated data?

### HRS-08.4 — Post-Employment Requirements Notification

Does the organization govern former employee behavior by formally notifying terminated individuals of their applicable, legally binding post-employment requirements for the protection of sensitive and/or regulated data?

### HRS-09 — Probationary Periods

Does the organization identify newly onboarded personnel for enhanced monitoring during their probationary period?

### HRS-10 — Personnel Sanctions

Does the organization sanction personnel failing to comply with established security policies, standards and procedures?

### HRS-10.1 — Workplace Investigations

Does the organization conduct employee misconduct investigations when there is reasonable assurance that a policy has been violated?

### HRS-10.2 — Updating Disciplinary Processes

Does the organization periodically review and, where appropriate, update disciplinary practices due to:
(1) Legal changes;
(2) Significant changes to operations; and
(3) Applicable threats and risks?

### HRS-10.3 — Preventative Access Restriction

Does the organization proactively restrict logical and physical access when an individual with access to sensitive and/or regulated data is under investigation for personnel sanctions that may lead to employment termination?

### HRS-11 — Personnel Transfer

Does the organization adjust logical and physical access authorizations to Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) and facilities upon personnel reassignment or transfer, in a timely manner?

### HRS-12 — Personnel Termination

Does the organization govern the termination of individual employment?

### HRS-12.1 — Automated Employment Status Notifications

Does the organization use automated mechanisms to notify Identity and Access Management (IAM) personnel or roles upon termination of an individual employment or contract?

### HRS-12.2 — Asset Collection

Does the organization retrieve organization-owned assets upon termination of an individual's employment?

### HRS-12.3 — High-Risk Terminations

Does the organization expedite the process of removing "high risk" individual's access to Technology Assets, Applications, Services and/or Data (TAASD) upon termination, as determined by management?

### HRS-13 — Third-Party Personnel

Does the organization govern third-party personnel by reviewing and monitoring third-party security, compliance and/or resilience roles and responsibilities?

### HRS-14 — Separation of Duties (SoD)

Does the organization implement and maintain Separation of Duties (SoD) to prevent potential inappropriate activity without collusion?

### HRS-15 — Incompatible Roles

Does the organization avoid incompatible development-specific roles through limiting and reviewing developer privileges to change hardware, software and firmware components within a production/operational environment?

### HRS-16 — Identify Critical Skills & Gaps

Does the organization evaluate the critical security, compliance and resilience skills needed to support its mission and identify gaps that exist?

### HRS-16.1 — Remediate Identified Skills Deficiencies

Does the organization remediate critical skills deficiencies necessary to support its mission and business functions?

### HRS-16.2 — Identify Vital Security, Compliance & Resilience Staff

Does the organization identify vital security, compliance and resilience staff?

### HRS-16.3 — Establish Redundancy for Vital Security, Compliance & Resilience Staff

Does the organization establish redundancy for vital security, compliance and resilience staff?

### HRS-16.4 — Perform Succession Planning

Does the organization perform succession planning for vital security, compliance and resilience roles?

### HRS-17 — Identifying Authorized Work Locations

Does the organization identify and document authorized working locations, including:
(1) Designated on-premises, organization-controlled work locations; and
(2) Other off-premises locations not under organization-control (e.g., work from home)?

### HRS-17.1 — Communicating Authorized Work Locations

Does the organization communicate authorized work locations to organizational personnel?

### HRS-18 — Reporting Suspicious Activities

Does the organization enable personnel to report suspicious activities and/or behavior without fear of reprisal or other negative consequences (e.g., whistleblower protections)?

### IAC-01 — Identification & Authentication Policy

Does the organization establish a formal, documented identification and authentication policy that:
 (1) Conveys executive management's intent;
 (2) Provides organizational direction and expected behaviors;
 (3) Is reviewed at least annually; and
 (4) Is updated, as necessary, to adapt to evolving risks, threats and other changes that affect the organization?

### IAC-02 — Identity & Access Management (IAM)

Does the organization facilitate the implementation of identification and access management controls?

### IAC-03 — Authenticate, Authorize and Audit (AAA)

Does the organization strictly govern the use of Authenticate, Authorize and Audit (AAA) solutions, both on-premises and those hosted by an External Service Provider (ESP)?

### IAC-03.1 — Replay-Resistant Authentication

Does the organization use automated mechanisms to employ replay-resistant authentication?

### IAC-03.2 — Retain Access Records

Does the organization retain a record of personnel accountability to ensure there is a record of all access granted to an individual (system and application-wise), who provided the authorization, when the authorization was granted and when the access was last reviewed?

### IAC-03.3 — Identity Providers (IdP) & Authorization Servers

Does the organization employ identity providers and authorization servers to manage user, device and Non-Person Entity (NPE) identities, attributes and access rights that support authentication and authorization decisions:
(1) In accordance with organization-defined identification and authentication policy; and
(2) Using organization-defined mechanisms?

### IAC-04 — User Provisioning & De-Provisioning

Does the organization utilize a formal user registration and de-registration process that governs the assignment of access rights?

### IAC-04.1 — Change of Roles & Duties

Does the organization revoke user access rights following changes in personnel roles and duties, if no longer necessary or permitted?

### IAC-04.2 — Termination of Employment

Does the organization revoke user access rights in a timely manner, upon termination of employment or contract?

### IAC-05 — Identity Proofing (Identity Verification)

Does the organization verify the identity of a user before issuing authenticators or modifying access permissions?

### IAC-05.1 — In-Person or Trusted Third-Party Registration

Does the organization conduct in-person or trusted third-party identify verification before user accounts for third-parties are created?

### IAC-05.2 — Identity Evidence

Does the organization require evidence of individual identification to be presented to the registration authority?

### IAC-05.3 — Identity Evidence Validation & Verification

Does the organization require that the presented identity evidence be validated and verified through organizational-defined methods of validation and verification?

### IAC-05.4 — In-Person Validation & Verification

Does the organization require that the validation and verification of identity evidence be conducted in person before a designated registration authority?

### IAC-05.5 — Address Confirmation

Does the organization require that a notice of proofing be delivered through an out-of-band channel to verify the user's address (physical or digital)?

### IAC-06 — Role-Based Access Control (RBAC)

Does the organization enforce Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) for Technology Assets, Applications, Services and/or Data (TAASD) to restrict access to individuals assigned specific roles with legitimate business needs?

### IAC-07 — Attribute-Based Access Control (ABAC)

Does the organization use automated mechanisms to enforce Attribute-Based Access Control (ABAC) through policy-driven, dynamic authorizations to:
 (1) Enforce usage conditions for users and/or role; and
 (2) Support the secure sharing of information?

### IAC-07.1 — Real-Time Access Decisions

Does the organization use automated mechanisms to utilize Machine Learning (ML) to make real-time access decisions based on advanced network analytics that leverages enterprise-wide data sources?

### IAC-07.2 — Access Profile Rules

Does the organization develop access profile rules for sensitive and/or regulated Technology Assets, Applications, Services and/or Data (TAASD) access based on User, Data, Network, Environment & Device attributes?

### IAC-08 — Account Management

Does the organization:
(1) Define authorized system account types;
(2) Define prohibited system account types; and
(3) Proactively govern individual, group, system, service, application, guest and temporary accounts?

### IAC-08.1 — Automated System Account Management (Directory Services)

Does the organization use automated mechanisms to support the management of system accounts (e.g., directory services)?

### IAC-08.2 — Authorized Accounts

Does the organization define and document the types of accounts allowed and prohibited on Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS)?

### IAC-08.3 — User & Service Account Inventories

Does the organization maintain a current list of authorized users and service accounts?

### IAC-08.4 — Disable Inactive Accounts

Does the organization use automated mechanisms to disable inactive accounts after an organization-defined time period?

### IAC-08.5 — Account Disabling for High Risk Individuals

Does the organization disable accounts immediately upon notification for users posing a significant risk to the organization?

### IAC-08.6 — Automated Audit Actions

Does the organization use automated mechanisms to audit account creation, modification, enabling, disabling and removal actions and notify organization-defined personnel or roles?

### IAC-08.7 — Account Separation Between Infrastructure Environments

Does the organization separate non-privileged accounts between infrastructure environments to reduce the risk that a compromise in one infrastructure environment laterally affects another infrastructure environment?

### IAC-08.8 — Multiple System Accounts

Does the organization implement security safeguards to manage the risk of compromise due to individuals having accounts on multiple Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS)?

### IAC-09 — Management Approval For New or Changed Accounts

Does the organization ensure management approvals are required for new accounts or changes in permissions to existing accounts?

### IAC-09.1 — Management Approval For Privileged Accounts

Does the organization restrict the assignment of privileged accounts to management-approved personnel and/or roles?

### IAC-10 — Privileged Account Management (PAM)

Does the organization restrict and control privileged access rights for users and Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS)?

### IAC-10.1 — Privileged Account Inventories

Does the organization inventory all privileged accounts and validate that each person with elevated privileges is authorized by the appropriate level of organizational management?

### IAC-10.2 — Privileged Account Separation

Does the organization separate privileged accounts between infrastructure environments to reduce the risk of a compromise in one infrastructure environment from laterally affecting other infrastructure environments?

### IAC-10.3 — Dedicated Privileged Account

Does the organization assign dedicated privileged user accounts to be used solely for duties requiring privileged access?

### IAC-10.4 — Privileged Command Execution

Does the organization ensure privilege change requests require additional levels of authentication?

### IAC-10.5 — Manual Override

Does the organization enable a manual override of the current account privileges to enable the timely response to unusual conditions without terminating the current session and establishing a new session as a higher-privileged user?

### IAC-11 — Emergency Accounts

Does the organization establish and control "emergency access only" accounts?

### IAC-11.1 — Removal of Temporary / Emergency Accounts

Does the organization use automated mechanisms to disable or remove temporary and emergency accounts after an organization-defined time period for each type of account?

### IAC-12 — Periodic Review of Individual & Service Account Privileges

Does the organization periodically-review the privileges assigned to individuals and service accounts to validate the need for such privileges and reassign or remove unnecessary privileges, as necessary?

### IAC-12.1 — System Account Reviews

Does the organization review all system accounts and disable any account that cannot be associated with a business process and owner?

### IAC-13 — User Identity (ID) Management

Does the organization ensure proper user identification management for non-consumer users and administrators?

### IAC-13.1 — Standardized Identifier Management (User Names)

Does the organization govern naming standards for usernames and Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS)?

### IAC-13.2 — Employment Status Identification

Does the organization identify contractors and other third-party users through unique username characteristics?

### IAC-13.3 — Citizenship Identification

Does the organization identify foreign nationals, including by their specific citizenship?

### IAC-13.4 — Dynamic Management

Does the organization dynamically manage usernames and system identifiers?

### IAC-13.5 — Cross-Organization Management

Does the organization coordinate username identifiers with external organizations for cross-organization management of identifiers?

### IAC-13.6 — Privileged Account Identifiers

Does the organization uniquely manage privileged accounts to identify the account as a privileged user or service?

### IAC-13.7 — Pairwise Pseudonymous Identifiers (PPID)

Does the organization generate pairwise pseudonymous identifiers with no identifying information about a data subject to discourage activity tracking and profiling of the data subject?

### IAC-14 — Authenticator Management

Does the organization:
(1) Securely manage authenticators for users and devices; and
(2) Ensure the strength of authentication is appropriate to the classification of the data being accessed?

### IAC-14.1 — Events Requiring Authenticator Change

Does the organization change authentication credentials:
(1) At predefined intervals; and/or
(2) Upon suspicion of credential compromise?

### IAC-14.2 — Protection of Authenticators

Does the organization protect authenticators commensurate with the sensitivity of the information to which use of the authenticator permits access?

### IAC-14.3 — No Embedded Unencrypted Static Authenticators

Does the organization ensure that unencrypted, static authenticators are not embedded in applications, scripts or stored on function keys?

### IAC-14.4 — Default Authenticators

Does the organization ensure default authenticators are changed as part of account creation or system installation?

### IAC-14.5 — Expiration of Cached Authenticators

Does the organization use automated mechanisms to prohibit the use of cached authenticators after organization-defined time period?

### IAC-15 — Password-Based Authentication

Does the organization enforce complexity, length and lifespan considerations to ensure strong criteria for password-based authentication?

### IAC-15.1 — Automated Support For Password Strength

Does the organization use automated mechanisms to determine if password authenticators are sufficiently strong enough to satisfy organization-defined password length and complexity requirements?

### IAC-15.2 — Password Managers

Does the organization protect and store passwords via a password manager tool?

### IAC-16 — Passkeys

Does the organization utilize passkeys, or equivalent cryptographic key pairing technologies, to authenticate users to Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS)?

### IAC-17 — Biometric Authentication

Does the organization ensure biometric-based authentication satisfies organization-defined biometric quality requirements for false positives and false negatives?

### IAC-18 — PKI-Based Authentication

Does the organization use automated mechanisms to validate certificates by constructing and verifying a certification path to an accepted trust anchor including checking certificate status information for PKI-based authentication?

### IAC-19 — Hardware Token-Based Authentication

Does the organization use automated mechanisms to ensure organization-defined token quality requirements are satisfied for hardware token-based authentication?

### IAC-20 — Authenticator Feedback

Does the organization obscure the feedback of authentication information during the authentication process to protect the information from possible exploitation/use by unauthorized individuals?

### IAC-21 — Restrictions on Shared Groups / Accounts

Does the organization authorize the use of shared/group accounts only under certain organization-defined conditions?

### IAC-21.1 — Group Authentication

Does the organization require individuals to be authenticated with an individual authenticator when a group authenticator is utilized?

### IAC-22 — User Responsibilities for Account Management

Does the organization compel users to follow accepted practices in the use of authentication mechanisms (e.g., passwords, passphrases, physical or logical security tokens, smart cards and certificates)?

### IAC-23 — Credential Sharing

Does the organization prevent the sharing of generic IDs, passwords or other generic authentication methods?

### IAC-24 — Reference Monitor

Does the organization implement a reference monitor that is tamperproof, always-invoked, small enough to be subject to analysis / testing and the completeness of which can be assured?

### IAC-25 — Access Enforcement

Does the organization enforce Logical Access Control (LAC) permissions that conform to the principle of "least privilege."?

### IAC-25.1 — Access To Sensitive / Regulated Data

Does the organization limit access to sensitive and/or regulated data to only those individuals whose job requires such access?

### IAC-25.2 — Database Access

Does the organization restrict access to databases containing sensitive and/or regulated data to only necessary Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) or those individuals whose job requires such access?

### IAC-26 — Use of Privileged Utility Programs

Does the organization restrict and tightly control utility programs that are capable of overriding system and application controls?

### IAC-27 — Dedicated Administrative Machines

Does the organization restrict executing administrative tasks or tasks requiring elevated access to a dedicated machine?

### IAC-28 — Dual Authorization for Privileged Commands

Does the organization use automated mechanisms to enforce dual authorization for privileged commands?

### IAC-29 — Revocation of Access Authorizations

Does the organization revoke logical and physical access authorizations?

### IAC-30 — Least Privilege

Does the organization utilize the concept of least privilege, allowing only authorized access to processes necessary to accomplish assigned tasks in accordance with organizational business functions?

### IAC-30.1 — Prohibit Non-Privileged Users from Executing Privileged Functions

Does the organization prevent non-privileged users from executing privileged functions to include disabling, circumventing or altering implemented security safeguards / countermeasures?

### IAC-30.2 — Authorize Access to Security Functions

Does the organization limit access to security functions to explicitly-authorized privileged users?

### IAC-30.3 — Non-Privileged Access for Non-Security Functions

Does the organization prohibit privileged users from using privileged accounts, while performing non-security functions?

### IAC-30.4 — Auditing Use of Privileged Functions

Does the organization audit the execution of privileged functions?

### IAC-30.5 — Network Access to Privileged Commands

Does the organization authorize remote access to perform privileged commands on critical Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) or where sensitive and/or regulated data is stored, transmitted and/or processed only for compelling operational needs?

### IAC-30.6 — Privilege Levels for Code Execution

Does the organization use automated mechanisms to prevent applications from executing at higher privilege levels than the user's privileges?

### IAC-31 — Permitted Actions Without Identification or Authorization

Does the organization identify and document the supporting rationale for specific user actions that can be performed on a system without identification or authentication?

### IAC-32 — Identification & Authentication for Organizational Users

Does the organization uniquely identify and centrally Authenticate, Authorize and Audit (AAA) organizational users and processes acting on behalf of organizational users?

### IAC-32.1 — Out-of-Band Authentication (OOBA)

Does the organization implement Out-of-Band Authentication (OOBA) under specific conditions?

### IAC-32.2 — Acceptance of PIV Credentials

Does the organization accept and electronically verify organizational Personal Identity Verification (PIV) credentials?

### IAC-33 — Identification & Authentication for Non-Organizational Users

Does the organization uniquely identify and centrally Authenticate, Authorize and Audit (AAA) third-party users and processes that provide services to the organization?

### IAC-33.1 — Acceptance of Third-Party Credentials

Does the organization use automated mechanisms to accept Federal Identity, Credential and Access Management (FICAM)-approved third-party credentials?

### IAC-33.2 — Acceptance of External Authenticators

Does the organization restrict the use of external authenticators to those that are National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST)-compliant and maintain a list of accepted external authenticators?

### IAC-33.3 — Disassociability

Does the organization disassociate user attributes or credential assertion relationships among individuals, credential service providers and relying parties?

### IAC-33.4 — Acceptance of PIV Credentials from Other Organizations

Does the organization accept and electronically verify Personal Identity Verification (PIV) credentials from third-parties?

### IAC-33.5 — Use of FICAM-Issued Profiles

Does the organization conform systems to Federal Identity, Credential and Access Management (FICAM)-issued profiles?

### IAC-34 — Identification & Authentication for Devices

Does the organization uniquely identify and centrally Authenticate, Authorize and Audit (AAA) devices before establishing a connection using bidirectional authentication that is cryptographically- based and replay resistant?

### IAC-34.1 — Device Attestation

Does the organization ensure device identification and authentication is accurate by centrally-managing the joining of systems to the domain as part of the initial asset configuration management process?

### IAC-34.2 — Device Authorization Enforcement

Does the organization enforce cryptographic communications keys to prevent one key from being used to access multiple devices?

### IAC-35 — Access Control For Mobile Devices

Does the organization enforce access control requirements for the connection of mobile devices to organizational Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS)?

### IAC-36 — Identification & Authentication for Third-Party Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS)

Does the organization identify and authenticate third-party Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS)?

### IAC-36.1 — Sharing Identification & Authentication Information

Does the organization ensure external service providers provide current and accurate information for any third-party user with access to its data or assets?

### IAC-36.2 — Privileged Access by Non-Organizational Users

Does the organization prohibit privileged access by non-organizational users?

### IAC-37 — Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA)

Does the organization use automated mechanisms to enforce Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) for:
 (1) Remote network access;
 (2) Third-party Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS); and/ or
 (3) Non-console access to critical TAAS that store, transmit and/or process sensitive and/or regulated data?

### IAC-37.1 — Replay-Resistant Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA)

Does the organization use automated mechanisms to enforce replay-resistant Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) through authenticators whose outputs cannot be reused, using:
 (1) Nonces;
 (2) One-time challenges;
 (3) Time-synchronous values; and/or
 (4) Channel binding?

### IAC-37.2 — Phishing-Resistant Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA)

Does the organization use automated mechanisms to enforce phishing-resistant Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) through authenticators that are cryptographically bound to the verifier's identity, preventing credential relay by an impersonating party?

### IAC-37.3 — Out-of-Band (OOB) Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA)

Does the organization implement Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) for access to privileged and non-privileged accounts such that one of the factors is independently provided by a device separate from the system being accessed?

### IAC-37.4 — Alternative Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA)

Does the organization enable alternative Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) tokens when the primary MFA solution is not able to be used?

### IAC-37.5 — Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) For Network Access to Privileged Accounts

Does the organization utilize Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) to authenticate network access for privileged accounts?

### IAC-37.6 — Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) For Network Access to Non-Privileged Accounts

Does the organization utilize Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) to authenticate network access for non-privileged accounts?

### IAC-37.7 — Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) For Local Access to Privileged Accounts

Does the organization utilize Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) to authenticate local access for privileged accounts?

### IAC-38 — Cryptographic Module Authentication

Does the organization use automated mechanisms to enable Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) to authenticate to a cryptographic module?

### IAC-39 — Hardware Security Modules (HSM)

Does the organization use automated mechanisms to utilize Hardware Security Modules (HSM) to protect authenticators on which the component relies?

### IAC-40 — Single Sign-On (SSO) Transparent Authentication

Does the organization provide a transparent authentication (e.g., Single Sign-On (SSO)) capability to its Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS)?

### IAC-41 — Adaptive Identification & Authentication

Does the organization allow individuals to utilize alternative methods of authentication under specific circumstances or situations?

### IAC-42 — Continuous Authentication

Does the organization use automated mechanisms to enable continuous re-authentication through the lifecycle of entity interactions?

### IAC-43 — Re-Authentication

Does the organization force users and devices to re-authenticate according to organization-defined circumstances that necessitate re-authentication?

### IAC-44 — Mutual Authentication (MA)

Does the organization enforce Mutual Authentication (MA) where both sides of a communications channel verify the identity of the other party through certificate exchange?

### IAC-45 — Federated Credential Management

Does the organization federate credentials to allow cross-organization authentication of individuals and devices?

### IAC-46 — Invalidate Session Identifiers at Logout

Does the organization use automated mechanisms to invalidate session identifiers upon user logout or other session termination?

### IAC-47 — Unique System-Generated Session Identifiers

Does the organization use automated mechanisms to generate and recognize unique session identifiers for each session?

### IAC-48 — Software Defined Storage (SDS) Data Access Control

Does the organization use automated mechanisms to utilize Software Defined Storage (SDS), or equivalent technologies, to enforce data access controls that:
 (1) Prevent access by unauthorized entities and by entities operating from unauthorized devices; and
 (2) Segregate access between communities of interest for data residing within the same classification level?

### IAC-49 — Sensitive / Regulated Data Access Enforcement

Does the organization configure Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) to restrict access to sensitive and/or regulated data?

### IAC-49.1 — Sensitive / Regulated Data Actions

Does the organization use automated mechanisms to generate event logs whenever sensitive and/or regulated data is collected, created, updated, deleted and/or archived?

### IAC-50 — Compliance As Code (CAC) Identity Governance

Does the organization inventory, uniquely identify and assign accountable ownership for Control Assurance Automation (CAA) automated identifies, including:
 (1) Service accounts;
 (2) API keys;
 (3) OAuth grants; and
 (4) Machine and workload identities?

### IAC-51 — Compliance As Code (CAC) Least Privileges

Does the organization restrict Control Assurance Automation (CAA) automated identities to:
 (1) Provide read-only, least-privilege access; and
 (2) Prohibit write and/or administrative permissions?

### IAC-52 — Compliance As Code (CAC) Credential Lifecycle Management

Does the organization rotate, expire and revoke credentials for Control Assurance Automation (CAA) automated identities:
 (1) On a defined cycle; and
 (2) Upon personnel, tooling or scope change?

### IAC-53 — Compliance As Code (CAC) Credentials Management

Does the organization govern Control Assurance Automation (CAA) automated identity credentials by:
 (1) Centralized storage in a password management tool; and
 (2) Prohibiting hardcoded credentials?

### IRO-01 — Incident Response Policy

Does the organization establish a formal, documented incident response policy that:
 (1) Conveys executive management's intent;
 (2) Provides organizational direction and expected behaviors;
 (3) Is reviewed at least annually; and
 (4) Is updated, as necessary, to adapt to evolving risks, threats and other changes that affect the organization?

### IRO-02 — Incident Response Operations

Does the organization implement and govern processes and documentation to facilitate an organization-wide response capability for cybersecurity and data protection-related incidents?

### IRO-03 — Continuous Incident Response Improvements

Does the organization use qualitative and quantitative data from incident response testing to:
(1) Determine the effectiveness of incident response processes;
(2) Continuously improve incident response processes; and
(3) Provide incident response measures and metrics that are accurate, consistent and in a reproducible format?

### IRO-04 — Incident Classification & Prioritization

Does the organization identify classes of incidents and actions to take to ensure the continuation of organizational missions and business functions?

### IRO-05 — Indicators of Compromise (IOC)

Does the organization define specific Indicators of Compromise (IOC) to identify the signs of potential cybersecurity events?

### IRO-06 — Incident Handling

Does the organization cover:
 (1) Preparation;
 (2) Automated event detection or manual incident report intake;
 (3) Analysis;
 (4) Containment;
 (5) Eradication; and
 (6) Recovery?

### IRO-06.1 — Correlation with External Organizations

Does the organization coordinate with approved third-parties to achieve a cross-organization perspective on incident awareness and more effective incident responses?

### IRO-07 — Automated Incident Handling Processes

Does the organization use automated mechanisms to support the incident handling process?

### IRO-07.1 — Automated Reporting

Does the organization use automated mechanisms to assist in the reporting of cybersecurity and data protection incidents?

### IRO-07.2 — Automated Tracking, Data Collection & Analysis

Does the organization use automated mechanisms to assist in the tracking, collection and analysis of information from actual and potential cybersecurity and data protection incidents?

### IRO-07.3 — Dynamic Reconfiguration

Does the organization use automated mechanisms to dynamically reconfigure system components as part of the incident response capability?

### IRO-07.4 — Automatic Disabling of Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS)

Does the organization automatically disable Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS), upon detection of a possible incident that meets organizational criteria, which allows for forensic analysis to be performed?

### IRO-08 — Incident Response Plan (IRP)

Does the organization maintain and make available a current and viable Incident Response Plan (IRP) to all stakeholders?

### IRO-08.1 — Incident Response Plan (IRP) Update

Does the organization regularly review and modify incident response practices to incorporate lessons learned, business process changes and industry developments, as necessary?

### IRO-09 — Incident Response Capabilities Testing

Does the organization formally test incident response capabilities through realistic exercises to determine the operational effectiveness of those capabilities?

### IRO-09.1 — Incident Response Capabilities Testing Coordination with Related Plans

Does the organization coordinate incident response testing with organizational elements responsible for related plans?

### IRO-10 — Incident Response Training

Does the organization train personnel in their incident response roles and responsibilities?

### IRO-10.1 — Simulated Incidents

Does the organization incorporate simulated events into incident response training to facilitate effective response by personnel in crisis situations?

### IRO-10.2 — Automated Incident Response Training Environments

Does the organization use automated mechanisms to provide a more thorough and realistic incident response training environment?

### IRO-11 — Integrated Security Incident Response Team (ISIRT)

Does the organization establish an integrated team of cybersecurity, IT and business function representatives that are capable of addressing cybersecurity and data protection incident response operations?

### IRO-12 — Public Relations & Reputation Repair

Does the organization proactively manage public relations associated with incidents and employ appropriate measures to prevent further reputational damage and develop plans to repair any damage to its reputation?

### IRO-13 — Chain of Custody & Forensics

Does the organization perform digital forensics and maintain the integrity of the chain of custody, in accordance with applicable laws, regulations and industry-recognized secure practices?

### IRO-13.1 — Licensed Forensic Investigators

Does the organization utilize licensed forensic investigators to perform data analysis for evidentiary purposes that may be used in legal proceedings or to prove wrongdoing?

### IRO-14 — Root Cause Analysis (RCA) & Lessons Learned

Does the organization incorporate lessons learned from analyzing and resolving cybersecurity and data protection incidents to reduce the likelihood or impact of future incidents?

### IRO-15 — Regulatory & Law Enforcement Contacts

Does the organization maintain incident response contacts with applicable regulatory and law enforcement agencies?

### IRO-16 — Incident Stakeholder Reporting

Does the organization timely-report incidents to applicable:
 (1) Internal stakeholders;
 (2) Affected clients & third-parties; and
 (3) Regulatory authorities?

### IRO-16.1 — Situational Awareness For Incidents

Does the organization document, monitor and report the status of cybersecurity and data protection incidents to internal stakeholders all the way through the resolution of the incident?

### IRO-16.2 — Cyber Incident Reporting for Sensitive / Regulated Data

Does the organization report sensitive and/or regulated data incidents in a timely manner?

### IRO-16.3 — Serious Incident Reporting

Does the organization report any serious incident involving its Technology Assets, Applications, Services and/or Data (TAASD) to relevant authorities in the locality where the incident occurred, in accordance with mandatory reporting:
(1) Requirements; and
(2) Timelines?

### IRO-16.4 — Vulnerabilities Related To Incidents

Does the organization report system vulnerabilities associated with reported cybersecurity and data protection incidents to organization-defined personnel or roles?

### IRO-17 — Incident Tracking Repository

Does the organization maintain a repository of cybersecurity events and incidents that documents:
(1) Details of the incident (e.g., category, severity and affected parties);
(2) Remediation actions taken through incident closure; and
(3) A summary from the Root Cause Analysis (RCA), if applicable?

### IRO-17.1 — Incident Pattern Analysis

Does the organization analyze historical incidents in aggregate to identify:
(1) Patterns;
(2) Trends; and
(3) Other common root causes in order to address the vulnerability and risk?

### IRO-17.2 — Recurring Incident Analysis

Does the organization periodically review incident response activities for the existence of recurring incidents?

### IRO-18 — Incident Reporting Assistance

Does the organization provide incident response advice and assistance to users of Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) for the handling and reporting of actual and potential cybersecurity and data protection incidents?

### IRO-18.1 — Automation Support of Availability of Information / Support

Does the organization use automated mechanisms to increase the availability of incident response-related information and support?

### IRO-19 — Supply Chain Coordination

Does the organization provide cybersecurity and data protection incident information to the provider of the Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) and other organizations involved in the supply chain for TAAS related to the incident?

### IRO-19.1 — Coordination With External Providers

Does the organization establish a direct, cooperative relationship between its incident response capability and external service providers?

### IRO-20 — Sensitive / Regulated Data Spill Response

Does the organization respond to sensitive and/or regulated data spills?

### IRO-20.1 — Sensitive / Regulated Data Spill Responsible Personnel

Does the organization formally assign personnel or roles with responsibility for responding to sensitive and/or regulated data spills?

### IRO-20.2 — Sensitive / Regulated Data Spill Training

Does the organization ensure incident response training material provides coverage for sensitive and/or regulated data spillage response?

### IRO-20.3 — Post-Sensitive / Regulated Data Spill Operations

Does the organization ensure that organizational personnel impacted by sensitive and/or regulated data spills can continue to carry out assigned tasks while contaminated Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) are undergoing corrective actions?

### IRO-20.4 — Sensitive / Regulated Data Exposure to Unauthorized Personnel

Does the organization address security safeguards for personnel exposed to sensitive and/or regulated data that is not within their assigned access authorizations?

### IRO-21 — Detonation Chambers (Sandboxes)

Does the organization utilize a detonation chamber capability to detect and/or block potentially-malicious files and email attachments?

### IRO-22 — Data Breach

Does the organization address data breaches, or other incidents involving the unauthorized disclosure of sensitive or regulated data, according to applicable laws, regulations and contractual obligations?

### IRO-23 — Artificial Intelligence (AI) & Autonomous Technologies (AAT) Incidents

Does the organization handle failures or incidents with Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Autonomous Technologies (AAT) deemed to be high-risk?

### IRO-24 — Cryptographic Incident Response (Emergency Algorithm Transition)

Does the organization establish the capability to respond to the compromise or disallowance of a Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC) or classical algorithm on a compressed timeline, including:
(1) Pre-identified algorithm alternates;
(2) Tested rollback and roll-forward procedures;
(3) Customer and/or counterparty communication templates; and
(4) Incident response rehearsals against defined scenarios?

### IRO-25 — Embedded Technology Incidents

Does the organization handle failures and/or incidents with embedded technologies?

### IRO-26 — Post-Incident Technology Assets, Applications and Services (TAAS) Validation

Does the organization utilize post-incident assurance activities to validate Technology Assets, Applications and Services (TAAS) are
 (1) Secure;
 (2) Compliant; and
 (3) Capable of supporting the resumption of normal business operations?

### IAO-01 — Information Assurance Policy

Does the organization establish a formal, documented information assurance policy that:
 (1) Conveys executive management's intent;
 (2) Provides organizational direction and expected behaviors;
 (3) Is reviewed at least annually; and
 (4) Is updated, as necessary, to adapt to evolving risks, threats and other changes that affect the organization?

### IAO-02 — Information Assurance (IA) Operations

Does the organization facilitate the implementation of security, compliance and resilience assessment and authorization controls?

### IAO-03 — Assessment Boundaries

Does the organization establish the scope of assessments by defining the assessment boundary, according to people, processes and technology that directly or indirectly impact the confidentiality, integrity, availability and safety of the Technology Assets, Applications, Services and/or Data (TAASD) under review?

### IAO-04 — Control Validation Testing (CVT)

Does the organization formally assess the security, compliance and resilience controls in Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) through Information Assurance Program (IAP) activities to determine the extent to which the controls are implemented correctly, operating as intended and producing the desired outcome with respect to meeting expected requirements?

### IAO-04.1 — Plan / Coordinate with Other Organizational Entities

Does the organization plan and coordinate Information Assurance Program (IAP) activities with affected stakeholders before conducting such activities in order to reduce the potential impact on operations?

### IAO-05 — Specialized Assessments

Does the organization conduct specialized assessments for:
(1) Statutory, regulatory and contractual compliance obligations;
(2) Monitoring capabilities;
(3) Mobile devices;
(4) Databases;
(5) Application security;
(6) Embedded technologies (e.g., IoT and OT);
(7) Vulnerability management;
(8) Malicious code;
(9) Insider threats;
(10) Performance/load testing;
(11) Artificial Intelligence and Autonomous Technologies (AAT); and/or
(12) Other Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) that require specialized expertise to determine conformity with security, compliance and/or resilience requirements?

### IAO-06 — Assessor Independence

Does the organization ensure assessors or assessment teams have the appropriate independence to conduct security, compliance and/or resilience control assessments?

### IAO-07 — Third-Party Assessment Reciprocity

Does the organization accept and respond to the results of external assessments that are performed by impartial, external organizations?

### IAO-08 — Adequate Security for Sensitive / Regulated Data In Support of Contracts

Does the organization protect sensitive and/or regulated data that is collected, developed, received, transmitted, used or stored in support of the performance of a contract?

### IAO-09 — Applied Security, Compliance and Resilience Controls Documentation

Does the organization generate authoritative documentation (e.g., System Security Plan (SSP)) that:
(1) Identifies key architectural and implementation information on in-scope Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS);
(2) Reflects the current state of applied security, compliance and resilience controls on applicable People, Processes, Technologies, Data and/or Facilities (PPTDF) that are contained within the system boundary; and
(3) Provides a historical record of applied security controls, including changes?

### IAO-10 — Threat Analysis & Flaw Remediation During Development

Does the organization require system developers and integrators to create and execute a Security Testing and Evaluation (ST&E) plan, or similar process, to identify and remediate flaws during development?

### IAO-11 — Technical Verification

Does the organization perform Information Assurance Program (IAP) activities to evaluate the design, implementation and effectiveness of technical security, compliance and resilience controls?

### IAO-12 — Capabilities Deficiency Tracking

Does the organization govern identified deficiencies (e.g., Plan of Action and Milestones (POA&M) or similar methodology) that formally documents, at a minimum:
(1) Deficiency tracking number;
(2) Applicable security, compliance and/or resilience control;
(3) Description of the deficiency(ies);
(4) Risk associated with the deficiency(ies);
(5) Source deficiency identification/detection;
(6) Temporary compensating controls, if applicable;
(7) Point of Contact (POC) (e.g., asset/process owner);
(8) Resources required to conduct remediation actions;
(9) Planned remedial actions to the deficiency(ies);
(10) Proposed remediation timeline; and
(11) Disposition statement (e.g., closeout summary)?

### IAO-12.1 — Deficiency Tracking Automation

Does the organization use automated mechanisms to help ensure tracked deficiencies are:
(1) Accurate;
(2) Up-to-date; and
(3) Readily-available?

### IAO-13 — Security Assessment Report (SAR)

Does the organization produce a Security Assessment Report (SAR) at the conclusion of a security assessment to certify the results of the assessment and assist with any remediation actions?

### IAO-14 — Security Authorization

Does the organization ensure Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) are officially authorized prior to "go live" in a production environment?

### IAO-15 — Control Assurance Automation (CAA) Automation

Does the organization utilize Control Assurance Automation (CAA) engineering practices, pipelines and tooling to automate applicable Control Validation Testing (CVT) through:
 (1) Machine-executable tests; and
 (2) Automated evidence collection and evaluation?

### MNT-01 — Maintenance Policy

Does the organization establish a formal, documented maintenance policy that:
 (1) Conveys executive management's intent;
 (2) Provides organizational direction and expected behaviors;
 (3) Is reviewed at least annually; and
 (4) Is updated, as necessary, to adapt to evolving risks, threats and other changes that affect the organization?

### MNT-02 — Maintenance Operations

Does the organization develop, disseminate, review & update procedures to facilitate the implementation of maintenance controls across the enterprise?

### MNT-03 — Controlled Maintenance

Does the organization conduct controlled maintenance activities throughout the lifecycle of the Technology Asset, Application and/or Service (TAAS)?

### MNT-04 — Timely Maintenance

Does the organization obtain maintenance support and/or spare parts for Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) within a defined Recovery Time Objective (RTO)?

### MNT-05 — Preventative Maintenance

Does the organization perform preventive maintenance on critical Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS)?

### MNT-06 — Predictive Maintenance

Does the organization perform predictive maintenance on critical Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS)?

### MNT-07 — Maintenance Validation

Does the organization validate:
(1) Maintenance activities were appropriately performed according to the work order; and
(2) Applicable security, compliance and resilience controls are operational?

### MNT-08 — Maintenance Monitoring

Does the organization maintain situational awareness of the quality and reliability of systems and components through tracking maintenance activities and component failure rates?

### MNT-09 — Prevent Unauthorized Removal

Does the organization prevent or control the removal of equipment undergoing maintenance that contains organizational information?

### MNT-10 — Automated Maintenance Activities

Does the organization use automated mechanisms to schedule, conduct and document maintenance and repairs?

### MNT-10.1 — Automated Support For Predictive Maintenance

Does the organization use automated mechanisms to transfer predictive maintenance data to a computerized maintenance management system?

### MNT-11 — Maintenance Tools

Does the organization control and monitor the use of system maintenance tools?

### MNT-11.1 — Inspect Tools

Does the organization inspect maintenance tools carried into a facility by maintenance personnel for improper or unauthorized modifications?

### MNT-11.2 — Inspect Media

Does the organization check media containing diagnostic and test programs for malicious code before the media are used?

### MNT-11.3 — Restrict Tool Usage

Does the organization use automated mechanisms to restrict the use of maintenance tools to authorized maintenance personnel and/or roles?

### MNT-12 — Remote Maintenance

Does the organization authorize, monitor and control remote, non-local maintenance and diagnostic activities?

### MNT-12.1 — Remote Maintenance Notifications

Does the organization require maintenance personnel to notify affected stakeholders when remote, non-local maintenance is planned (e.g., date/time)?

### MNT-12.2 — Remote Maintenance Pre-Approval

Does the organization require maintenance personnel to obtain pre-approval and scheduling for remote, non-local maintenance sessions?

### MNT-12.3 — Remote Maintenance Disconnect Verification

Does the organization provide remote disconnect verification to ensure remote, non-local maintenance and diagnostic sessions are properly terminated?

### MNT-12.4 — Remote Maintenance Cryptographic Protection

Are cryptographic mechanisms utilized to protect the integrity and confidentiality of remote, non-local maintenance and diagnostic communications?

### MNT-12.5 — Auditing Remote Maintenance

Does the organization audit remote, non-local maintenance and diagnostic sessions, as well as review the maintenance action performed during remote maintenance sessions?

### MNT-13 — Remote Maintenance Comparable Security & Sanitization

Does the organization require Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) performing remote, non-local maintenance and/or diagnostic services implement a security capability comparable to the capability implemented on the system being serviced?

### MNT-13.1 — Separation of Maintenance Sessions

Does the organization protect maintenance sessions through replay-resistant sessions that are physically or logically separated communications paths from other network sessions?

### MNT-14 — Authorized Maintenance Personnel

Does the organization maintain a current list of authorized maintenance organizations or personnel?

### MNT-14.1 — Maintenance Personnel Without Appropriate Access

Does the organization ensure the risks associated with maintenance personnel who do not have appropriate access authorizations, clearances or formal access approvals are appropriately mitigated?

### MNT-15 — Non-System Related Maintenance

Does the organization ensure that non-escorted personnel performing non-IT maintenance activities in the physical proximity of systems have required access authorizations?

### MNT-16 — Maintain Configuration Control During Maintenance

Does the organization maintain proper physical security and configuration control over technology assets awaiting service or repair?

### MNT-17 — Field Maintenance

Does the organization securely conduct field maintenance on geographically deployed assets?

### MNT-18 — Off-Site Maintenance

Does the organization ensure off-site maintenance activities are conducted securely and the asset(s) undergoing maintenance actions are secured during physical transfer and storage while off-site?

### MDM-01 — Mobile Device Management Policy

Does the organization establish a formal, documented mobile device management policy that:
 (1) Conveys executive management's intent;
 (2) Provides organizational direction and expected behaviors;
 (3) Is reviewed at least annually; and
 (4) Is updated, as necessary, to adapt to evolving risks, threats and other changes that affect the organization?

### MDM-02 — Centralized Management Of Mobile Devices

Does the organization implement and govern Mobile Device Management (MDM) controls?

### MDM-03 — Restricting Access To Authorized Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS)

Does the organization restrict the connectivity of unauthorized mobile devices from communicating with organizational Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS)?

### MDM-04 — Full Device & Container-Based Encryption

Are cryptographic mechanisms utilized to protect the confidentiality and integrity of information on mobile devices through full-device or container encryption?

### MDM-05 — Separate Mobile Device Profiles

Does the organization enforce a separate device workspace on applicable mobile devices to separate work-related and personal-related applications and data?

### MDM-06 — Personally-Owned Mobile Devices

Does the organization restrict the connection of personally-owned, mobile devices to organizational Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS)?

### MDM-07 — Organization-Owned Mobile Devices

Does the organization prohibit the installation of non-approved applications or approved applications not obtained through the organization-approved application store?

### MDM-08 — Mobile Device Geofencing

Does the organization restrict the functionality of mobile devices based on geographic location?

### MDM-09 — Remote Purging

Does the organization remotely purge selected information from mobile devices?

### MDM-10 — Mobile Device Tampering

Does the organization protect mobile devices from tampering through inspecting devices returning from locations that the organization deems to be of significant risk, prior to the device being connected to its network?

### NET-01 — Network Security Policy

Does the organization establish a formal, documented network security policy that:
 (1) Conveys executive management's intent;
 (2) Provides organizational direction and expected behaviors;
 (3) Is reviewed at least annually; and
 (4) Is updated, as necessary, to adapt to evolving risks, threats and other changes that affect the organization?

### NET-02 — Network Security Controls (NSC)

Does the organization develop, govern & update procedures to facilitate the implementation of Network Security Controls (NSC)?

### NET-03 — Boundary Protection

Does the organization monitor and control communications at the external network boundary and at key internal boundaries within the network?

### NET-03.1 — Limit Network Connections

Does the organization limit the number of concurrent external network connections to its Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS)?

### NET-03.2 — External Telecommunications Services

Does the organization maintain a managed interface for each external telecommunication service that protects the confidentiality and integrity of the information being transmitted across each interface?

### NET-03.3 — Prevent Discovery of Internal Information

Does the organization prevent the public disclosure of internal network information?

### NET-03.4 — Direct Internet Access Restrictions

Does the organization prohibit, or strictly-control, Internet access from sensitive and/or regulated data enclaves (secure zones)?

### NET-03.5 — Prevent Unauthorized Exfiltration

Does the organization use automated mechanisms to prevent the unauthorized exfiltration of sensitive and/or regulated data across managed interfaces?

### NET-03.6 — Protocol Compliance Enforcement

Does the organization use automated mechanisms to ensure network traffic complies with Internet Engineering Task Force (IETF) protocol specifications?

### NET-03.7 — Domain Name Verification

Does the organization ensure that domain name lookups, whether for internal or external domains, are validated according to Domain Name System Security Extensions (DNSSEC)?

### NET-03.8 — Bandwidth Control

Does the organization implement bandwidth control technologies to limit the amount of bandwidth used by categories of domains that are bandwidth-intensive?

### NET-03.9 — Internet Address Denylisting

Does the organization implement Internet address denylisting protections that blocks traffic received from or destined to a denylisted Internet address?

### NET-03.10 — Certificate Denylisting

Does the organization prevent communication with Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) that use a set of known bad certificates?

### NET-03.11 — Content Disarm and Reconstruction (CDR)

Does the organization use automated mechanisms to implement Content Disarm and Reconstruction (CDR) to remove active content from files traversing trust boundaries, resulting in reconstructed content containing only known safe elements?

### NET-03.12 — Network Processing Rules For Personal Data (PD)

Does the organization apply network-based processing rules to data elements of Personal Data (PD)?

### NET-03.13 — Split Tunneling

Does the organization prevent split tunneling for remote devices unless the split tunnel is securely provisioned using organization-defined safeguards?

### NET-04 — Data Flow Enforcement – Access Control Lists (ACLs)

Does the organization implement and govern Access Control Lists (ACLs) to provide data flow enforcement that explicitly restrict network traffic to only what is authorized?

### NET-04.1 — Deny Traffic by Default & Allow Traffic by Exception

Does the organization configure firewall and router configurations to deny network traffic by default and allow network traffic by exception (e.g., deny all and permit by exception)?

### NET-04.2 — Human Reviews

Does the organization enforce the use of human reviews for Access Control Lists (ACLs) and similar rulesets on a routine basis?

### NET-05 — Interconnection Security Agreements (ISAs)

Does the organization authorize connections from systems to other systems using Interconnection Security Agreements (ISAs), or similar methods, that document, for each interconnection:
(1) Interface characteristics;
(2) Security, compliance and resilience requirements; and;
(3) The nature of the information communicated?

### NET-05.1 — External System Connections

Does the organization prohibit the direct connection of a sensitive system to an external network without the use of an organization-defined boundary protection device?

### NET-05.2 — Internal System Connections

Does the organization control internal system connections through authorizing internal connections of systems and documenting, for each internal connection, the interface characteristics, security requirements and the nature of the information communicated?

### NET-06 — Network Segmentation (macrosegmentation)

Does the organization implement network segmentation within network architectures to isolate Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) from other network resources?

### NET-06.1 — Security Management Subnets

Does the organization implement security management subnets to isolate security tools and support components from other internal system components by implementing separate subnetworks with managed interfaces to other components of the system?

### NET-07 — Out-of-Band Channels

Does the organization utilize out-of-band channels for the electronic transmission of information and/or the physical shipment of system components or devices to authorized individuals?

### NET-08 — Separate Subnets To Isolate Functions

Does the organization implement physically or logically separate subnetworks to isolate organization-defined Technology Assets, Applications, Services and/or Data (TAASD)?

### NET-08.1 — Sensitive / Regulated Data Enclave (Secure Zone)

Does the organization implement segmentation controls to restrict inbound and outbound connectivity for sensitive and/or regulated data enclaves (secure zones)?

### NET-08.2 — Segregation From Enterprise Services

Does the organization isolate sensitive and/or regulated data enclaves (secure zones) from corporate-provided IT resources by providing enclave-specific IT services (e.g., directory services, DNS, NTP, ITAM, antimalware and patch management) to those isolated network segments?

### NET-09 — Network Device Plane Segmentation

Does the organization use automated mechanisms to separate network appliance functions (e.g., management, control and data planes) to prevent ordinary traffic from accessing functions that:
(1) Manage network appliances; and/or
(2) Affect network operations?

### NET-10 — Virtual Local Area Network (VLAN) Separation

Does the organization enable Virtual Local Area Networks (VLANs) to limit the ability of devices on a network to directly communicate with other devices on the subnet and limit an attacker's ability to laterally move to compromise neighboring systems?

### NET-11 — Microsegmentation

Does the organization use automated mechanisms to enable microsegmentation, either physically or virtually, to divide the network according to application and data workflows communications needs?

### NET-12 — Software Defined Networking (SDN)

Does the organization use automated mechanisms to enable dynamic, policy-driven network segmentation, access controls and traffic management with a Software Defined Networking (SDN) architecture?

### NET-13 — Domain Name Service (DNS) Resolution

Does the organization ensure Domain Name Service (DNS) resolution is designed, implemented and managed to protect the security of name / address resolution?

### NET-13.1 — Architecture & Provisioning for Name / Address Resolution Service

Does the organization ensure systems that collectively provide Domain Name Service (DNS) resolution service are fault-tolerant and implement internal/external role separation?

### NET-13.2 — Secure Name / Address Resolution Service (Recursive or Caching Resolver)

Does the organization perform data origin authentication and data integrity verification on the Domain Name Service (DNS) resolution responses received from authoritative sources when requested by client systems?

### NET-13.3 — Domain Registrar Security

Does the organization lock the domain name registrar to prevent a denial of service caused by unauthorized deletion, transfer or other unauthorized modification of a domain's registration details?

### NET-14 — Zero Trust Architecture (ZTA)

Does the organization treat all users and devices as potential threats and prevent access to data and resources until the users can be properly authenticated and their access authorized?

### NET-15 — Policy Decision Point (PDP)

Does the organization use automated mechanisms to evaluate access requests against established criteria to dynamically and uniformly enforce access rights and permissions?

### NET-16 — Network Access Control (NAC)

Does the organization use automated mechanisms to employ Network Access Control (NAC), or a similar technology, which is capable of detecting unauthorized devices and disable network access to those unauthorized devices?

### NET-17 — DNS & Content Filtering

Does the organization force Internet-bound network traffic through a proxy device (e.g., Policy Enforcement Point (PEP)) for URL content filtering and DNS filtering to limit a user's ability to connect to dangerous or prohibited Internet sites?

### NET-18 — Authenticated Proxy

Does the organization force systems and processes to authenticate Internet-bound traffic with a proxy to enable user, group and/or location-aware security controls?

### NET-18.1 — Route Internal Traffic to Proxy Servers

Does the organization route internal communications traffic to external networks through organization-approved proxy servers at managed interfaces?

### NET-18.2 — Route Privileged Network Access

Does the organization use automated mechanisms to route networked, privileged accesses through a dedicated, managed interface for purposes of access control and auditing?

### NET-19 — Application Proxy

Does the organization terminate, inspect, control and reinitiate application traffic, regardless of the user's location or the security posture of the surrounding network?

### NET-20 — Visibility of Encrypted Communications

Does the organization configure the proxy to make encrypted communications traffic visible to monitoring tools and mechanisms?

### NET-20.1 — Content Check for Encrypted Data

Does the organization prevent encrypted data from bypassing content-checking mechanisms?

### NET-21 — Denial of Service (DoS) Protection

Does the organization use automated mechanisms to protect against or limit the effects of denial of service attacks?

### NET-22 — Guest Networks

Does the organization implement and manage a secure guest network?

### NET-23 — Intranets

Does the organization establish trust relationships with other organizations owning, operating, and/or maintaining intranet systems, allowing authorized individuals to:
(1) Access the intranet from external Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS); and
(2) Process, store, and/or transmit organization-controlled information using the external TAAS?

### NET-24 — Wireless Networking

Does the organization control authorized wireless usage and monitor for unauthorized wireless access?

### NET-24.1 — Wireless Networking Authentication & Encryption

Does the organization secure Wi-Fi (e.g., IEEE 802.11) and prevent unauthorized access by:
 (1) Authenticating devices trying to connect; and
 (2) Encrypting transmitted data?

### NET-24.2 — Wireless Boundaries

Does the organization confine wireless communications to organization-controlled boundaries?

### NET-25 — Rogue Wireless Detection

Does the organization test for the presence of Wireless Access Points (WAPs) and identify all authorized and unauthorized WAPs within the facility(ies)?

### NET-26 — Remote Access
