Does the organization configure systems that process, store or transmit sensitive and/or regulated data to notify the user, upon successful logon, of the number of unsuccessful logon attempts since the last successful logon?

### SEA-30 — Clock Synchronization

Does the organization utilize time-synchronization technology to synchronize all critical system clocks?

### SEA-31 — Application Container

Does the organization utilize an application container (virtualization approach) to isolate to a known set of dependencies, access methods and interfaces?

### SEA-32 — Privileged Environments

Does the organization prevent privileged operating environments from existing within unprivileged operating environments, including physical or virtual deployments of Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS)?

### OPS-01 — Security Operations Policy

Does the organization establish a formal, documented security operations policy that:
 (1) Conveys executive management's intent;
 (2) Provides organizational direction and expected behaviors;
 (3) Is reviewed at least annually; and
 (4) Is updated, as necessary, to adapt to evolving risks, threats and other changes that affect the organization?

### OPS-02 — Operations Security

Does the organization facilitate the implementation of operational security controls?

### OPS-03 — Security Concept Of Operations (CONOPS)

Does the organization develop a security Concept of Operations (CONOPS), or a similarly-defined plan for achieving cybersecurity objectives, that documents management, operational and technical measures implemented to apply defense-in-depth techniques that is communicated to all appropriate stakeholders?

### OPS-04 — Standardized Operating Procedures (SOP)

Does the organization identify and document Standardized Operating Procedures (SOP), or similar documentation, to enable the proper execution of day-to-day / assigned tasks?

### OPS-04.1 — System Administrative Processes

Does the organization develop, implement and govern system administration processes, with corresponding Standardized Operating Procedures (SOP), for operating and maintaining Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS)?

### OPS-04.2 — Database Administrative Processes

Does the organization develop, implement and govern database management processes, with corresponding Standardized Operating Procedures (SOP), for operating and maintaining databases?

### OPS-05 — Service Delivery (Business Process Support)

Does the organization define supporting business processes and implement appropriate governance and service management to ensure appropriate planning, delivery and support of its technology capabilities supporting business functions, workforce, and/or customers based on industry-recognized standards to achieve the specific goals of the process area?

### OPS-06 — Secure Practices Guidelines

Does the organization provide guidelines and recommendations for the secure use of Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) to assist in the configuration, installation and use of the product and/or service?

### OPS-07 — Security Operations Center (SOC)

Does the organization establish and maintain a Security Operations Center (SOC) that facilitates a 24x7 response capability?

### OPS-08 — Security Orchestration, Automation, and Response (SOAR)

Does the organization utilize Security Orchestration, Automation and Response (SOAR) tools to define, prioritize and automate the response to security incidents?

### OPS-09 — Shadow Information Technology Detection

Does the organization detect the presence of unauthorized Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) in use?

### SAT-01 — Security Awareness & Training Policy

Does the organization establish a formal, documented security awareness and training policy that:
 (1) Conveys executive management's intent;
 (2) Provides organizational direction and expected behaviors;
 (3) Is reviewed at least annually; and
 (4) Is updated, as necessary, to adapt to evolving risks, threats and other changes that affect the organization?

### SAT-02 — Security, Compliance & Resilience-Minded Workforce

Does the organization facilitate the implementation of security workforce development and awareness controls?

### SAT-03 — Maintaining Workforce Development Relevancy

Does the organization periodically review security workforce development and awareness training to account for changes to:
(1) Organizational policies, standards and procedures;
(2) Assigned roles and responsibilities;
(3) Relevant threats and risks; and
(4) Technological developments?

### SAT-04 — Security, Compliance & Resilience Awareness Training

Does the organization provide all employees and contractors appropriate security, compliance and resilience awareness education and training that is relevant for their job function?

### SAT-04.1 — Simulated Cyber Attack Scenario Training

Does the organization include simulated actual cyber-attacks through practical exercises that are aligned with current threat scenarios?

### SAT-05 — Role-Based Security, Compliance & Resilience Training

Does the organization provide role-based security, compliance and resilience-related training:
(1) Before authorizing access to the system or performing assigned duties;
(2) When required by system changes; and
(3) Annually thereafter?

### SAT-05.1 — Sensitive / Regulated Data Storage, Handling & Processing

Does the organization ensure that every user accessing a system processing, storing or transmitting sensitive and/or regulated data is formally trained in data handling requirements?

### SAT-05.2 — Privileged User Training

Does the organization provide specific training for privileged users to ensure privileged users understand their unique roles and responsibilities?

### SAT-05.3 — AI & Autonomous Technologies Risk Management Training

Does the organization ensure personnel and external stakeholders are provided with position-specific risk management training for Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Autonomous Technologies (AAT)?

### SAT-05.4 — Vendor-Specific Security, Compliance & Resilience Training

Does the organization incorporate vendor-specific security, compliance and resilience training in support of new technology initiatives?

### SAT-06 — Cyber Threat Environment Situational Awareness

Does the organization provide role-based security, compliance and resilience awareness training that is current and relevant to the cyber threats that users might encounter in day-to-day business operations?

### SAT-06.1 — Social Engineering & Mining

Does the organization include awareness training on recognizing and reporting potential and actual instances of social engineering and social mining?

### SAT-06.2 — Suspicious Communications & Anomalous System Behavior

Does the organization provide training to personnel on organization-defined indicators of malware to recognize suspicious communications and anomalous behavior?

### SAT-06.3 — Counterintelligence Training

Does the organization provide specialized counterintelligence awareness training that enables personnel to collect, interpret and act upon a range of data sources that may signal the presence of a hostile actor?

### SAT-06.4 — Anti-Counterfeit Training

Does the organization train personnel to detect counterfeit system components, including hardware, software and firmware?

### SAT-06.5 — Quantum Security Awareness

Does the organization deliver differentiated quantum security awareness and training content to:
(1) General workforce;
(2) Technical roles; and
(3) Leadership roles?

### SAT-07 — Continuing Professional Education (CPE) - Security, Compliance & Resilience Personnel

Does the organization ensure security, compliance and resilience personnel receive Continuing Professional Education (CPE) training to maintain currency and proficiency with industry-recognized secure practices that are pertinent to their assigned roles and responsibilities?

### SAT-08 — Continuing Professional Education (CPE) - DevOps Personnel

Does the organization ensure application development and operations (DevOps) personnel receive Continuing Professional Education (CPE) training on Secure Software Development Practices (SSDP) to appropriately address evolving threats?

### SAT-09 — Practical Security Training Exercises

Does the organization include practical exercises in security, compliance and resilience training that reinforce training objectives?

### SAT-10 — Security, Compliance & Resilience Training Records

Does the organization document, retain and monitor individual training activities, including:
(1) Initial security, compliance and resilience awareness training;
(2) Recurring awareness training; and
(3) Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS)-specific training?

### SAT-11 — Training Feedback

Does the organization:
(1) Monitor individual training results; and
(2) Report findings to stakeholders?

### SAT-12 — Security, Compliance & Resilience Knowledge Sharing

Does the organization improve knowledge sharing across security, compliance and resilience personnel allowing for:
(1) Efficient operations; and
(2) Rapid and effective response to incidents?

### TDA-01 — Technology Development & Acquisition Policy

Does the organization establish a formal, documented technology development and acquisition policy that:
 (1) Conveys executive management's intent;
 (2) Provides organizational direction and expected behaviors;
 (3) Is reviewed at least annually; and
 (4) Is updated, as necessary, to adapt to evolving risks, threats and other changes that affect the organization?

### TDA-02 — Technology Development & Acquisition

Does the organization facilitate the implementation of tailored development and acquisition strategies, contract tools and procurement methods to meet unique business needs?

### TDA-03 — Development Methods, Techniques & Processes

Does the organization require software developers to ensure that their software development processes employ industry-recognized secure practices for secure programming, engineering methods, quality control processes and validation techniques to minimize flawed and/or malformed software?

### TDA-03.1 — Software Assurance Maturity Model (SAMM)

Does the organization utilize a Software Assurance Maturity Model (SAMM) to govern a secure development lifecycle for the development of Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS)?

### TDA-03.2 — Secure Settings By Default

Does the organization implement secure configuration settings by default to reduce the likelihood of Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) being deployed with weak security settings that would put the TAAS at a greater risk of compromise?

### TDA-04 — Developer Architecture & Design

Does the organization require the developers of Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) to produce a design specification and security architecture that:
(1) Is consistent with and supportive of its security architecture which is established within and is an integrated part of its enterprise architecture;
(2) Accurately and completely describes the required security functionality and the allocation of security, compliance and resilience controls among physical and logical components; and
(3) Expresses how individual security functions, mechanisms and services work together to provide required security capabilities and a unified approach to protection?

### TDA-04.1 — Programming Language Selection

Does the organization:
(1) Define organization-approved programming language(s) for software development; and
(2) Document the justification for selection decisions?

### TDA-05 — Secure Software Development Practices (SSDP)

Does the organization develop applications based on Secure Software Development Practices (SSDP)?

### TDA-05.1 — Criticality Analysis During Development

Does the organization require the developer of the Technology Asset, Application and/or Service (TAAS) to perform a criticality analysis at organization-defined decision points in the Secure Development Life Cycle (SDLC)?

### TDA-05.2 — Threat Modeling

Does the organization perform threat modelling and other secure design techniques, to ensure that threats to software and solutions are identified and accounted for?

### TDA-05.3 — Supporting Toolchain

Does the organization use automated mechanisms to improve the accuracy, consistency and comprehensiveness of secure practices throughout the asset's lifecycle?

### TDA-05.4 — Software Design Review

Does the organization have an independent review of the software design to validate:
(1) Applicable security, compliance and resilience requirements are met; and
(2) Identified risks are remediated?

### TDA-05.5 — Software Design Root Cause Analysis (RCA)

Does the organization assess software design processes that includes:
(1) Conducting Root Cause Analysis (RCA) to identify the underlying causes of issues or failures;
(2) Developing actions to address the root cause of the issue or failure; and
(3) Implementing the actions and monitoring the implementation for effectiveness?

### TDA-06 — Product Management

Does the organization design and implement product management processes to proactively govern the design, development and production of Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) across the System Development Life Cycle (SDLC) to:
(1) Improve functionality;
(2) Enhance security and resiliency capabilities;
(3) Correct security deficiencies; and
(4) Conform with applicable statutory, regulatory and/or contractual obligations?

### TDA-06.1 — Product Conformity Governance

Does the organization ensure developed Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) conform to applicable statutory and regulatory requirements, based on the product's and/or service's:
(1) Use case(s); and
(2) Geographic markets?

### TDA-06.2 — Continuous Monitoring Plan

Does the organization require the developers of Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) to produce a plan for the continuous monitoring of security, compliance and/or resilience control effectiveness?

### TDA-06.3 — Ongoing Product Security Support

Does the organization deliver security updates to Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS), where applicable, through:
(1) Automatic updates; and
(2) Notification of available updates to affected users?

### TDA-06.4 — Integrity Mechanisms for Software / Firmware Updates

Does the organization utilize integrity validation mechanisms for security updates?

### TDA-06.5 — Software Release Integrity Verification

Does the organization publish integrity verification information for software releases?

### TDA-06.6 — Information Assurance Enabled Products

Does the organization limit the use of commercially-provided Information Assurance (IA) and IA-enabled IT products to those products that have been successfully evaluated against a National Information Assurance partnership (NIAP)-approved Protection Profile or the cryptographic module is FIPS-validated or NSA-approved?

### TDA-07 — Disclosure of Vulnerabilities

Does the organization disclose information about vulnerabilities to relevant stakeholders, including:
(1) A description of the vulnerability(ies);
(2) Affected product(s) and/or service(s);
(3) Potential impact of the vulnerability(ies);
(4) Severity of the vulnerability(ies); and
(5) Guidance to remediate the vulnerability(ies)?

### TDA-07.1 — Reporting Exploitable Vulnerabilities

Does the organization notify applicable stakeholders about potentially exploitable vulnerabilities in organization-developed Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS), as required by statutory, regulatory and/or contractual obligations?

### TDA-08 — Technical Documentation Artifacts

Does the organization generate appropriate technical documentation artifacts for Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) in sufficient detail to demonstrate conformity with applicable statutory, regulatory and contractual compliance requirements?

### TDA-08.1 — Product-Specific Risk Assessment Artifacts

Does the organization include a detailed cybersecurity risk assessment in the technical documentation for Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) to demonstrate applicable risks in approved use cases?

### TDA-08.2 — Functional Properties

Does the organization require software developers to provide information describing the functional properties of the security, compliance and resilience controls to be utilized within Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) in sufficient detail to permit analysis and testing of the controls?

### TDA-08.3 — Administrator Documentation

Does the organization obtain, protect and distribute administrator documentation for Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) that describe:
 (1) Secure configuration, installation and operation of the TAAS;
 (2) Effective use and maintenance of security features/functions; and
 (3) Known vulnerabilities regarding configuration and use of administrative (e.g., privileged) functions?

### TDA-08.4 — Identification & Justification of Ports, Protocols & Services

Does the organization require process owners to identify, document and justify the business need for the ports, protocols and other services necessary to operate their technology solutions?

### TDA-08.5 — Products With Digital Elements

Does the organization categorize applicable security and resiliency requirements for products and/or services with digital elements?

### TDA-09 — Product Tampering and Counterfeiting (PTC)

Does the organization maintain awareness of component authenticity by developing and implementing Product Tampering and Counterfeiting (PTC) practices that include the means to detect and prevent counterfeit components?

### TDA-10 — Customized Development of Critical Components

Does the organization custom-develop critical system components, when Commercial Off The Shelf (COTS) solutions are unavailable?

### TDA-11 — DevSecOps

Does the organization integrate security, compliance and resilience into Development, Security and Operations (DevSecOps) to prioritize secure practices throughout the Software Development Lifecycle (SDLC)?

### TDA-11.1 — Minimum Viable Product (MVP) Security Requirements

Does the organization design, develop and produce Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) in such a way that risk-based technical and functional specifications ensure Minimum Viable Product (MVP) criteria establish an appropriate level of security and resiliency based on applicable risks and threats?

### TDA-11.2 — Insecure Ports, Protocols & Services

Does the organization mitigate the risk associated with the use of insecure ports, protocols and services necessary to operate technology solutions?

### TDA-11.3 — Commercial Off-The-Shelf (COTS) Security Solutions

Does the organization utilize only Commercial Off-the-Shelf (COTS) security products?

### TDA-11.4 — Logging Syntax

Does the organization require system developers to use an industry-defined secure logging format to generate event logs for specified event types at organization-defined level of detail?

### TDA-11.5 — Physical Diagnostic & Test Interfaces

Does the organization secure physical diagnostic and test interfaces to prevent misuse?

### TDA-11.6 — Diagnostic & Test Interface Monitoring

Does the organization enable endpoint devices to log events and generate alerts for attempts to access diagnostic and test interfaces?

### TDA-12 — Input Data Validation

Does the organization check the validity of information inputs?

### TDA-12.1 — Error Handling

Does the organization handle error conditions by:
 (1) Identifying potentially security-relevant error conditions;
 (2) Generating error messages that provide information necessary for corrective actions without revealing sensitive or potentially harmful information in error logs and administrative messages that could be exploited; and
 (3) Revealing error messages only to authorized personnel?

### TDA-12.2 — Designated Roles To View Error Messages

Does the organization:
(1) Define personnel and/or role(s) authorized to receive security-relevant error messages; and
(2) Restrict access to error messages to authorized personnel and/or role(s)?

### TDA-13 — Minimizing Attack Surfaces

Does the organization minimize the attack surface of Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) by reasonably mitigating known exploitable vulnerabilities?

### TDA-13.1 — Pre-Established Secure Configurations

Does the organization ensure vendors / manufacturers:
 (1) Deliver the Technology Asset, Application and/or Service (TAAS) with a pre-established, secure configuration implemented; and
 (2) Use the pre-established, secure configuration as the default for any subsequent TAAS reinstallation or upgrade?

### TDA-13.2 — Malware Testing Prior to Release

Does the organization utilize at least one(1) malware detection tool to identify if any known malware exists in the final binaries of the product or security update?

### TDA-14 — Product Testing & Reviews

Does the organization regularly review Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) for an appropriate level of security and resiliency based on applicable risks and threats?

### TDA-14.1 — Security, Compliance & Resilience Representatives For Product Changes

Does the organization include appropriate security, compliance and resilience representatives in the product feature and/or functionality change control review process?

### TDA-15 — Secure Development Environments

Does the organization maintain a segmented development network to ensure a secure development environment?

### TDA-15.1 — Separation of Development, Testing and Operational Environments

Does the organization manage separate development, testing and operational environments to reduce the risks of unauthorized access or changes to the operational environment and to ensure no impact to production Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS)?

### TDA-15.2 — Secure Migration Practices

Does the organization ensure secure migration practices purge Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) of test/development/staging data and accounts before it is migrated into a production environment?

### TDA-16 — Library Privileges

Does the organization restrict software library privileges to those individuals with a pertinent business need for access?

### TDA-16.1 — Access to Program Source Code

Does the organization limit privileges to change software resident within software libraries?

### TDA-16.2 — Approved Code

Does the organization govern the approval of binaries and code for production use?

### TDA-16.3 — Archiving Software Releases

Does the organization archive software releases and all of their components (e.g., code, package files, third-party libraries and documentation) to maintain integrity verification information?

### TDA-16.4 — Software Escrow

Does the organization escrow source code and supporting documentation to ensure software availability in the event the software provider goes out of business or is unable to provide support?

### TDA-17 — Security, Compliance & Resilience Testing Throughout Development

Does the organization require system developers/integrators consult with security, compliance and/or resilience personnel to:
(1) Create and implement a Security Testing and Evaluation (ST&E) plan, or similar capability;
(2) Implement a verifiable flaw remediation process to correct weaknesses and deficiencies identified during the control testing and evaluation process; and
(3) Document the results?

### TDA-17.1 — Static Code Analysis

Does the organization require the developers of Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) to employ static code analysis tools to identify and remediate common flaws and document the results of the analysis?

### TDA-17.2 — Dynamic Code Analysis

Does the organization require the developers of Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) to employ dynamic code analysis tools to identify and remediate common flaws and document the results of the analysis?

### TDA-17.3 — Malformed Input Testing

Does the organization utilize testing methods to ensure Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) continue to operate as intended when subject to invalid or unexpected inputs on its interfaces?

### TDA-17.4 — Application Penetration Testing

Does the organization perform application-level penetration testing of custom-made Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS)?

### TDA-17.5 — Manual Code Review

Does the organization require the developers of Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) to employ a manual code review process to identify and remediate unique flaws that require knowledge of the application's requirements and design?

### TDA-18 — Use of Live Data

Does the organization approve, document and control the use of live data in development and test environments?

### TDA-18.1 — Test Data Integrity

Does the organization ensure the integrity of test data through existing security, compliance and resilience controls?

### TDA-19 — Developer Screening

Does the organization ensure that the developers of Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) have the requisite skillset and appropriate access authorizations?

### TDA-19.1 — Developer Knowledge & Skills Register

Does the organization maintain a cybersecurity knowledge and skills register for developers?

### TDA-19.2 — Requisite Developer Training

Does the organization ensure developers of Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) who lack the requisite skillset receive suitable training on Secure Software Development Practices (SSDP)?

### TDA-20 — Developer Configuration Management

Does the organization require system developers and integrators to perform configuration management during system design, development, implementation and operation?

### TDA-20.1 — Developer Threat Analysis & Flaw Remediation

Does the organization require system developers and integrators to develop and implement an ongoing Security Testing and Evaluation (ST&E) plan, or similar process, to objectively identify and remediate vulnerabilities prior to release to production?

### TDA-20.2 — Developer-Provided Training

Does the organization require the developers of Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) to provide training on the correct use and operation of the Technology Asset, Application and/or Service (TAAS)?

### TDA-20.3 — Software / Firmware Integrity Verification

Does the organization require developers of Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) to enable integrity verification of software and firmware components?

### TDA-20.4 — Hardware Integrity Verification

Does the organization require developers of Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) to enable integrity verification of hardware components?

### TDA-21 — Bills of Material (BOMs)

Does the organization generate, or obtain, Bills of Material (BOMs) that identify the components comprising Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS), including component versions and supplier information?

### TDA-21.1 — Cryptographic Bill of Materials (CBOM)

Does the organization develop and maintain a Cryptographic Bill of Materials (CBOM) by analyzing its cryptographic architecture, including:
(1) Hardware;
(2) Firmware;
(3) Software modules; and
(4) Communication protocols?

### TDA-21.2 — Hardware Bill of Materials (HBOM)

Does the organization generate, or obtain, a Hardware Bill of Materials (HBOM) for Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) that lists hardware components in use, including component identifiers, versions and suppliers?

### TDA-21.3 — Indentured Bill of Materials (IBOM)

Does the organization generate, or obtain, an Indentured Bill of Materials (IBOM) that documents the hierarchical relationship between assemblies, sub-assemblies and components comprising Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS)?

### TDA-21.4 — Software Bill of Materials (SBOM)

Does the organization generate, or obtain, a Software Bill of Materials (SBOM) for Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) that lists software packages in use, including versions and applicable licenses?

### TPM-01 — Third-Party Management Policy

Does the organization establish a formal, documented third-party management policy that:
 (1) Conveys executive management's intent;
 (2) Provides organizational direction and expected behaviors;
 (3) Is reviewed at least annually; and
 (4) Is updated, as necessary, to adapt to evolving risks, threats and other changes that affect the organization?

### TPM-02 — Third-Party Management

Does the organization facilitate the implementation of third-party management controls?

### TPM-03 — Acquisition Strategies, Tools & Methods

Does the organization utilize tailored acquisition strategies, contract tools and procurement methods for the purchase of unique Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS)?

### TPM-04 — Supply Chain Risk Management (SCRM)

Does the organization:
(1) Evaluate security risks and threats associated with Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) supply chains; and
(2) Take appropriate remediation actions to minimize its exposure to those risks and threats, as necessary?

### TPM-04.1 — Processes To Address Weaknesses or Deficiencies

Does the organization address identified weaknesses or deficiencies in the security of the supply chain?

### TPM-04.2 — Limit Potential Harm

Does the organization utilize security safeguards to limit harm from potential adversaries who identify and target its supply chain?

### TPM-05 — Security, Compliance & Resilience Outsourcing Limitations

Does the organization ensure third-parties involved in developing, implementing and/or maintaining Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) provide assurance of internal oversight capabilities that demonstrate:
(1) Governance of internal controls;
(2) Risk management, including analysis and mitigation activities; and
(3) Compliance with applicable laws, regulations and contractual obligations?

### TPM-05.1 — Outsourcing Non-Essential Functions or Services

Does the organization identify non-essential functions or services that are capable of being outsourced to external service providers and align with its enterprise architecture and security standards?

### TPM-06 — Supplier Diversity

Does the organization obtain security, compliance and resilience technologies from different suppliers to minimize supply chain risk?

### TPM-07 — Adequate Supply

Does the organization develop and implement a spare parts strategy to ensure that an adequate supply of critical components is available to meet operational needs?

### TPM-08 — Third-Party Inventories

Does the organization maintain a current, accurate and complete list of External Service Providers (ESPs) that can potentially impact the Confidentiality, Integrity, Availability and/or Safety (CIAS) of its Technology Assets, Applications, Services and/or Data (TAASD)?

### TPM-09 — Third-Party Criticality Assessments

Does the organization identify, prioritize and assess suppliers and partners of critical Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) using a supply chain risk assessment process relative to their importance in supporting the delivery of high-value services?

### TPM-10 — Third-Party Risk Assessments & Approvals

Does the organization conduct a risk assessment prior to the acquisition or outsourcing of technology-related Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS)?

### TPM-11 — Responsible, Accountable, Supportive, Consulted & Informed (RASCI) Matrix

Does the organization document and maintain a Responsible, Accountable, Supportive, Consulted & Informed (RASCI) matrix, or similar documentation, to delineate assignment for security, compliance and resilience controls between internal stakeholders and External Service Providers (ESPs)?

### TPM-12 — Third-Party Services

Does the organization mitigate the risks associated with third-party access to its Technology Assets, Applications, Services and/or Data (TAASD)?

### TPM-12.1 — Conflict of Interests

Does the organization ensure that the interests of external service providers are consistent with and reflect organizational interests?

### TPM-12.2 — Third-Party Processing, Storage and Service Locations

Does the organization restrict the location of information processing/storage based on business requirements?

### TPM-12.3 — Third-Party Authentication Practices

Does the organization ensure External Service Providers (ESPs) use unique authentication factors for each of its customers?

### TPM-12.4 — External Connectivity Requirements - Identification of Ports, Protocols & Services

Does the organization require External Service Providers (ESPs) to identify and document the business need for ports, protocols and other services it requires to operate its Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS)?

### TPM-13 — Third-Party Personnel Security

Does the organization control personnel security requirements including security roles and responsibilities for third-party providers?

### TPM-14 — Third-Party Contract Requirements

Does the organization require contractual requirements for applicable security, compliance and resilience requirements with third-parties, reflecting its needs to protect its Technology Assets, Applications, Services and/or Data (TAASD)?

### TPM-14.1 — Contract Flow-Down Requirements

Does the organization ensure applicable security, compliance and resilience requirements are included in contracts that flow-down to applicable sub-contractors and suppliers?

### TPM-14.2 — Provider Contingency Plan

Does the organization contractually-require external service providers to have contingency plans that meet organizational contingency requirements?

### TPM-15 — Review of Third-Party Services

Does the organization monitor, regularly review and assess External Service Providers (ESPs) for compliance with established contractual requirements for security, compliance and resilience controls?

### TPM-16 — Third-Party Scope Review

Does the organization perform recurring validation of the Responsible, Accountable, Supportive, Consulted & Informed (RASCI) matrix, or similar documentation, to ensure security, compliance and resilience control assignments accurately reflect current:
(1) Contractual obligations for the External Service Provider (ESP);
(2) Business practices;
(3) Applicable stakeholders; and
(4) Deployed Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS)?

### TPM-17 — Managing Changes To Third-Party Services

Does the organization control changes to services by suppliers, taking into account the criticality of business Technology Assets, Applications, Services and/or Data (TAASD) that are in scope by the third-party?

### TPM-18 — Third-Party Deficiency Remediation

Does the organization address weaknesses or deficiencies in supply chain elements identified during independent or organizational assessments of such elements?

### TPM-19 — Break Clauses

Does the organization include "break clauses" within contracts for failure to meet contract criteria for security, compliance and/or resilience controls?

### TPM-20 — Foreign Ownership, Control or Influence (FOCI)

Does the organization minimize risk associated with Foreign Ownership, Control or Influence (FOCI) through Supply Chain Risk Management (SCRM) practices?

### TPM-20.1 — Ownership Change Monitoring

Does the organization periodically review External Service Providers (ESP) for changes that affect Foreign Ownership, Control or Influence (FOCI)?

### TPM-20.2 — Ownership Change Provisions

Does the organization contractually impose safeguards (e.g., additional controls, access modification and contract termination) from Foreign Ownership, Control or Influence (FOCI) concerns to ensure that:
(1) Unauthorized access to sensitive and/or regulated data is prevented; and
(2) Performance of contracts is not adversely affected?

### TPM-21 — Third-Party Incident Response & Recovery Capabilities

Does the organization ensure response/recovery planning and testing are conducted with critical suppliers/providers?

### TPM-21.1 — Security Compromise Notification Agreements

Does the organization compel External Service Providers (ESPs) to provide notification of actual or potential compromises in the supply chain that can potentially affect or have adversely affected Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) that the organization utilizes?

### TPM-22 — First-Party Declaration (1PD)

Does the organization obtain a First-Party Declaration(1PD) from applicable External Service Providers (ESPs) that provides assurance of compliance with specified statutory, regulatory and contractual obligations for security, compliance and resilience controls, including any flow-down requirements to subcontractors?

### TPM-23 — Third-Party Attestation (3PA)

Does the organization obtain an attestation from an independent Third-Party Assessment Organization (3PAO) that provides assurance of conformity with specified statutory, regulatory and contractual obligations for security, compliance and resilience controls, including any flow-down requirements to contractors and subcontractors?

### TPM-24 — Terminating Third-Party Relationships

Does the organization establish, maintain and execute a documented exit strategy for applicable third-party relationships prior to the cessation of third-party services to support an orderly, secure, compliant and resilient transition to another third-party or to internally-managed services?

### TPM-24.1 — Third-Party Transition Planning

Does the organization define and document third-party transition activities, responsibilities, dependencies, milestones and timelines necessary to support an orderly cessation and transition of third-party services?

### TPM-24.2 — Technology Assets, Applications, Services and Data (TAASD) Portability

Does the organization ensure applicable Technology Assets, Applications, Services and Data (TAASD) can be securely and reliably transferred, migrated or otherwise made available to a replacement third-party or internally-managed service prior to the cessation of third-party services?

### TPM-24.3 — Technology Assets, Applications, Services and Data (TAASD) Disposition

Does the organization govern the return, transfer, retention and/or secure destruction of organizational Technology Assets, Applications, Services and Data (TAASD) held, managed or processed by third-parties upon cessation of third-party services?

### TPM-24.4 — Third-Party Access Revocation

Does the organization timely revoke third-party physical and logical access to organizational Technology Assets, Applications, Services and Data (TAASD) upon cessation of third-party services or when such access is no longer required?

### TPM-24.5 — Third-Party Knowledge & Operational Transfer

Does the organization ensure applicable knowledge, documentation, configurations, credentials, procedures and operational responsibilities are transferred to authorized personnel, a replacement third-party or internally-managed service prior to the cessation of third-party services?

### TPM-24.6 — Third-Party Exit Obligations Management

Does the organization identify and address applicable legal, regulatory, contractual, licensing, records retention and other compliance obligations associated with the cessation and transition of third-party services?

### TPM-24.7 — Third-Party Exit Contingencies

Does the organization establish contingency measures to maintain security, compliance, resilience and continuity of operations when a third-party relationship is terminated unexpectedly or the third-party is unable or unwilling to support an orderly transition?

### THR-01 — Threat Management Policy

Does the organization establish a formal, documented threat management policy that:
 (1) Conveys executive management's intent;
 (2) Provides organizational direction and expected behaviors;
 (3) Is reviewed at least annually; and
 (4) Is updated, as necessary, to adapt to evolving risks, threats and other changes that affect the organization?

### THR-02 — Threat Intelligence Program

Does the organization implement a threat intelligence program that includes a cross-organization information-sharing capability that can influence the development of the system and security architectures, selection of security solutions, monitoring, threat hunting, response and recovery activities?

### THR-03 — Dynamic Threat Awareness

Does the organization determine and maintain ongoing awareness of the current cyber threat environment?

### THR-04 — Threat Intelligence Feeds

Does the organization maintain situational awareness of vulnerabilities and evolving threats by leveraging the knowledge of attacker tactics, techniques and procedures to facilitate the implementation of preventative and compensating controls?

### THR-05 — Threat Intelligence Reporting

Does the organization utilize external threat intelligence feeds to generate and disseminate organization-specific security alerts, advisories and/or directives?

### THR-06 — Threat Catalog

Does the organization develop and keep current a catalog of applicable internal and external threats to the organization, both natural and manmade?

### THR-07 — Material Threats

Does the organization define criteria necessary to designate a threat as a material threat?

### THR-08 — Threat Analysis

Does the organization identify, assess, prioritize and document the potential impact(s) and likelihood(s) of applicable internal and external threats?

### THR-09 — Behavioral Baselining

Does the organization use automated mechanisms to establish behavioral baselines that capture information about user and entity behavior to enable dynamic threat discovery?

### THR-10 — Predictive Cyber Analytics

Does the organization employ advanced automation and analytics capabilities to predict and identify risks to Technology Assets, Applications, Services and/or Data (TAASD)?

### THR-11 — Indicators of Exposure (IOE)

Does the organization develop Indicators of Exposure (IOE) to understand the potential attack vectors that attackers could use to attack the organization?

### THR-12 — Vulnerability Disclosure Program (VDP)

Does the organization establish a Vulnerability Disclosure Program (VDP) to assist with the secure development and maintenance of Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) that receives unsolicited input from the public about vulnerabilities in organizational TAAS?

### THR-12.1 — Security Disclosure Contact Information

Does the organization enable public submissions of discovered or potential security vulnerabilities?

### THR-13 — Threat Hunting

Does the organization perform cyber threat hunting that uses Indicators of Compromise (IoC) to detect, track and disrupt threats that evade existing security controls?

### THR-14 — Tainting

Does the organization embed false data or steganographic data in files to enable the organization to determine if data has been exfiltrated and provide a means to identify the individual(s) involved?

### THR-15 — Insider Threat Program

Does the organization implement an insider threat program that includes a cross-discipline insider threat incident handling team?

### THR-16 — Insider Threat Awareness

Does the organization utilize security awareness training on recognizing and reporting potential indicators of insider threat?

### VPM-01 — Vulnerability & Patch Management Policy

Does the organization establish a formal, documented vulnerability and patch management policy that:
 (1) Conveys executive management's intent;
 (2) Provides organizational direction and expected behaviors;
 (3) Is reviewed at least annually; and
 (4) Is updated, as necessary, to adapt to evolving risks, threats and other changes that affect the organization?

### VPM-02 — Vulnerability & Patch Management Program (VPMP)

Does the organization facilitate the implementation and monitoring of vulnerability management controls?

### VPM-03 — Attack Surface Scope

Does the organization define and manage the scope for its attack surface management activities?

### VPM-04 — Vulnerability Exploitation Analysis

Does the organization identify, assess, prioritize and document the potential impact(s) and likelihood(s) of applicable internal and external threats exploiting known vulnerabilities?

### VPM-05 — Vulnerability Ranking

Does the organization identify and assign a risk ranking to newly discovered security vulnerabilities using reputable outside sources for security vulnerability information?

### VPM-06 — Vulnerability Remediation Process

Does the organization ensure that vulnerabilities are properly identified, tracked and remediated?

### VPM-06.1 — Centralized Management of Flaw Remediation Processes

Does the organization centrally-manage the flaw remediation process?

### VPM-06.2 — Continuous Vulnerability Remediation Activities

Does the organization address new threats and vulnerabilities on an ongoing basis and ensure assets are protected against known attacks?

### VPM-06.3 — Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) Mitigations

Does the organization prioritize remediation and mitigation of Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) by:
(1) Reducing or removing public exposure to exploitation; and
(2) Expediting patch deployment actions?

### VPM-07 — Time To Remediate / Benchmarks For Corrective Action

Does the organization track the effectiveness of remediation operations through metrics reporting?

### VPM-08 — Software & Firmware Patching

Does the organization conduct software patching for all deployed Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS), including firmware?

### VPM-08.1 — Automated Software & Firmware Updates

Does the organization use automated mechanisms to install the latest stable versions of security-relevant software and firmware updates?

### VPM-08.2 — Software Patch Integrity

Does the organization ensure software and/or firmware patches are:
(1) Obtained from trusted sources; and
(2) Checked for integrity?

### VPM-08.3 — Automated Remediation Status

Does the organization use automated mechanisms to determine the state of system components with regard to flaw remediation?

### VPM-09 — Deferred Patching Decisions

Does the organization facilitate the deferral of software and/or firmware patches when the disadvantages of applying the patch outweighs the benefits?

### VPM-10 — Pre-Deployment Patch Testing

Does the organization perform due diligence on software and/or firmware update stability by conducting pre-production testing in a non-production environment?

### VPM-11 — Out-of-Cycle Patching

Does the organization perform out-of-cycle software and/or firmware updates to address time-sensitive remediations?

### VPM-12 — Vulnerability Scanning

Does the organization detect vulnerabilities and configuration errors by routine vulnerability scanning of systems and applications?

### VPM-12.1 — Update Vulnerability Scanning Tools

Does the organization update vulnerability scanning tools?

### VPM-12.2 — Breadth / Depth of Coverage For Vulnerability Scanning

Does the organization identify the breadth and depth of coverage for vulnerability scanning that define the system components scanned and types of vulnerabilities that are checked for?

### VPM-12.3 — Privileged Access For Vulnerability Scanning Tools

Does the organization implement privileged access authorization for selected vulnerability scanning activities?

### VPM-12.4 — Reviewing Vulnerability Scanner Usage

Does the organization monitor logs associated with scanning activities and associated administrator accounts to ensure that those activities are limited to the timeframes of legitimate scans?

### VPM-13 — Vulnerability Trend Analysis

Does the organization use automated mechanisms to compare the results of vulnerability scans over time to determine trends in system vulnerabilities?

### VPM-13.1 — Review Historical Event logs

Does the organization review historical event logs to determine if identified vulnerabilities have been previously exploited?

### VPM-14 — External Vulnerability Assessment

Does the organization perform quarterly external vulnerability scans (outside its network looking inward) via a reputable vulnerability service provider, which include rescans until passing results are obtained or all “high” vulnerabilities are resolved, as defined by the Common Vulnerability Scoring System (CVSS)?

### VPM-15 — Internal Vulnerability Assessment

Does the organization perform quarterly internal vulnerability scans, which includes all segments of its internal network, as well as rescans until passing results are obtained or all “high” vulnerabilities are resolved, as defined by the Common Vulnerability Scoring System (CVSS)?

### VPM-16 — Acceptable Discoverable Information

Does the organization define what information is allowed to be discoverable by adversaries and take corrective actions to remediate non-compliant Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS)?

### VPM-17 — Correlate Scanning Information

Does the organization use automated mechanisms to correlate the output from vulnerability scanning tools to determine the presence of multi-vulnerability/multi-hop attack vectors?

### VPM-18 — Penetration Testing

Does the organization conduct penetration testing on Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS)?

### VPM-19 — Independent Penetration Agent or Team

Does the organization utilize an independent assessor or penetration team to perform penetration testing?

### VPM-20 — Technical Surveillance Countermeasures Security

Does the organization utilize a technical surveillance countermeasures survey?

### VPM-21 — Red Team Exercises

Does the organization utilize "red team" exercises to simulate attempts by adversaries to compromise Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) in accordance with organization-defined rules of engagement?

### WEB-01 — Web Security Policy

Does the organization establish a formal, documented web security policy that:
 (1) Conveys executive management's intent;
 (2) Provides organizational direction and expected behaviors;
 (3) Is reviewed at least annually; and
 (4) Is updated, as necessary, to adapt to evolving risks, threats and other changes that affect the organization?

### WEB-02 — Web Security

Does the organization facilitate the implementation of an enterprise-wide web management policy, as well as associated standards, controls and procedures?

### WEB-03 — Web Security Standard

Does the organization ensure the Open Web Application Security Project (OWASP) Application Security Verification Standard is incorporated into its Secure Systems Development Lifecycle (SSDLC) process?

### WEB-04 — Web Application Framework

Does the organization use a robust Web Application Framework to support the development of secure web applications, including web services, web resources and web Application Programming Interfaces (APIs)?

### WEB-05 — Unauthorized Code On Web Pages

Does the organization prevent unauthorized code from being present in a secure page as it is rendered in a client's browser?

### WEB-06 — Client-Facing Web Services

Does the organization deploy reasonably-expected security, compliance and resilience controls to protect the confidentiality and availability of client data that is stored, transmitted or processed by the Internet-based service?

### WEB-07 — Strong Customer Authentication (SCA)

Does the organization implement Strong Customer Authentication (SCA) for consumers to reasonably prove their identity?

### WEB-08 — Web Application Input Validation & Sanitization

Does the organization ensure all input handled by a web application is validated and/or sanitized?

### WEB-09 — Secure Web Traffic

Does the organization ensure all web application content is delivered using cryptographic mechanisms (e.g., TLS)?

### WEB-10 — Web Application Output Encoding

Does the organization ensure output encoding is performed on all content produced by a web application to reduce the likelihood of cross-site scripting and other injection attacks?

### WEB-11 — Web Browser Security

Does the organization ensure web applications implement Content-Security-Policy, HSTS and X-Frame-Options response headers to protect both the web application and its users?

### WEB-12 — Website Change Detection

Does the organization detect and respond to Indicators of Compromise (IoC) for unauthorized alterations, additions, deletions or changes on websites that store, process and/or transmit sensitive and/or regulated data?

### WEB-13 — Publicly Accessible Content Reviews

Does the organization routinely review the content on publicly accessible systems for sensitive and/or regulated data and remove such information, if discovered?

∙ Encryption at rest and in transit

Large business (250–999 staff):

∙ Aggregated telemetry classified as restricted
∙ Access logging and periodic review

Enterprise (>1,000 staff):
∙ Enterprise GRC / CCM platform with data classification labels, RBAC and encryption
∙ DLP monitoring of the evidence repository
∙ Retention limits and access reviews for aggregated telemetry

### EMB-03 — Separate Operating Environments For Embedded Technologies

Micro-small business (<10 staff):
∙ Separate Wi-Fi network or VLAN for IoT devices (e.g., cameras, printers, smart devices)
∙ Firewall rules blocking IoT-to-workstation traffic

Small business (10–49 staff):
∙ Dedicated VLAN(s) for IoT/OT with firewall rules
∙ Network Access Control (NAC) or MAC filtering for embedded devices

Medium business (50–249 staff):
∙ Network segmentation for IoT/OT with firewall enforcement
∙ Network Access Control (NAC) (e.g., Cisco ISE, Aruba ClearPass, FortiNAC)
∙ Industrial DMZ for OT environments

Large business (250–999 staff):
∙ Purdue model-based OT segmentation with industrial DMZ
∙ OT-aware firewalls (e.g., Fortinet, Palo Alto, Cisco)
∙ OT visibility platform (e.g., Claroty, Nozomi, Armis)

Enterprise (>1,000 staff):
∙ Enterprise OT/IoT segmentation program aligned with ISA/IEC 62443 zones and conduits
∙ OT-aware firewalls and unidirectional gateways where required
∙ OT visibility and detection platform (e.g., Claroty, Nozomi, Dragos, Armis)

## Assessment objectives

### GOV-01_A01

a formal, documented security, compliance and resilience governance policy is approved by executive management, or a formally delegated authority, and conveys executive management's intent for security, compliance and resilience governance.

### GOV-01_A02

the security, compliance and resilience governance policy provides organizational direction and states the behaviors expected of personnel and other applicable parties with respect to security, compliance and resilience governance.

### GOV-01_A03

the current version of the security, compliance and resilience governance policy is communicated to, and accessible by, the personnel and other applicable parties who are expected to comply with it.

### GOV-01_A04

the security, compliance and resilience governance policy is reviewed at least annually.

### GOV-01_A05

the security, compliance and resilience governance policy is updated, as necessary, in response to changes in risks, threats, business practices and/or statutory, regulatory and contractual obligations that affect the organization.

### GOV-02_A01

an organization-wide cybersecurity / data privacy governance program is developed.

### GOV-02_A02

the cybersecurity / data privacy governance program addresses management commitment.

### GOV-02_A03

the cybersecurity / data privacy governance program addresses statutory, regulatory and/or contractual compliance obligations.

### GOV-02_A04

the cybersecurity / data privacy governance program is protected from unauthorized disclosure.

### GOV-02_A05

the cybersecurity / data privacy governance program is protected from unauthorized modification.

### GOV-02_A06

the cybersecurity / data privacy governance program is disseminated.

### GOV-02_A07

the cybersecurity / data privacy governance program provides an overview of the requirements for the security program.

### GOV-02_A08

the cybersecurity / data privacy governance program provides a description of the security program management controls in place or planned for meeting those requirements.

### GOV-02_A09

the cybersecurity / data privacy governance program provides a description of the common controls in place or planned for meeting those requirements.

### GOV-02_A10

the cybersecurity / data privacy governance program includes the identification and assignment of roles.

### GOV-02_A11

the cybersecurity / data privacy governance program includes the identification and assignment of responsibilities.

### GOV-02_A12

the cybersecurity / data privacy governance program addresses coordination among organizational entities.

### GOV-02_A13

the cybersecurity / data privacy governance program reflects the coordination among the organizational entities responsible for cybersecurity / data privacy.

### GOV-02_A14

the cybersecurity / data privacy governance program is approved by a senior official with responsibility and accountability for the risk being incurred to organizational operations.

### GOV-02_A15

the frequency at which to review / update the organization-wide cybersecurity / data privacy governance program is defined.

### GOV-02_A16

events that trigger the review / update of the organization-wide cybersecurity / data privacy governance program are defined.

### GOV-02_A17

the cybersecurity / data privacy governance program is reviewed / updated frequently.

### GOV-02_A18

the cybersecurity / data privacy governance program is reviewed / updated following events.

### GOV-02_A19

cybersecurity & data protection governance operations are conducted according to documented policies, standards, procedures and/or other organizational directives.

### GOV-02_A20

resources are assigned to support cybersecurity & data protection governance operations (e.g., people, processes, technologies, data and/or facilities)

### GOV-02_A21

responsibility and authority for the performance of cybersecurity & data protection governance-related activities are assigned to designated personnel.

### GOV-02_A22

personnel performing cybersecurity & data protection governance-related activities have the skills and knowledge needed to perform their assigned duties.

### GOV-02_A23

the design of security, compliance and resilience governance controls is documented.

### GOV-02_A24

security, compliance and resilience governance controls are monitored to determine whether they are implemented and operating as designed.

### GOV-03_A01

the security, compliance and resilience controls and related processes to be centrally managed are defined.

### GOV-03_A02

the defined security, compliance and resilience controls are centrally managed.

### GOV-03_A03

the defined security, compliance and resilience-related processes are centrally managed.

technology and process terminology is standardized to reduce confusion amongst groups and departments.

### GOV-03.3_A01

### GOV-03.4_A01

policies and procedures are reviewed <A.03.15.01.ODP[01]: frequency>.

### GOV-04.1_A05

policies and procedures are updated <A.03.15.01.ODP[01]: frequency>.

### GOV-04.2_A01

exception requests to standards are formally submitted for review, along with a business justification for the deviation and proposed compensating controls.

### GOV-04.2_A03

### GOV-04.3_A05

### AAT-11.2_A02

Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Autonomous Technologies (AAT) are designated as "High Risk" if one (1), or more, of the following criteria are met:
(1) AAT is used as a safety component of a product or service;
(2) AAT poses a significant risk of harm to an individual's health, safety or fundamental rights; and/or
(3) AAT materially influences the outcome of an individual's decision making.

### IAC-37.1_A01

the accounts, Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) and access scenarios for which replay-resistant Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) is required are defined.

### IAC-37.1_A02

automated mechanisms enforce replay-resistant Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) such that authenticator outputs cannot be reused to authenticate a subsequent session.

### IAC-37.1_A03

where nonces are used, the verifier generates a unique nonce for each authentication attempt and rejects authenticator outputs that reuse a prior nonce.

### IAC-37.1_A04

where one-time challenges are used, the verifier issues a unique challenge for each authentication attempt and rejects responses to previously issued challenges.

### IAC-37.1_A05

where time-synchronous values are used, the verifier accepts each One-Time Password (OTP) value only within its validity window and rejects reuse of a previously accepted value.

### IAC-37.1_A06

where channel binding is used, the authenticator output is cryptographically bound to the authenticated protected channel so that it cannot be replayed over a different channel.

### IAC-37.1_A07

configurations of in-scope authentication mechanisms are reviewed to confirm replay-resistant Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) remains enforced.

### IAC-37.2_A01

the accounts, Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) and access scenarios for which phishing-resistant Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) is required are defined.

### IAC-37.2_A02

automated mechanisms enforce phishing-resistant Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) using authenticators that are cryptographically bound to the verifier's identity (e.g., FIDO2 / WebAuthn or Public Key Infrastructure (PKI)-based authenticators).

### IAC-37.2_A03

authenticator outputs are not accepted by a verifier other than the one to which the authenticator is cryptographically bound, preventing credential relay by an impersonating party.

### IAC-37.2_A04

authenticators that are not phishing-resistant (e.g., SMS, voice, email or push-notification codes) are not accepted as a factor for in-scope accounts and access scenarios.

### IAC-37.2_A05

configurations of in-scope authentication mechanisms are reviewed to confirm phishing-resistant Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) remains enforced.

### E-GOV-02 — Cybersecurity & Data Protection Standards

Cybersecurity & Data Protection Standards

Documented evidence of an appropriately-scoped cybersecurity & data protection standards. Standards are mandatory requirements regarding processes, actions and configurations. Standards are intended to be granular and prescriptive to ensure Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) are designed and operated to include appropriate cybersecurity & data protection protections

### E-GOV-03 — Cybersecurity & Data Protection Controls

Cybersecurity & Data Protection Controls

Documented evidence of an appropriately-scoped cybersecurity & data protection controls. Controls are technical, administrative or physical safeguards. Controls are the nexus used to manage risks through preventing, detecting or lessening the ability of a particular threat from negatively impacting business processes. Controls directly map to standards, since control testing is designed to measure specific aspects of how standards are actually implemented.

### E-GOV-04 — Cybersecurity & Data Protection Procedures

Cybersecurity & Data Protection Procedures

Documented evidence of an appropriate appropriately-scoped cybersecurity & data protection procedures. Procedures are a documented set of steps necessary to perform a specific task or process in conformance with an applicable standard. Procedures help address the question of how the organization actually operationalizes a policy, standard or control. The result of a procedure is intended to satisfy a specific control. Procedures are also commonly referred to as “control activities.”

### E-GOV-05 — Cybersecurity & Data Protection Policies & Standards Reviews

Cybersecurity & Data Protection Policies & Standards Reviews

Documented evidence of a periodic review process for the organization's cybersecurity & data protection policies and standards to identify necessary updates.

### E-GOV-06 — Exception Management

Exception Management

Documented evidence of authorized exceptions to standards (e.g., configurations, practices, etc.)
