Cybersecurity Risk Assessment (RA)

Documented evidence of a cybersecurity-specific risk assessment.

### E-RSK-05 — Supply Chain Risk Assessment (SCRA)

Supply Chain Risk Assessment (SCRA)

Documented evidence of supply chain-specific risk assessment that evaluates risks that are specific to its supply chain.

### E-RSK-06 — Risk Threshold

Risk Threshold

Documented evidence the organization has a defined risk threshold.

### E-RSK-07 — Risk Tolerance

Risk Tolerance

Documented evidence the organization has a defined risk tolerance.

### E-RSK-08 — Risk Appetite

Risk Appetite

Documented evidence the organization has a defined risk appetite.

### E-RSK-09 — Risk Catalog

Risk Catalog

Documented evidence of a risk catalog.

### E-RSK-10 — Material Risk Definition

Material Risk Definition

Documented evidence of criteria necessary to designate a risk as a material risk.

### E-RSK-11 — Risk Alternatives

Risk Alternatives

Documented evidence of alternative courses of action to manage material risks.

### E-RSK-12 — Risk Management Justification

Risk Management Justification

Document evidence of justification for selecting a specific course of action to manage material risk.

### E-RSK-13 — Risk Treatment Options

Risk Treatment Options

Documented evidence of organization-approved risk treatment options.

### E-RSK-14 — Risk Treatment Plan

Risk Treatment Plan

Documented Risk Treatment Plan (RTP) for applicable stakeholders to utilize in remediating identified risks according to a defined timeline.

### E-RSK-15 — Instances Requiring A Risk Assessment

Instances Requiring A Risk Assessment

Documented criteria that define instances requiring a risk assessment to be performed.

### E-SAT-01 — Continuing Professional Education (CPE)

Continuing Professional Education (CPE)

Documented evidence of Continuing Professional Education (CPE) requirements for cybersecurity & data privacy personnel.

### E-SAT-02 — Initial User Training

Initial User Training

Documented evidence of initial user training for security, compliance and/or resilience topics.

### E-SAT-03 — Practical Exercises

Practical Exercises

Documented evidence of practical user training exercises for security, compliance and/or resilience topics (e.g., phishing exercise).

### E-SAT-04 — Recurring User Training

Recurring User Training

Documented evidence of recurring (e.g., annual) user training for security, compliance and/or resilience topics.

### E-SAT-05 — Role-Based Training

Role-Based Training

Documented evidence of specialized user training for privileged users, executives, individuals who handle sensitive/regulated data, etc.

### E-SAT-06 — Training Materials

Training Materials

Documented evidence of security awareness training materials (e.g., curriculum, course work, presentations, etc.)

### E-SAT-07 — Training Records

Training Records

Documented evidence of security awareness training records

### E-SEA-01 — Logon Banner

Logon Banner

Documented evidence of a system use notification message or logon banner.

### E-SEA-02 — Security Architecture

Security Architecture

Documented evidence of security architecture-related documentation.

### E-TDA-01 — Secure Software Development Principles (SSDP)

Secure Software Development Principles (SSDP)

Documented evidence of a Secure Software Development Principles (SSDP). This is program-level documentation in the form of a runbook, playbook or a similar format provides guidance on organizational practices that support existing policies and standards.

### E-TDA-02 — Secure Engineering & Data Privacy (SEDP)

Secure Engineering & Data Privacy (SEDP)

Documented evidence of a Secure Engineering & Data Privacy (SEDP) program. This is program-level documentation in the form of a runbook, playbook or a similar format provides guidance on organizational practices that support existing policies and standards.

### E-TDA-03 — Application Security Testing (AST)

Application Security Testing (AST)

Documented evidence of application security testing (e.g., DAST, SAST, fuzzing, etc.).

### E-TDA-04 — Design and Development Plan (DDP)

Design and Development Plan (DDP)

Documented evidence of an engineering method to control the design process and govern the lifecycle of the product/service.

### E-TDA-05 — Failure Mode and Effect Analysis (FMEA)

Failure Mode and Effect Analysis (FMEA)

Documented evidence of an engineering method designed to define, identify, and present solutions for system failures, problems, or errors.

### E-TDA-06 — Multi Patient Harm View (MPHV)

Multi Patient Harm View (MPHV)

Documented evidence of a description of a Multi Patient Harm View (MPHV) that explains how the device / system defends against and/or responds to attacks with the potential to harm multiple patients. [note MPHV is specific to medical device manufacturers]

### E-TDA-07 — Ports, Protocols & Services (PPS)

Ports, Protocols & Services (PPS)

Documented evidence of all ports, protocols and services in use by the system, application or service.

### E-TDA-08 — Secure Engineering Principles (SEP)

Secure Engineering Principles (SEP)

Documented evidence of defined secure engineering principles used to ensure Sensitivity, Integrity, Availability & Safety (CIAS) concerns are properly addressed in the design and implementation of Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS).

### E-TDA-09 — Security Architecture View

Security Architecture View

Documented evidence that identifies security-relevant system elements and their interfaces:
• Define security context, domains, boundaries, and external interfaces of the system;
• Align the architecture with (a) the system security objectives and requirements, (b) security design characteristics; and
• Establish traceability of architecture elements to user and system security requirements.

### E-TDA-10 — Security Use Case View (SUCV)

Security Use Case View (SUCV)

Documented evidence of diagrams, with explanatory text, describing various security scenarios in each of the operational and clinical functionality states of the system and how the system addresses each scenario architecturally. [note SUCV is specific to medical device manufacturers]

### E-TDA-11 — Software Assurance Maturity Model (SAMM)

Software Assurance Maturity Model (SAMM)

Documented evidence of a Software Assurance Maturity Model (SAMM).

### E-TDA-12 — Software Bill of Materials (SBOM)

Software Bill of Materials (SBOM)

Documented evidence of a Software Bill of Materials (SBOM).

### E-TDA-13 — Software Escrow

Software Escrow

Documented evidence of a software escrow solution.

### E-TDA-14 — System Security Plan (SSP)

System Security Plan (SSP)

Documented evidence of at least one (1) System Security Plan (SSP) that covers the sensitive/regulated data environment. There may be multiple SSPs, based on applicable contracts.

### E-TDA-15 — Updateability / Patchability View

Updateability / Patchability View

Documented evidence of a description of the end-to-end process permitting software updates and patches to be deployed to the device/service.

### E-TDA-16 — Vulnerability Disclosure Program (VDP)

Vulnerability Disclosure Program (VDP)

Documented evidence of a Vulnerability Disclosure Program (VDP) (e.g., bug bounty).

### E-TDA-17 — System Design Documentation

System Design Documentation

Documented evidence of system design documentation.

### E-TDA-18 — System Security Plan (SSP) Reviews

System Security Plan (SSP) Reviews

Documented evidence of reviews and/or updates to System Security Plan (SSP) documentation.

### E-TDA-19 — Hardware / Indentured Bill of Materials (HBOM / IBOM)

Hardware / Indentured Bill of Materials (HBOM / IBOM)

Documented evidence of Hardware Bills of Materials (HBOM) and/or Indentured Bills of Materials (IBOM).

### E-TDA-20 — Development / Test / Production Environment Separation

Development / Test / Production Environment Separation

Documented evidence of secure development environments and separation of development, test and production environments, including secure migration practices.

### E-TDA-21 — Test Data Management

Test Data Management

Documented evidence of restrictions on the use of live / sensitive data in testing and test data integrity controls.

### E-TDA-22 — Anti-Counterfeit & Product Tampering Controls

Anti-Counterfeit & Product Tampering Controls

Documented evidence of anti-counterfeit and product tampering controls, including anti-counterfeit training.

### E-THR-01 — Indicators of Exposure (IOE)

Indicators of Exposure (IOE)

Documented evidence of defined Indicators of Exposure (IOE).

### E-THR-02 — Industry Associations / Memberships

Industry Associations / Memberships

Documented evidence of industry associations the organization utilizes to maintain situational awareness of evolving threats and trends.

### E-THR-03 — Threat Intelligence Feeds (TIF)

Threat Intelligence Feeds (TIF)

Documented evidence of threat intelligence feeds.

### E-THR-04 — Threat Intelligence Program (TIP)

Threat Intelligence Program (TIP)

Documented evidence of a formal capability that intakes and analysis threat information to determine specific threat to the organization and necessary actions to mitigate the threat(s).

### E-THR-05 — Threat Mitigation

Threat Mitigation

Documented evidence of steps taken to mitigate identified threats.

### E-THR-06 — Threat Catalog

Threat Catalog

Documented evidence of a threat catalog.

### E-THR-07 — Threat Analysis

Threat Analysis

Documented evidence of a completed threat analysis.

### E-THR-08 — Behavioral Baselining

Behavioral Baselining

Documented evidence of behavioral baselining to determine normal vs abnormal activities.

### E-THR-09 — Insider Threat Program

Insider Threat Program

Documented evidence of an insider threat program, including the cross-discipline incident handling team and insider threat monitoring.

### E-TPM-01 — Third-Party Contracts

Third-Party Contracts

Documented evidence of third-party contractual obligations for cybersecurity & data privacy protections.

### E-TPM-02 — Third-Party Criticality Assessment

Third-Party Criticality Assessment

Documented evidence of third-party criticality assessment that evaluates the critical nature of each third-party the organization works with.

### E-TPM-03 — Third-Party Service Reviews

Third-Party Service Reviews

Documented evidence of a formal, annual stakeholder review of third-party services for each External Service Provider (ESP).

### E-TPM-04 — Service Level Agreements (SLAs)

Service Level Agreements (SLAs)

Documented evidence of third-party Service Level Agreements (SLAs) to support business operations.

### E-TPM-05 — Break Clauses

Break Clauses

Documented evidence of "break clauses" in third-party contracts.

### E-TPM-06 — Third-Party Terms & Conditions

Third-Party Terms & Conditions

Documented evidence of terms and conditions for external systems.

### E-TPM-07 — System Connection or Processing Agreements

System Connection or Processing Agreements

Documented evidence of system connection or processing agreements.

### E-TPM-08 — Third-Party Exit / Transition Plan

Third-Party Exit / Transition Plan

Documented evidence of exit strategies and transition plans for third-party relationships, including TAASD portability, disposition, knowledge transfer and exit contingencies.

### E-TPM-09 — Third-Party Access Revocation Records

Third-Party Access Revocation Records

Documented evidence that third-party physical and logical access was revoked upon cessation of services.

### E-TPM-10 — Foreign Ownership, Control or Influence (FOCI) Assessments

Foreign Ownership, Control or Influence (FOCI) Assessments

Documented evidence of Foreign Ownership, Control or Influence (FOCI) assessments and ownership change monitoring for third-parties.

### E-TPM-11 — Supplier Diversity & Concentration Risk Analysis

Supplier Diversity & Concentration Risk Analysis

Documented evidence of supplier diversity, adequate supply and outsourcing limitation analyses addressing single-source / concentration dependencies.

### E-VPM-01 — Vulnerability & Patch Management Program (VPMP)

Vulnerability & Patch Management Program (VPMP)

Documented evidence of a Vulnerability & Patch Management Program (VPMP). This is program-level documentation in the form of a runbook, playbook or a similar format provides guidance on organizational practices that support existing policies and standards.

### E-VPM-02 — Penetration Testing - Application

Penetration Testing - Application

Documented evidence of Application Security Testing (AST) activities:
• Abuse case, malformed, and unexpected inputs (e.g., Robustness or Fuzz testing);
• Attack surface analysis;
• Vulnerability chaining;
• Closed box testing of known vulnerability scanning;
• Software composition analysis of binary executable files; and/or
• Static and dynamic code analysis, including testing for credentials that are “hardcoded,” default, easily guessed, and easily compromised.

### E-VPM-03 — Penetration Testing - Network

Penetration Testing - Network

Documented evidence of internal and external network penetration testing activities that focus on discovering and exploiting security vulnerabilities.

### E-VPM-04 — Red Team Testing

Red Team Testing

Documented evidence of "red team" testing.

### E-VPM-05 — Vulnerability Assessments

Vulnerability Assessments

Documented evidence of internal and external vulnerability assessment activities.

### E-VPM-06 — Attack Surface Scope

Attack Surface Scope

Documented evidence of the organization defining its attack surface (e.g., may be in the form of graphical network diagrams or other forms of written documentation).

### E-VPM-07 — Flaw Remediation Change Control

Flaw Remediation Change Control

Documented evidence of installation/change control records for security-relevant software and firmware updates.

### E-VPM-08 — Flaw Remediation Test Results

Flaw Remediation Test Results

Documented evidence of test results from the installation of software and firmware updates to correct system flaws.

### E-VPM-09 — Flaw Remediation Actions

Flaw Remediation Actions

Documented evidence of list of recent security flaw remediation actions performed on the system (e.g., list of installed patches, service packs, hot fixes, and other software updates to correct system flaws).

### E-VPM-10 — Applicable Flaws & Vulnerabilities

Applicable Flaws & Vulnerabilities

Documented evidence of flaws and vulnerabilities potentially affecting a specific system, application and/or service.

### E-VPM-11 — Vulnerability Scanning

Vulnerability Scanning

Documented evidence of internal and external vulnerability scans being performed.

### E-VPM-12 — Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) Mitigation Records

Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) Mitigation Records

Documented evidence of Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) identification and mitigation status.

### E-VPM-13 — Deferred Patching Decisions

Deferred Patching Decisions

Documented evidence of risk-based decisions to defer patches, including approvals and compensating measures.

### E-WEB-01 — Web Security Standard & Application Framework

Web Security Standard & Application Framework

Documented evidence of the organization's web security standard and approved web application framework(s).

### E-WEB-02 — Client-Facing Web Services Protections

Client-Facing Web Services Protections

Documented evidence of protections for client-facing web services, including Strong Customer Authentication (SCA) and secure web traffic.

### E-WEB-03 — Website Change Detection & Unauthorized Code Monitoring

Website Change Detection & Unauthorized Code Monitoring

Documented evidence of website change detection and monitoring for unauthorized code on web pages.

### E-WEB-04 — Web Application Input Validation & Output Encoding

Web Application Input Validation & Output Encoding

Documented evidence of web application input validation, sanitization and output encoding controls (e.g., test results, framework configuration).

## Risks

### R-AC-1 — Loss of Accountability / Attribution

Loss of Accountability / Attribution

Actions, transactions, asset ownership or other relevant activity cannot be reliably attributed to an accountable individual, service or system, impairing traceability, non-repudiation and enforcement.

### R-AC-2 — Excessive or Unauthorized Privilege

Excessive or Unauthorized Privilege

Users, services or systems obtain or retain privileges beyond those required for authorized duties, increasing the ability to access, change, disclose or disrupt protected resources.

### R-AC-3 — Unauthorized Privilege Elevation

Unauthorized Privilege Elevation

An actor, account, service or process gains privileges beyond its authorized level, enabling access to restricted functions, data or administrative capabilities.

### R-AC-4 — Unauthorized Access

Unauthorized Access

Individuals, groups, services, devices or processes gain access to Technology Assets, Applications, Services, Data and/or Facilities (TAASDF) without appropriate authorization.

### R-AC-5 — Identity Compromise / Impersonation

Identity Compromise / Impersonation

A user, service or machine identity is compromised, spoofed or hijacked, allowing an unauthorized actor to authenticate or operate as a trusted identity.

### R-AM-1 — Loss, Theft or Damage of Assets

Loss, Theft or Damage of Assets

Technology, data, equipment or other organizational assets are lost, stolen, destroyed, damaged or otherwise rendered unavailable for authorized use.

### R-AM-2 — Unauthorized Modification / Loss of System Integrity

Unauthorized Modification / Loss of System Integrity

Unauthorized or unintended changes alter the configuration, code, data or state of a Technology Asset, Application and/or Service (TAAS) causing it to operate in an untrusted or unreliable manner.

### R-AM-3 — Unauthorized Retention / Inability to Dispose of Data

Unauthorized Retention / Inability to Dispose of Data

Sensitive and/or regulated data is retained beyond authorized or necessary periods, cannot be reliably located or disposed of, or remains recoverable after intended destruction, creating security, data privacy, legal or discovery exposure.

### R-BC-1 — Business / Service Interruption

Business / Service Interruption

Critical business processes, mission functions and Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) become unavailable, materially degraded or unable to meet required service levels.

### R-BC-2 — Data Loss / Integrity Compromise

Data Loss / Integrity Compromise

Data is destroyed, unavailable, corrupted, altered or otherwise loses required integrity or recoverability, impairing business, legal or operational use.

### R-BC-3 — Reduced Operational Productivity

Reduced Operational Productivity

Personnel, systems and/or business processes operate below required efficiency or throughput because necessary Technology Assets, Applications, Services and/or Data (TAASD) are unavailable or degraded.

### R-BC-4 — System / Data Compromise (Technical Vector)

System / Data Compromise (Technical Vector)

Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) experience a technical attack vector compromise that results in unauthorized access, disclosure, modification, destruction or disruption (e.g., malware, phishing, hacking, etc.).

### R-BC-5 — System / Data Compromise (Non-Technical Vector)

System / Data Compromise (Non-Technical Vector)

Technology Assets, Applications, Services and/or Data (TAASD) experience a non-technical attack vector compromise that results in unauthorized access, disclosure, modification, destruction or disruption (e.g., social engineering, sabotage, etc.).

### R-EX-1 — Revenue Loss

Revenue Loss

The organization experiences reduced current or future revenue because a control deficiency disrupts operations:
(1) Causes customer loss;
(2) Prevents sales; and/or
(3) Otherwise impairs revenue-generating activity.

### R-EX-2 — Contractual Default / Termination

Contractual Default / Termination

The organization breaches, defaults on, loses, terminates or fails to renew a contract because it cannot meet required security, data privacy, compliance, resilience and/or performance obligations.

### R-EX-3 — Loss of Competitive Advantage

Loss of Competitive Advantage

The organization loses market position, strategic differentiation, intellectual advantage or customer preference because a control deficiency
(1) Exposes data;
(2) Disrupts performance; and/or
(3) Weakens stakeholder confidence.

### R-EX-4 — Reputational Harm / Loss of Stakeholder Trust

Reputational Harm / Loss of Stakeholder Trust

Customers, partners, regulators, investors, employees or the public lose confidence in the organization, resulting in:
(1) Reputational damage; and/or
(2) Diminished brand value.

### R-EX-5 — Regulatory / Legal / Contractual Financial Liability

Regulatory / Legal / Contractual Financial Liability

The organization incurs fines, penalties, judgments, remediation, settlements, damages, indemnification costs or other financial liability due to legal, regulatory or contractual noncompliance.

### R-EX-6 — Exposure from Unaddressed Vulnerabilities

Exposure from Unaddressed Vulnerabilities

Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) remain exploitable because they are not remediated, mitigated or otherwise addressed, increasing exposure to compromise.

### R-EX-7 — System / Service Compromise

System / Service Compromise

Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) are compromised, resulting in loss of confidentiality, integrity, availability, authenticity and/or safety.

### R-EX-8 — Failure to Achieve Strategic / Mission Objectives

Failure to Achieve Strategic / Mission Objectives

A control deficiency materially prevents, delays or degrades the organization's ability to achieve strategic, mission or program objectives.

### R-EX-9 — Intellectual Property / Trade Secret Loss

Intellectual Property / Trade Secret Loss

The strategic or competitive value of proprietary data, trade secrets, research, designs, source code or other Intellectual Property (IP) is reduced when it is:
(1) Improperly disclosed;
(2) Stolen;
(3) Copied; and/or
(4) Rendered non-exclusive,

### R-EX-10 — Fraud / Theft / Direct Financial Loss

Fraud / Theft / Direct Financial Loss

The organization or its stakeholders suffer direct monetary loss through:
(1) Fraud;
(2) Theft;
(3) Unauthorized transactions;
(4) Diversion of funds; or
(5) Other financially harmful activity.

### R-EX-11 — Loss of Authorization / Certification / License

Loss of Authorization / Certification / License

The organization loses or is unable to obtain or maintain an authorization, certification, accreditation, license or other permission required to operate, sell, contract or access a market.

### R-GV-1 — Failure to Support Business / Mission Objectives

Failure to Support Business / Mission Objectives

Security, data privacy, compliance or resilience deficiencies prevent Technology Assets, Applications, Services and/or Data (TAASD) from reliably supporting required business operations, mission functions or strategic objectives.

### R-GV-2 — Unaddressed Security / Compliance Exposure

Unaddressed Security / Compliance Exposure

Incorrect or incomplete control scoping leaves applicable People, Processes, Technologies, Data and/or Facilities (PPTDF)  without required safeguards, creating unmanaged security, data privacy, compliance and/or resilience exposure.

### R-GV-3 — Unperformed / Unowned Control Responsibilities

Unperformed / Unowned Control Responsibilities

Required security, data privacy, compliance and/or resilience activities are not performed, coordinated or escalated because responsibility or accountability is unclear or unassigned.

### R-GV-4 — Uncontrolled Internal Security / Privacy Exposure

Uncontrolled Internal Security / Privacy Exposure

Internal practices are insufficient to prevent, detect, respond to or recover from security, data privacy, compliance and/or resilience events, leaving organizational operations and assets exposed.

### R-GV-5 — Uncontrolled Third-Party Security / Privacy Exposure

Uncontrolled Third-Party Security / Privacy Exposure

Weak third-party governance or Cybersecurity Supply Chain Risk Management (C-SCRM) practices leave the organization exposed to security, data privacy, compliance, resilience or dependency risks originating from suppliers and External Service Providers (ESP).

### R-GV-6 — Lack of oversight of internal controls

Lack of oversight of internal controls

Internal control deficiencies, failures or changes remain unidentified or unresolved, allowing risk exposure to persist and reducing the organization's ability to demonstrate due diligence and due care.

### R-GV-7 — Lack of oversight of third-party controls

Lack of oversight of third-party controls

Third-party control deficiencies, failures or changes remain unidentified or unresolved, allowing supplier-originated exposure to persist and reducing the organization's ability to demonstrate appropriate Third-Party Risk Management (TPRM) oversight.

### R-GV-8 — Harm from Illegal, Abusive or Unsafe Content / Conduct

Harm from Illegal, Abusive or Unsafe Content / Conduct

Illegal, abusive, threatening or otherwise harmful content or conduct causes:
(1) Operational disruption;
(2) Legal exposure;
(3) Personnel harm;
(4) Loss of trust; and/or
(5) Other adverse organizational consequences.

### R-GV-9 — Inability to Demonstrate Due Diligence / Due Care

Inability to Demonstrate Due Diligence / Due Care

The organization cannot produce defensible evidence that applicable risks, controls and obligations were reasonably identified, implemented, monitored and/or governed.

### R-GV-10 — Unreliable Assurance / Decision Information

Unreliable Assurance / Decision Information

Executive management, the Board of Directors (BoD), assessors or other stakeholders rely on inaccurate, incomplete or untimely control, risk or compliance information, leading to:
(1) Unsound decisions; and/or
(2) False assurance.

### R-IR-1 — Loss of Investigative / Evidentiary Capability

Loss of Investigative / Evidentiary Capability

Required evidence, logs, records or chain-of-custody integrity are unavailable or unreliable that prevents the organization from reliably:
(1) Reconstructing;
(2) Investigating;
(3) Attributing / taking legal action for; and/or
(4) Learning from an incident.

### R-IR-2 — Delayed Containment / Increased Incident Impact

Delayed Containment / Increased Incident Impact

An incident is not contained, eradicated, communicated or escalated in a timely and appropriate manner, allowing the scope, duration, cost and/or harm of the incident to increase.

### R-IR-3 — Incident Persistence / Recurrence

Incident Persistence / Recurrence

Root causes, persistence mechanisms or affected conditions are not effectively remediated, allowing the incident, vulnerability or compromise to continue or recur.

### R-IR-4 — Incident Response / Recovery Cost

Incident Response / Recovery Cost

The organization incurs unplanned investigation, containment, recovery, notification, legal, forensic, restoration and/or other costs associated with managing an incident or loss event.

### R-OR-1 — Recovery Failure / Unacceptable Recovery Delay

Recovery Failure / Unacceptable Recovery Delay

The organization cannot restore critical services, data, facilities or capabilities within required recovery objectives after a disruption.

### R-OR-2 — Concentration / Single-Point Dependency Failure

Concentration / Single-Point Dependency Failure

Failure of a highly concentrated supplier, technology, facility, region or other dependency causes disproportionate disruption because adequate alternatives or redundancy are unavailable.

### R-SA-1 — Undetected / Delayed Detection of Adverse Activity

Undetected / Delayed Detection of Adverse Activity

Malicious, abnormal, unauthorized or otherwise material activity is not detected or recognized in time to prevent or limit harm.

### R-SA-2 — Lack of a security-minded workforce

Lack of a security-minded workforce

Personnel are more likely to:
(1) Make unsafe decisions;
(2) Fall victim to social engineering;
(3) Mishandle data;
(4) Violate requirements; and/or
(5) Fail to recognize and report security or privacy concerns.

### R-SC-1 — Third-Party Cybersecurity Compromise / Exposure

Third-Party Cybersecurity Compromise / Exposure

A supplier or External Service Provider (ESP) experiencing a cybersecurity weakness, incident or compromise causes loss of Confidentiality, Integrity, Availability and/or Safety (CIAS) in organizational products, services, data or operations.

### R-SC-2 — Third-Party Physical Security Disruption / Exposure

Third-Party Physical Security Disruption / Exposure

A physical security event affecting a supplier's or External Service Provider's (ESP)  facilities, personnel, equipment or other assets disrupts or compromises products, services, data or operations relied upon by the organization.

### R-SC-3 — Sub-Tier / Fourth-Party Supply Chain Exposure

Sub-Tier / Fourth-Party Supply Chain Exposure

Risks originating from a supplier's or External Service Provider's (ESP)  own suppliers, subcontractors or dependencies propagate through the supply chain and affect organizational Confidentiality, Integrity, Availability and/or Safety (CIAS), compliance and/or operations.

### R-SC-4 — Third-Party Legal / Compliance Exposure

Third-Party Legal / Compliance Exposure

Third-party noncompliance, unlawful conduct, sanctions, litigation or other legal conditions cause the organization to:
(1) Violate obligations;
(2) Lose contracts;
(3) Incur legal and/or financial liability; and/or
(4) Experience operational restrictions.

### R-SC-5 — Harm from Unauthorized / Unintended Product or Service Use

Harm from Unauthorized / Unintended Product or Service Use

A product or service is used outside its authorized, intended or approved purpose, creating security, data privacy, safety, legal, operational or financial harm.

### R-SC-6 — Third-Party Dependency Failure

Third-Party Dependency Failure

A critical third-party product, service or capability becomes unavailable, degraded, discontinued or otherwise unable to support required operations, causing business operations disruption.

### R-SC-7 — Counterfeit / Non-Conforming Component Impact

Counterfeit / Non-Conforming Component Impact

Counterfeit, substituted, defective or non-conforming products or components cause reliability, security, safety, warranty or operational failures in organizational Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS).

### R-AI-1 — AI Output / Decision Integrity Failure

AI Output / Decision Integrity Failure

An Artificial Intelligence (AI) model produces inaccurate, manipulated, biased, unsafe or otherwise unreliable outputs or decisions that cause dependent controls, users or processes to act incorrectly.

### R-AI-2 — AI Data Confidentiality / Integrity / Provenance Loss

AI Data Confidentiality / Integrity / Provenance Loss

Training, fine-tuning, embedding, retrieval or inference data is disclosed, altered, contaminated, misattributed or stripped of required provenance, undermining data privacy, security or Artificial Intelligence (AI) reliability.

### R-AI-3 — Unauthorized / Harmful Autonomous Action

Unauthorized / Harmful Autonomous Action

An Artificial Intelligence (AI) agent or autonomous system takes an action outside authorized scope or intended objectives, causing security, data privacy, safety, legal, financial and/or operational harm.

### R-AI-4 — Sensitive Data / Compliance Exposure from Unsanctioned AI Use

Sensitive Data / Compliance Exposure from Unsanctioned AI Use

Unapproved or ungoverned Artificial Intelligence (AI) use:
(1) Exposes sensitive and/or regulated data;
(2) Creates unauthorized processing;
(3) Introduces Intellectual Property (IP) or licensing issues; and/or
(4) Causes statutory, regulatory and/or contractual noncompliance.

### R-AI-5 — Unintended or Unsafe Technology Behavior

Unintended or Unsafe Technology Behavior

Artificial Intelligence (AI) exhibits emergent, unanticipated or unintended behavior that produces incorrect, unsafe or harmful outcomes or causes dependent controls and processes to operate outside intended boundaries.

### R-AI-6 — AI Bias / Discriminatory Outcome

AI Bias / Discriminatory Outcome

Artificial Intelligence (AI)-supported decisions or outputs produce unjustified, systematically biased or discriminatory outcomes that create legal, ethical, reputational or individual harm.

### R-OT-1 — OT Safety / Process Availability Failure

OT Safety / Process Availability Failure

Failure or compromise of Operational Technology (OT) or Industrial Control System (ICS) functions causes:
(1) Loss or degradation of safety functions;
(2) Physical-process availability; and/or
(3)  Equipment integrity / unsafe operating conditions.

### R-IP-1 — Long-Term Confidentiality Loss from Cryptographic Obsolescence

Long-Term Confidentiality Loss from Cryptographic Obsolescence

Sensitive and/or regulated data requiring long confidentiality lifetimes becomes susceptible to Harvest Now, Decrypt Later (HNDL) collection and future decryption.

### R-IP-2 — Loss of Confidentiality

Loss of Confidentiality

Sensitive and/or regulated data is disclosed or made accessible to unauthorized:
(1) Individuals;
(2) Entities; and/or
(3) Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS).

### R-IP-3 — Loss of Data Integrity

Loss of Data Integrity

Data is altered, corrupted, fabricated, deleted or otherwise changed without authorization or reliable detection, causing it to become untrustworthy for its intended use.

### R-IP-4 — Loss of Data / Service Availability

Loss of Data / Service Availability

Technology Assets, Applications, Services and/or Data (TAASD) are unavailable or inaccessible when required to support authorized business or mission needs.

### R-IP-5 — Loss of Authenticity / Provenance

Loss of Authenticity / Provenance

The organization cannot reliably establish the origin, authenticity, lineage or trustworthiness of:
(1) Data;
(2) Software;
(3) System components;
(4) Communications; and/ or
(5) Transactions.

### R-IP-6 — Privacy Harm / Unauthorized Processing

Privacy Harm / Unauthorized Processing

Individuals are harmed and/or the organization is exposed to statutory and/or regulatory actions when  Personal Data (PD) is collected, received, processed, stored, transmitted, shared, updated and/or disposed of without appropriate:
(1) Authority;
(2) Transparency;
(3) Limitation; and/or
(4) Protection,

### R-SF-1 — Injury / Loss of Life

Injury / Loss of Life

A control deficiency contributes to unsafe conditions that cause or materially increase the likelihood of:
(1) Human injury;
(2) Illness; and/or
(3) Loss of life.

### R-SF-2 — Physical / Environmental Damage

Physical / Environmental Damage

A control deficiency contributes to damage or destruction of:
(1) Physical assets;
(2) Facilities;
(3) Equipment; and/or
(4) The environment.

### R-PE-1 — Loss of Critical Knowledge / Capability

Loss of Critical Knowledge / Capability

The organization loses essential knowledge, skills, authority or operational capability because critical personnel are unavailable, depart or cannot perform required duties.

## Threats

### NT-1 — Drought & Water Shortage

Drought & Water Shortage

Insufficient precipitation or water availability that restricts municipal, industrial or facility water supplies and can impair cooling, fire suppression, sanitation, facility operations or dependent utility services.

### NT-2 — Earthquakes

Earthquakes

Sudden ground movement caused by seismic activity that can damage facilities, technology, utilities and transportation infrastructure, disrupt personnel access and impair the operation or recovery of controls.

### NT-3 — Fire & Wildfires

Fire & Wildfires

Fire affecting a facility or surrounding area that can injure personnel, destroy or damage technology and records, interrupt utilities and facility access and impair primary or recovery control capabilities.

### NT-4 — Floods

Floods

Water intrusion or inundation caused by rainfall, surface water, storm surge, infrastructure failure or other sources that can damage facilities and technology, interrupt utilities and make control-supporting locations inaccessible.

### NT-5 — Hurricanes & Tropical Storms

Hurricanes & Tropical Storms

A hurricane, tropical storm or other tropical cyclone that can produce destructive winds, flooding, storm surge, utility outages, transportation disruption and facility damage that impair control execution or recovery.

### NT-6 — Landslides & Debris Flow

Landslides & Debris Flow

Movement of soil, rock or debris that can damage or isolate facilities, transportation routes, utilities and communications needed to execute or recover controls.

### NT-7 — Pandemic (Disease) Outbreaks

Pandemic (Disease) Outbreaks

A widespread infectious disease event that can reduce workforce availability, disrupt suppliers and essential services, restrict facility access and degrade the organization's ability to operate, monitor or recover controls.

### NT-8 — Severe Weather

Severe Weather

Severe meteorological conditions, including high winds, hail, extreme heat, heavy precipitation or similar events, that can damage facilities or technology, disrupt utilities and transportation, or otherwise degrade control execution.

### NT-9 — Space Weather

Space Weather

Solar or geomagnetic activity that can disrupt satellites, radio communications, navigation, timing services, electrical grids or other technologies on which control execution depends.

### NT-10 — Thunderstorms & Lightning

Thunderstorms & Lightning

Thunderstorms or lightning that can cause electrical surges, fires, utility outages, communications disruption or equipment damage that impairs control execution.

### NT-11 — Tornadoes

Tornadoes

A tornado or associated severe wind event that can damage facilities, equipment, utilities and transportation infrastructure, endanger personnel and interrupt the operation or recovery of controls.

### NT-12 — Tsunamis

Tsunamis

A tsunami or related coastal inundation event that can cause rapid flooding, structural damage, utility disruption, loss of access and widespread damage to control-supporting facilities and infrastructure.

### NT-13 — Volcanoes

Volcanoes

Volcanic activity, including eruption, ashfall, lava, gases or related seismic effects, that can damage or contaminate facilities and equipment, disrupt transportation and utilities and impair control execution.

### NT-14 — Winter Storms & Extreme Cold

Winter Storms & Extreme Cold

Snow, ice, freezing temperatures or other severe winter conditions that can interrupt utilities and transportation, damage equipment, restrict personnel access and degrade control execution or recovery.

### MT-1 — Civil or Political Unrest

Civil or Political Unrest

Civil disturbance, protest activity, political instability or related violence that can restrict personnel or facility access, disrupt transportation and utilities, damage assets, interrupt suppliers or otherwise impair control execution.

### MT-2 — Malicious Cyber Activity

Malicious Cyber Activity

Deliberate malicious cyber activity, including exploitation, malware, credential abuse, denial-of-service, social engineering or other attack techniques, that can disable, bypass, manipulate or otherwise impair controls and their supporting technologies.

### MT-3 — Hazardous Materials Emergencies

Hazardous Materials Emergencies

An accidental release, spill, leak, fire, explosion or other hazardous-materials event that can endanger personnel, require evacuation, damage facilities or interrupt operations and control-supporting infrastructure.

### MT-4 — Nuclear, Biological and Chemical (NBC) Weapons

Nuclear, Biological and Chemical (NBC) Weapons

Intentional use or release of chemical, biological, radiological or nuclear agents that can cause casualties, contamination, evacuation, infrastructure disruption and prolonged loss of access to facilities or resources needed for control execution.

### MT-5 — Physical Crime

Physical Crime

Physical criminal activity that results in unauthorized entry, theft, vandalism, sabotage or damage to facilities, equipment, records or other assets needed for control execution.

### MT-6 — Terrorism & Armed Attacks

Terrorism & Armed Attacks

Terrorist activity, active-assailant events or other armed attacks that can cause casualties, facility damage, evacuation, loss of access, infrastructure disruption or interruption of control-supporting operations.

### MT-7 — Utility Service Disruption

Utility Service Disruption

Sustained or material loss or degradation of electricity, water, natural gas, telecommunications, internet connectivity or other utility services required to operate facilities, technologies or controls.

### MT-8 — Dysfunctional Management Practices

Dysfunctional Management Practices

Management interference, direction, override or other intentional circumventions that prevents established controls from being performed, enforced, monitored or escalated as designed.

### MT-9 — Human Error

Human Error

Unintentional action or omission by personnel, contractors or other authorized users that misconfigures, disables, bypasses, damages or otherwise impairs a control or its supporting technology, process or data.

### MT-10 — Technical / Mechanical Failure

Technical / Mechanical Failure

Non-malicious failure, degradation or malfunction of hardware, software, communications, mechanical equipment or supporting infrastructure that causes a control to become unavailable, unreliable or ineffective.

### MT-11 — Statutory / Regulatory / Contractual Change

Statutory / Regulatory / Contractual Change

A change in applicable laws, regulations, government directives or contractual obligations that invalidates existing assumptions, requires different safeguards, restricts technologies or suppliers, or otherwise causes established controls to become insufficient or inoperable.

### MT-12 — Data Quality Degradation / Data Poisoning

Data Quality Degradation / Data Poisoning

Use or introduction of inaccurate, stale, corrupted, incomplete, manipulated or otherwise untrustworthy data that causes controls, analytics or automated decisions to operate incorrectly or ineffectively.

### MT-13 — Artificial Intelligence & Autonomous Technologies (AAT) System Failure or Unintended Behavior

Artificial Intelligence & Autonomous Technologies (AAT) System Failure or Unintended Behavior

Non-malicious failure, malfunction, hallucination, unsafe output, goal misalignment, unintended autonomous action or other erroneous behavior by Artificial Intelligence & Autonomous Technologies that impairs a control or dependent business process.

### MT-14 — Fraud, Corruption and/or Intentional Criminal Conduct

Fraud, Corruption and/or Intentional Criminal Conduct

Intentional criminal or corrupt conduct by an insider, third party or other actor that can bypass, manipulate or disable controls (e.g., fraud, bribery, theft, embezzlement, extortion or deliberate policy circumvention).

### MT-15 — Conflict of Interest (COI) / Undue Influence / Insider Misconduct

Conflict of Interest (COI) / Undue Influence / Insider Misconduct

A Conflict of Interest (COI) or improper influence that causes a person with authority or access to make biased decisions, circumvent safeguards, conceal issues or otherwise impair objective control execution.

### MT-16 — Economic Shock / Market Disruption

Economic Shock / Market Disruption

Material economic instability, recession, inflation, interest-rate or exchange-rate shocks, commodity volatility or similar macroeconomic conditions that disrupt staffing, suppliers, investment or resources needed to sustain control execution.

### MT-17 — Foreign Ownership, Control, or Influence (FOCI)

Foreign Ownership, Control, or Influence (FOCI)

Foreign Ownership, Control or Influence (FOCI) that is used to shape decisions, compel access, redirect operations or obtain sensitive information in a manner that can bypass or undermine organizational or supply-chain controls.

### MT-18 — Geopolitical Conflict / Government Intervention

Geopolitical Conflict / Government Intervention

Political conflict, government intervention, war, civil instability, nationalization, export restriction or other geopolitical action that disrupts suppliers, infrastructure, communications, access or resources required for control execution.

### MT-19 — Sanctions / Trade Restriction Disruption

Sanctions / Trade Restriction Disruption

Imposition, expansion or enforcement of sanctions, export controls, exclusions or trade restrictions that removes or constrains access to suppliers, technologies, services, personnel or financial channels required for control execution.

### MT-20 — Counterfeit / Non-Conforming Products

Counterfeit / Non-Conforming Products

Counterfeit, substituted, defective or non-conforming components, materials, software or services enter the supply chain and cause control-supporting products to perform unpredictably, fail prematurely or operate outside required specifications.

### MT-21 — Hazardous / Degraded Operational Environment

Hazardous / Degraded Operational Environment

Environmental, physical or operating conditions at the place of performance that exceed design assumptions or safe operating limits and degrade personnel, equipment or processes needed for control execution.

### MT-22 — Manufacturing Capacity / Supply Disruption

Manufacturing Capacity / Supply Disruption

Loss, reduction or delay of manufacturing capacity, materials, components or supplier output that prevents timely availability of products or services required for control execution (e.g., sole-source or concentration failures).

### MT-23 — Product Defect / Design Failure

Product Defect / Design Failure

A design flaw, manufacturing defect, quality failure or specification deviation in a product or service that causes unsafe, unreliable or ineffective operation of a control or its supporting technology.

### MT-24 — Supplier Financial Distress / Insolvency

Supplier Financial Distress / Insolvency

Financial distress, loss of liquidity, hostile acquisition, bankruptcy or insolvency of a critical supplier that interrupts contractual performance, support, maintenance or delivery of control-dependent products or services.

### MT-25 — Workforce Shortage / Loss of Critical Skills / Labor Disruption

Workforce Shortage / Loss of Critical Skills / Labor Disruption

Loss, shortage, unavailability or labor disruption of personnel with required knowledge, skills or authorization that prevents controls from being performed, maintained, monitored or recovered as intended.

### MT-26 — Transportation / Logistics Disruption

Transportation / Logistics Disruption

Accident, cargo loss, carrier failure, route closure, capacity shortage or other transportation or logistics disruption that delays or prevents delivery of products, equipment or services needed for control execution.

### MT-27 — Infrastructure Failure / Degradation

Infrastructure Failure / Degradation

Failure, degradation or unavailability of transportation, communications, energy, facilities or other foundational infrastructure on which the organization or its supply chain depends for control execution.

### MT-28 — Harvest Now / Decrypt Later (HNDL)

Harvest Now / Decrypt Later (HNDL)

A threat actor intercepts and retains currently encrypted sensitive information with the intent to decrypt it later when cryptanalytic or quantum capabilities make the deployed cryptography vulnerable.

### MT-29 — Adversarial Artificial Intelligence (AI) Attack

Adversarial Artificial Intelligence (AI) Attack

Deliberate manipulation or exploitation of an AI system through adversarial inputs, prompt injection, jailbreaking, data or model poisoning, model theft, inference attacks or related techniques that bypass, alter or impair controls or AI-dependent functions.

### MT-30 — Operational Technology (OT) / Industrial Control System (ICS) Attack

Operational Technology (OT) / Industrial Control System (ICS) Attack

Deliberate cyberattack against Operational Technology (OT) or Industrial Control System (ICS) environments that manipulates, disrupts or disables industrial processes, safety functions, equipment or control-supporting operations.

### MT-31 — Cryptographic Compromise / Cryptanalytic Capability Advancement

Cryptographic Compromise / Cryptanalytic Capability Advancement

Advances in computing, cryptanalysis or attack techniques reduce the effective security of deployed cryptographic algorithms or key sizes, causing cryptographic controls to provide less protection than intended.
